source: Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004

sections.title: Short title
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text: This Act may be cited as the Criminal Code Act.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di short name wey dem fit use call dis Act. Dem fit call am di Criminal Code Act.

sections.title: Savings in respect of Northern States
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text: The provisions of this Act shall take effect subject to the provisions of the Penal Code (Northern States) Federal Provisions Act. [Cap. P3.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section say di provisions of dis Act go work subject to di provisions of di Penal Code (Northern States) Federal Provisions Act.

sections.title: The Criminal Code and extent
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text:
(1) The provisions contained in the Code of Criminal Law set forth in the Schedule to this Act, and hereinafter called "the Code", shall, except to the extent specified in subsection (2) of this section, be State laws with respect to the several matters therein dealt with. [Schedule.]
(2) The provisions contained in the Code which relate to any matter contained in the First Schedule to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, shall be the law of the Federal Republic of Nigeria with respect to the several matters therein dealt with. [Cap. C23. L.N. 112 of 1964. L.S.L.N. 16 of 1972. L.N. 155 of 1960.]
(3) The Code may be cited as the Criminal Code. [L.N. 112 of 1964. Cap. C38. L.N. 47 of 1955.]
(4) The provisions of Chapters 2, 4 and 5 of the Criminal Code shall apply in relation to any offence against any Order, Act, Law, or Statute and to all persons charged with any such offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain di Criminal Code wey dey di Schedule to dis Act and where e dey work. Di Code na State laws for di matters wey e talk about, except for wetin subsection (2) talk. Di parts of di Code wey concern any matter wey dey di First Schedule to di Constitution of di Federal Republic of Nigeria na di law of di Federal Republic of Nigeria for dem. Dem fit call di Code di Criminal Code. Chapters 2, 4 and 5 of di Criminal Code go work for any crime against any Order, Act, Law or Statute, and for all person wey dem charge for any of dem.

sections.title: Construction of Acts, laws, rules, regulations, and other instruments
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text:
The following rules shall, unless the context otherwise indicates, apply with respect to the construction of Acts, laws and other instruments- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(1) When in any Act, Law or other instrument, public or private, the term "felony" is used, or reference is made to an offence by the name of felony, it shall be taken that reference is intended to be an offence which is a felony under the provisions of the Code.
(2) When in any Act, law or other instrument, public or private, the term "larceny" is used, it shall be taken that reference is intended to be the offence of stealing.
(3) When in any Act, law or other instrument, public or private, reference is made to any offence by any specific name, it shall be taken that reference is intended to be the offence which, under the provisions of the Code, is constituted by the act or omission that would heretofore have constituted the offence referred to.
(4) When in any Act, law or other instrument, public or private, reference is made to any of the provisions hereby repealed, it shall be taken that reference is intended to be the corresponding provisions or substituted provisions of the Code.
sections.pidgin: Dis section give rules on how to read Acts, laws and other documents, unless di context show another thing. If dem use di word felony for any of dem, e mean crime wey na felony (serious crime) under di Code. If dem use di word larceny, e mean di crime of stealing. If dem name any crime, e mean di crime wey di Code set for di act or omission wey for before don make am. If dem mention any provision wey dis Act don cancel, e mean di matching or replacement provision for di Code.

sections.title: Provisions of Code, exclusive with certain exceptions
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text:
No person shall be liable to be tried or punished in any court in Nigeria for an offence except under the express provisions of the Code or of some Act or law which is in force in, or forms part of, the laws of Nigeria:
Provided that, in the case of an offence committed before the commencement of this Act, the offender may be tried and punished either under the law in force when the offence was committed, or under the Code, provided that, the offender shall not be punished to any greater extent than was authorised by the former law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say person fit only face trial or punishment for any court for Nigeria for crime wey di Code, or another Act or law wey dey force for Nigeria, clearly talk. For crime wey person commit before dis Act start, dem fit try and punish am under di law wey dey force when e do am, or under di Code. But dem no go punish am pass wetin di old law allow.

sections.title: Civil remedies
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text:
When by the Code any act is declared to be lawful, no action can be brought in respect thereof.
Savings Except as aforesaid, the provisions of this Act shall not affect any right of action which any person would have had against another if this Act had not been passed; nor shall the omission from the Code of any penal provision in respect of any act or omission which, before the time of the coming into operation of the Code, constituted an actionable wrong, affect any right of action in respect thereof.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about civil cases. If di Code say any act dey right (di law allow am), nobody fit bring case for court because of am. Apart from dat, dis Act no touch any right wey person get to sue another person before dis Act pass. Di fact say di Code no put punishment for act or omission wey before na wrong wey person fit sue for, no touch di right to sue for am too.

sections.title: Contempt of court
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text: Nothing in this Act or in the Code shall affect the authority of courts of record to punish a person summarily for the offence commonly known as contempt of court; but so that a person cannot be so punished and also punished under the provisions of the Code for the same act or omission.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say dis Act and di Code no take away di power wey courts of record get to punish person quick quick for contempt of court. But dem no fit punish person for contempt of court and still punish am under di Code for di same act or omission.

sections.title: Printing of amendments
sections.chapter: The Act
sections.text:
Whenever any amendment is made in the Code, all copies thereof printed by the Federal Government Printer after the amendment shall be so printed as to set forth the actual provisions of the Code after omitting all repealed provisions or words, and embodying all newly enacted or substituted provisions or words.
SCHEDULE [Section 2 (1).]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk how dem go print di Code after any change. All copies wey di Federal Government Printer print after di change must show di real provisions of di Code, without di provisions or words wey dem don cancel, and with di new or replacement provisions or words.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Interpretation
sections.pidgin: Dis section give di meaning of many words wey dem dey use for di Code. E cover words like 'harm', 'grievous harm', 'dangerous harm', 'maim' and 'wound', and also 'property', 'money', 'court', 'public place', 'dwelling-house', 'brothel', 'prostitution' and 'Christian marriage'. E also explain words about post office and telegraph, words about who dey work for public service, and words like 'utter', 'knowingly' and 'valuable security'. Night mean di time between 6:30 for evening and 6:30 for morning. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Definition of offence
sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Interpretation
sections.text: An act or omission which renders the person doing the act or making the omission liable to punishment under this Code, or under any Act, or law, is called an offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell wetin dem call offence. Any act or omission wey go make di person wey do am face punishment under dis Code, or under any Act or law, na crime (offence).

sections.title: Division of offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Interpretation
sections.text:
Offences are of three kinds, namely, felonies, misdemeanors, and simple offences.
A felony is any offence which is declared by law to be a felony, or is punishable, without proof of previous conviction, with death or with imprisonment for three years or more.
A misdemeanor is any offence which is declared by law to be a misdemeanor, or is punishable by imprisonment for not less than six months, but less than three years.
All offences, other than felonies and misdemeanors, are simple offences.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk di three kinds of crime: felonies, misdemeanours and simple offences. Felony (serious crime) na any crime wey law say na felony, or wey dem fit punish with death or prison for 3 years or more, without proof say di court don find di person guilty before. Misdemeanour (small crime) na any crime wey law say na misdemeanour, or wey dem fit punish with prison for not less than 6 months but less than 3 years. All other crimes na simple offence (small crime).

sections.title: Attempts to commit offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Interpretation
sections.text:
When a person, intending to commit an offence, begins to put his intention into execution by means adapted to its fulfilment, and manifests his intention by some overt act, but does not fulfil his intention to such an extent as to commit the offence, he is said to attempt to commit the offence.
It is immaterial, except so far as regards punishment, whether the offender does all that is necessary on his part for completing the commission of the offence, or whether the complete fulfilment of his intention is prevented by circumstances independent of his will, or whether he desists of his own motion from the further prosecution of his intention.
It is immaterial that by reason of circumstances not known to the offender it is impossible in fact to commit the offence.
The same facts may constitute one offence and an attempt to commit another offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin 'try' mean for crime. If person wan commit crime, start to do am with way wey fit finish am, and show im mind with action, but e no finish am reach di point wey di crime complete, e don try di crime. E no matter, except for punishment, whether di person do everything wey e need to do, or something wey e no control stop am, or e stop by imself. E no matter too if e no fit happen for fact because of something wey di person no know. Di same facts fit be one crime and also try to commit another crime.

sections.title: Arrest without warrant
sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Interpretation
sections.text:
The expression "the offender may be arrested without warrant" means that the provisions of this Code relating to the arrest of offenders or suspected offenders without warrant are applicable to the offence in question, either generally or subject to such conditions, if any, as to time, place, or circumstance, or as to the person authorised to make the arrest, as are specified in the particular case.
Except when otherwise stated, the fact that an offence is within the definition of a felony as set forth in this Code imports that the offender may be arrested without warrant.
The expression "the offender cannot be arrested without warrant" means that the provisions of this Code relating to the arrest of offenders or suspected offenders without warrant are not applicable to the offence in question, except subject to such conditions, if any, as to time, place, or circumstance, or as to the person authorised to make the arrest, as are specified in the particular case.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin 'police fit arrest am without court paper (warrant)' mean. E mean say di parts of dis Code wey talk about arrest without warrant dey work for dat crime, either generally or with di conditions of time, place, circumstance or di person wey fit arrest, wey dem talk for dat case. Unless dem talk another thing, any crime wey be felony (serious crime) mean say police fit arrest am without warrant. 'Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant)' mean say dem no dey work for dat crime, except with di conditions wey dem talk for dat case.

sections.title: Carnal knowledge
sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Interpretation
sections.text:
When the term "carnal knowledge" or the term "carnal connection" is used in defining an offence, it is implied that the offence, so far as regards that element of it, is complete upon penetration.
"unlawful carnal knowledge" means carnal connection which takes place otherwise than between husband and wife.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain 'carnal knowledge' and 'carnal connection'. When dem use dis words to define crime, di crime don complete once penetration happen. 'Unlawful carnal knowledge' mean carnal connection wey no be between husband and wife.

sections.title: Principal offenders
sections.chapter: Chapter 2: Parties to offences
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk who dem count as person wey take part for crime. Dem count each of dem say e don commit di crime, and dem fit charge dem say dem do am: person wey do di act or omission; person wey do or no do something so dat e go help another person commit am; person wey help another person commit am; and person wey counsel or procure another person to commit am. For di fourth one, dem fit charge am say e commit am imself or say e counsel or procure am. Di court finding am guilty of counselling or procuring get di same result as finding am guilty of committing am. Person wey procure another person to do act wey go be crime if e do am imself face di same punishment.

sections.title: Offences committed in prosecution of common purpose
sections.chapter: Chapter 2: Parties to offences
sections.text: When two or more persons form a common intention to prosecute an unlawful purpose in conjunction with one another, and in the prosecution of such purpose an offence is committed of such a nature that its commission was a probable consequence of the prosecution of such purpose, each of them is deemed to have committed the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about when two or more people agree together to do something against di law. If one crime happen as dem dey do dat thing, and di crime na wetin fit likely follow from am, each of dem don commit di crime.

sections.title: Mode of execution immaterial
sections.chapter: Chapter 2: Parties to offences
sections.text:
When a person counsels another to commit an offence, and an offence is actually committed after such counsel by the person to whom it is given, it is immaterial whether the offence actually committed is the same as that counselled or a different one, provided in either case that the facts constituting the offence actually committed are a probable consequence of carrying out the counsel.
In either case, the person who gave the counsel is deemed to have counselled the other person to commit the offence actually committed by him.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about when person counsel another person to commit crime. If di person commit crime after di counsel, e no matter whether di crime na di same one wey dem counsel or another one, as long as e likely to follow from carrying out di counsel. For both cases, dem go count di person wey give di counsel say e counsel di other person to commit di crime wey e actually commit.

sections.title: Accessories after the fact
sections.chapter: Chapter 2: Parties to offences
sections.text:
A person who receives or assists another who is, to his knowledge, guilty of an offence, in order to enable him to escape punishment, is said to become an accessory after the fact to the offence.
A wife does not become an accessory after the fact to an offence of which her husband is guilty by receiving or assisting him in order to enable him to escape punishment; nor by receiving or assisting, in her husband's presence and by his authority, another person who is guilty of an offence in the commission of which her husband has taken part, in order to enable that other person to escape punishment; nor does a husband become accessory after the fact to an offence of which his wife is guilty by receiving or assisting her in order to enable her to escape punishment.
In this section the terms "wife" and "husband" mean respectively the wife and husband of a Christian marriage.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey help another person hide or run after di crime don happen. Person wey receive or help another person wey e sabi say don commit crime, so dat di person go escape punishment, na dat kind person. Wife no be dat kind person if she receive or help her husband so, or if she receive or help, for her husband presence and with im authority, another person wey take part for crime with her husband. Husband too no be dat kind person if e help im wife so. For dis section, wife and husband mean di wife and husband for Christian marriage.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text:
(1) In this Chapter- [L.N. 155 of 1960.]
"Federal law" means any Act enacted by the National Assembly having effect with respect to the Federation and any Act enacted before the 1st day of October, 1960, which under the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria has effect with respect to the Federation; [Cap. C23.]
"law of a State" means any written law enacted by the House of Assembly of the State or having effect as if it were enacted by the said House of Assembly;
"law" includes any order, rule of court, regulation or proclamation made under the authority of such law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section give meaning of some words for Chapter 3. 'Federal law' mean any Act wey di National Assembly make wey get effect for di Federation, and any Act wey dem make before 1 October 1960 wey, under di Constitution, get effect for di Federation. 'Law of a State' mean any written law wey di House of Assembly of di State make, or wey get effect as if di House make am. 'Law' include any order, rule of court, regulation or proclamation wey dem make under di authority of such law.

sections.title: Effect of changes in law
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text: A person shall not be punished for doing or omitting to do an act unless the act or omission constituted an offence under the law in force when it occurred.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say dem no fit punish person for doing or no doing something, except say di act or omission na crime under di law wey dey force when e happen.

sections.title: Application of code as to offences wholly or partially committed in Nigeria
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text:
Where by the provisions of any Federal law the doing of any act or the making of any omission constituted an offence, those provisions shall apply to every person who is in Nigeria at the time of his doing the act or making the omission.
With regard to such offences which are of such a nature that they comprise several elements, if any acts or omissions or events actually occur, which, if they all occurred in Nigeria, would constitute an offence and any of such acts or omissions or events occur in Nigeria, although all or some of the other acts or omissions or events which, if they occurred in Nigeria, would be elements of the offence occur elsewhere than in Nigeria; then-
(1) if the act or omission, which in the case of an offence wholly committed in Nigeria would be the initial element of the offence, occurs in Nigeria, the person who does that act or makes that omission is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment, as if all the subsequent elements of the offence had occurred in Nigeria; and
(2) if that act or omission occurs elsewhere than in Nigeria, and the person who does that act or makes that omission afterwards comes into Nigeria, he is by such coming into Nigeria guilty of an offence of the same kind, and is liable to the same punishment, as if that act or omission had occurred in Nigeria and he had been in Nigeria when it occurred.
But in any such case it is a defence to the charge to prove that the accused person did not intend that the act or omission should have effect in Nigeria. This section does not extend to a case in which the only material event that occurs in Nigeria is the death in Nigeria of a person whose death is caused by an act, done or omitted to be done, at a place not in Nigeria and at a time when he was not in Nigeria.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk how Federal laws take work for crime wey happen partly outside Nigeria. Any person wey dey Nigeria when e do act or omission wey Federal law make crime don commit am. If crime get many parts and some happen for Nigeria, and di first part happen for Nigeria, di person don commit di same kind of crime and go face di same punishment. If di first part happen outside Nigeria and di person come enter Nigeria after, e don commit am by coming. But e get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di accused fit prove say e no wan make di act or omission get effect for Nigeria. Dis section no cover case wey di only main event for Nigeria na di death for Nigeria of person wey die from act or omission outside Nigeria when e no dey Nigeria.

sections.title: Offences against laws of a State
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text:
(1) Where by the provisions of any law of a State the doing of any act or the making of any omission is constituted an offence, those provisions shall apply to every person who is in the State at the time of his doing the act or making the omission.
(2) With regard to any such offence which is of such a nature that it comprises several elements, if any acts or omissions or events actually occur, which, if they all occurred in the State, would constitute an offence, and any of such acts or omissions or events occur in the State, although all or some of the other acts or omissions or events which, if they occurred in the State, would be elements of the offence, occur elsewhere than in the State, then-
(a) if the act or omission, which in the case of an offence committed wholly in the State would be the initial element of the offence, occurs in the State, the person who does that act or makes that omission is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if all the subsequent elements of the offence had occurred in the State; and
(b) if that act or omission occurs elsewhere than in the State, and the person who does that act or makes that omission afterwards comes into the State, he is by such coming into the State guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment, as if that act or omission had occurred in the State and he had been in the State when it occurred.
But in any such case, it is a defence to the charge to prove that the accused person did not intend that the act or omission should have effect in the State. This subsection does not extend to a case in which the only material event that occurs in the State is the death in the State of a person whose death is caused by an act, done or omitted to be done, at a place not in the State and at a time when he was not in the State.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk how laws of a State take work for crime wey happen partly outside di State. Any person wey dey di State when e do act or omission wey law of di State make crime don commit am. If crime get many parts and di first part happen for di State, di person don commit di same kind of crime and go face di same punishment. If di first part happen outside di State and di person come enter di State after, e don commit am by coming. But e get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di accused fit prove say e no wan make di act or omission get effect for di State. Dis no cover case wey di only main event for di State na di death of person wey die from act or omission outside di State.

sections.title: Offences procured or counselled by persons out of Nigeria
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text:
(1) Any person who, having while out of Nigeria procured another to do or omit to do in Nigeria an act of such a nature that if he had himself done the act or made the omission in Nigeria, he would have been guilty of an offence, afterwards comes into Nigeria, is by such coming into Nigeria guilty of an offence of the same kind, and is liable to the same punishment, as if he himself had done the act or made the omission in Nigeria.
Any person who, having while out of Nigeria counselled or procured the commission of an offence which is actually committed in Nigeria, afterwards comes into Nigeria, is by such coming into Nigeria guilty of an offence of the same kind, and is liable to the same punishment, as if he had been in Nigeria when the offence was committed.
(2) In this section, "offence" means an offence against any Federal law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey, when e dey outside Nigeria, procure another person to do or no do something for Nigeria wey go be crime if e do am imself, and e come enter Nigeria after. By coming enter Nigeria, e don commit di same kind of crime and go face di same punishment as if e do am imself for Nigeria. Di same go apply to person wey counsel or procure crime wey dem actually commit for Nigeria while e dey outside Nigeria, and e come enter Nigeria after. For dis section, crime mean crime against any Federal law.

sections.title: Offences against State laws procured, etc., outside the State
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text: The provisions of section 13 shall apply in relation to offences against a law of the State as they apply in relation to offences against a Federal law but as if references to Nigeria were references to the State.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say section 13 go work for crimes against law of di State di same way e work for crimes against Federal law, but make dem read 'Nigeria' as 'di State'.

sections.title: Offences procured in Nigeria to be committed out of Nigeria
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text: Any person who, while in Nigeria, procures another to do an act or make an omission at a place not in Nigeria of such a nature that, if he had himself done the act or made the omission in Nigeria, he would have been guilty of an offence, and that, if he had himself done the act or made the omission, he would have been guilty of an offence under the laws in force in the place where the act or omission is done or made, is guilty of an offence of the same kind, and is liable to the same punishment, as if the act had been done or the omission had been made in Nigeria.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey, while e dey Nigeria, procure another person to do act or omission for place outside Nigeria. If di act or omission go be crime if e do am imself for Nigeria, and e go also be crime under di laws wey dey force for dat place, e don commit di same kind of crime and go face di same punishment as if di act or omission happen for Nigeria.

sections.title: Offences procured in the State to be committed out of the State
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text: Any person who, while in a State, procures another to do an act or make an omission at a place not in the State of such a nature that if he had himself done the act or made the omission in the State, he would have been guilty of an offence against a law of the State, and that, if he had himself done the act or made the omission, he would have been guilty of an offence under the laws of the place where the act or omission is done or made, is guilty of an offence of the same kind, and is liable to the same punishment, as if the act had been done or the omission had been made in the State.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey, while e dey for a State, procure another person to do act or omission for place wey no be dat State. If di act or omission go be crime against law of di State if e do am imself, and e go also be crime under di laws of di place where e happen, e don commit di same kind of crime and go face di same punishment as if di act or omission happen for di State.

sections.title: Armed forces and police forces
sections.chapter: Chapter 3: Application of Criminal Law
sections.text: Members of the armed forces and of the police force of Nigeria are subject to the special laws relating to the forces to which they respectively belong, but are not exempt from the provisions of this Code. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section say members of di armed forces and di police force of Nigeria dey under di special laws for di force wey dem belong, but dem still dey under di provisions of dis Code.

sections.title: Kinds of punishments
sections.chapter: Chapter 4: Punishments
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of any other written law, the punishments which may be inflicted under this Code are death, imprisonment, caning, fine and forfeiture. [1960 No. 30.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section list di punishments wey fit dey under dis Code, subject to any other written law. Dem be death, prison, caning, fine (money wey person go pay) and forfeiture.

sections.title: Caning for male persons under seventeen
sections.chapter: Chapter 4: Punishments
sections.text: Whenever a male person who, in the opinion of the court, has not attained seventeen years of age, has been found guilty of any offence the court may, in its discretion, order him to be caned in addition to or in substitution for any other punishments to which he is liable.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about caning for male person wey, as di court see am, never reach 17 years. If di court find am guilty of any crime, di court fit order make dem cane am, either on top any other punishment wey e fit get or instead of am.

sections.title: Forfeiture of bribes
sections.chapter: Chapter 4: Punishments
sections.text: When any person is convicted of an offence under section 98, 98A, 98B, 99, 112, 117, 126, 128 or 494 of this Code, the court may, in addition to or in lieu of any penalty which may be imposed, order the forfeiture to the State of any property which has passed in connection with the commission of the offence or, if such property cannot be forfeited or cannot be found, of such sum as the court shall assess as the value of such property, and any property or sum so forfeited shall be dealt with in such manner as the Governor may direct. Payment of any sum so ordered to be forfeited may be enforced in the same manner and subject to the same incidents as in the case of the payment of a fine. [1960 No. 30. 1966 No. 84. 1960 No. 30. L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about property wey dem give as bribe. If di court find person guilty of crime under section 98, 98A, 98B, 99, 112, 117, 126, 128 or 494 of dis Code, di court fit order make State take any property wey pass hand for di crime, either on top or instead of any other punishment. If dem no fit take di property or dem no see am, di court fit order make person pay di sum wey di court value di property. Dem go handle di property or money as di Governor direct. Dem fit force payment of di money di same way dem dey force payment of fine (money wey person go pay).

sections.title: Forfeiture of property used in postal offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 4: Punishments
sections.text: When any person is convicted of an offence under section 170, 175, 177, 179, 180 or 183 of this Code, the court may, in addition to or in lieu of any penalty which may be imposed, order the forfeiture of any personal property which has been used in the commission of the offence or in respect of which the offence has been committed and may order such property to be destroyed or otherwise dealt with as to it may seem fit.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about property wey dem use for post crimes. If di court find person guilty of crime under section 170, 175, 177, 179, 180 or 183 of dis Code, di court fit order make dem take any personal property wey dem use do di crime or wey di crime concern, either on top or instead of any other punishment. Di court fit order make dem destroy am or handle am as di court see fit.

sections.title: Prerogative
sections.chapter: Chapter 4: Punishments
sections.text: Nothing in this Code affects the prerogative of mercy where exercised in accordance with the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. [L.N. 112 of 1964. Cap. C23.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section say nothing for dis Code touch di prerogative of mercy, when dem use am according to di Constitution of di Federal Republic of Nigeria.

sections.title: Ignorance of law
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: Ignorance of the law does not afford any excuse for any act or omission which would otherwise constitute an offence, unless knowledge of the law by the offender is expressly declared to be an element of the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say if person no know di law, dat no be excuse for act or omission wey go be crime, except say di law clearly make di person knowing di law part of wetin make di crime.

sections.title: Bona fide claim of right
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: A person is not criminally responsible, as for an offence relating to property, for an act done or omitted to be done by him with respect to any property in the exercise of an honest claim of right and without intention to defraud.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say person no dey criminally responsible for crime wey concern property, if e do or no do something about any property with honest claim of right and without wanting to cheat.

sections.title: Intention: motive
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
Subject to the express provisions of this Code relating to negligent acts and omissions, a person is not criminally responsible for an act or omission which occurs independently of the exercise of his will, or for an event which occurs by accident.
Unless the intention to cause a particular result is expressly declared to be an element of the offence constituted, in whole or part, by an act or omission, the result intended to be caused by an act or omission is immaterial.
Unless otherwise expressly declared, the motive by which a person is induced to do or omit to do an act, or to form an intention, is immaterial so far as regards criminal responsibility.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about intention and motive. Person no dey criminally responsible for act or omission wey happen without im will, or for event wey happen by accident, but dis dey subject to wetin dis Code talk about careless acts and omissions. Di result wey person wan cause no matter, except say di law clearly make intention to cause one particular result part of di crime. Di reason (motive) wey make person do or no do something no matter for criminal responsibility, except say di law talk another thing.

sections.title: Mistake of fact
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
A person who does or omits to do an act under an honest and reasonable, but mistaken, belief in the existence of any state of things, is not criminally responsible for the act or omission to any greater extent than if the real state of things had been such as he believed to exist.
The operation of this rule may be excluded by the express or implied provisions of the law relating to the subject.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about mistake of fact. If person do or no do something because e honestly and reasonably believe say something dey true wey no be true, di person no dey criminally responsible pass as if di thing wey e believe na di real situation. But di law for dat matter fit remove dis rule, either clearly or by wetin e mean.

sections.title: Extraordinary emergencies
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: Subject to the express provisions of this Code relating to acts done upon compulsion or provocation or in self-defence, a person is not criminally responsible for an act done or omission made under such circumstances of sudden or extraordinary emergency that an ordinary person possessing ordinary power of self-control could not reasonably be expected to act otherwise.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sudden or extraordinary emergency. Person no dey criminally responsible for act or omission wey e do for such emergency wey ordinary person wey get ordinary power to control imself no fit reasonably do another thing. Dis dey subject to di parts of dis Code wey talk about acts wey person do under force, provocation or self-defence.

sections.title: Presumption of sanity
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: Every person is presumed to be of sound mind and to have been of sound mind at any time which comes in question, until the contrary is proved.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say di law count every person as person wey get sound mind, and wey get sound mind any time wey question dey about am, until dem prove say e no be so.

sections.title: Insanity
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
A person is not criminally responsible for an act or omission if at the time of doing the act or making the omission he is in such a state of mental disease or natural mental infirmity as to deprive him of capacity to understand what he is doing, or of capacity to control his actions, or of capacity to know that he ought not to do the act or make the omission.
A person whose mind, at the time of his doing or omitting to do an act, is affected by delusions on some specific matter or matters, but who is not otherwise entitled to the benefit of the foregoing provisions of this section, is criminally responsible for the act or omission to the same extent as if the real state of things had been such as he was induced by the delusion to believe to exist.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about insanity. Person no dey criminally responsible for act or omission if, when e do am, im mind sick or e get natural weakness of mind so dat e no fit understand wetin e dey do, or e no fit control im actions, or e no fit know say e no suppose do or leave am. If person get delusions about one or more particular matter, but di first part no cover am, e still dey criminally responsible to di same extent as if di real situation na wetin di delusion make am believe.

sections.title: Intoxication
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
(1) Save as provided in this section, intoxication shall not constitute a defence to any criminal charge.
(2) Intoxication shall be a defence to any criminal charge if by reason thereof the person charged at the time of the act or omission complained of did not know that such act or omission was wrong or did not know what he was doing and-
(a) the state of intoxication was caused without his consent by the malicious or negligent act of another person; or
(b) the person charged was by reason of intoxication insane, temporarily or otherwise, at the time of such act or omission.
(3) Where the defence under the preceding subsection is established, then in a case falling under paragraph (a) thereof, the accused person shall be discharged, and in a case falling under paragraph (b), sections 229 and 230 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply.
(4) Intoxication shall be taken into account for the purpose of determining whether the person charged had formed any intention, specific or otherwise, in the absence of which he would not be guilty of the offence.
(5) For the purposes of this section, "intoxication" shall be deemed to include a state produced by narcotics or drugs.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about intoxication. Normally, intoxication no be defence (reason wey di law accept) for any criminal charge. But e na defence if di person no know say di act or omission dey wrong, or no know wetin e dey do, and either another person bad or careless act make am drunk without im agreement, or di intoxication make am insane, for small time or otherwise. For di first case, dem must discharge di accused. For di second case, sections 229 and 230 of di Criminal Procedure Act go apply. Dem go also look intoxication to know whether di person get di intention wey di crime need. Intoxication include state wey narcotics or drugs cause.

sections.title: Immature age
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
A person under the age of seven years is not criminally responsible for any act or omission.
A person under the age of twelve years is not criminally responsible for an act or omission, unless it is proved that at the time of doing the act or making the omission he had capacity to know that he ought not to do the act or make the omission.
A male person under the age of twelve years is presumed to be incapable of having carnal knowledge.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about young age. Person wey never reach 7 years no dey criminally responsible for any act or omission. Person wey never reach 12 years no dey criminally responsible, unless dem prove say, when e do am, e fit know say e no suppose do or leave am. Dem presume say male person wey never reach 12 years no fit have carnal knowledge.

sections.title: Judicial officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: Except as expressly provided by this Code, a judicial officer is not criminally responsible for anything done or omitted to be done by him in the exercise of his judicial functions, although the act done is in excess of his judicial authority or although he is bound to do the act omitted to be done.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say, except where dis Code clearly talk another thing, judicial officer no dey criminally responsible for anything wey e do or no do as e dey do im judicial work, even if wetin e do pass im judicial authority, or even if e suppose do wetin e no do.

sections.title: Justification and excuse: compulsion
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk when person no dey criminally responsible for act or omission. E dey so if e do am to carry out di law; to obey order of competent authority wey di law bind am to obey, except say di order clear say e against di law; to resist real unlawful violence wey dem threaten am or another person wey dey im presence, as e reasonably need; or to save imself from immediate death or grievous harm wey person wey dey there and fit do am threaten, as e believe say e no fit escape another way. But di last one no cover crime wey death punish, or crime wey grievous harm to another person or intention to cause am dey inside, or person wey join unlawful association or plan together make dem threaten am. Whether order clear say e against di law na question of law.

sections.title: Compulsion of husband
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
A married woman is not free from criminal responsibility for doing or omitting to do an act merely because the act or omission takes place in the presence of her husband.
But a wife of a Christian marriage is not criminally responsible for doing or omitting to do an act which she is actually compelled by her husband to do or omit to do, and which is done or omitted to be done in his presence, except in the case of an act or omission which would constitute an offence punishable with death, or an offence of which grievous harm to the person of another, or an intention to cause such harm, is an element, in which case the presence of her husband is immaterial.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wife wey act for her husband presence. Married woman no free from criminal responsibility just because di act or omission happen for her husband presence. But wife for Christian marriage no dey criminally responsible for act or omission wey her husband really force her to do or no do, for im presence. But if di crime na wey death punish, or wey grievous harm to another person or intention to cause am dey inside, her husband presence no matter.

sections.title: No conspiracy between husband and wife alone
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: A husband and wife of Christian marriage are not criminally responsible for a conspiracy between themselves alone.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say husband and wife for Christian marriage no dey criminally responsible for plan together wey na only dem two make.

sections.title: Offences by partners and members of companies with respect to partnership or corporate property
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text: A person who, being a member of a co-partnership, corporation, or joint stock company, does or omits to do any act with respect to the property of the co-partnership, corporation, or company, which, if he were not a member of the co-partnership, corporation or company, would constitute an offence, is criminally responsible to the same extent as if he were not such member.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about members of partnership, corporation or joint stock company. If member do or no do any act about di property of di partnership, corporation or company, wey go be crime if e no be member, e dey criminally responsible to di same extent as if e no be member.

sections.title: Liability of husband and wife for offences committed by either with respect to the other's property
sections.chapter: Chapter 5: Criminal responsibility
sections.text:
When a husband and wife of a Christian marriage are living together, neither of them incurs any criminal responsibility for doing or omitting to do any act with respect to the property of the other, except in the case of an act or omission of which an intention to injure or defraud some other person is an element, and except in the case of an act done by either of them when leaving or deserting, or when about to leave or desert, the other.
Subject to the foregoing provisions, a husband and wife are, each of them, criminally responsible for any act done by him or her with respect to the property of the other, which would be an offence if they were not husband and wife, and to the same extent as if they were not husband and wife.
But in the case of a Christian marriage neither of them can institute criminal proceedings against the other while they are living together.
In this section, the term "property" used with respect to a wife means her separate property.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about husband and wife for Christian marriage wey dey live together, and di property of each other. Neither of dem dey criminally responsible for act or omission about di other property, except where intention to injure or cheat another person dey inside, and except for act wey either do when e dey leave or desert, or about to leave or desert, di other. Apart from dat, each of dem dey criminally responsible for act about di other property wey go be crime if dem no be husband and wife, to di same extent. But for Christian marriage, neither fit start criminal case against di other while dem dey live together. For dis section, wife property mean her separate property.

sections.title: Treason
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
(1) Any person who levies war against the State, in order to intimidate or overawe the President or the Governor of a State, is guilty of treason, and is liable to the punishment of death. [L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
(2) Any person conspiring with any person, either within or without Nigeria, to levy war against the State with intent to cause such levying of war as would be treason if committed by a citizen of Nigeria, is guilty of treason and is liable to the punishment of death:
Provided that nothing in this section shall prevent any act from being treason which is so by the laws of England as in force in Nigeria.
(3) (Inserted by L.N. 112 of 1964 and deleted by L.N. 139 of 1965).
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about treason. Person wey levy war against di State to scare or overpower di President or di Governor of a State don commit treason. Person wey plan together with another person, inside or outside Nigeria, to levy war against di State so dat war go happen wey go be treason if citizen of Nigeria do am, don commit treason too. Di punishment na death. But anything wey be treason under di laws of England as dem dey force for Nigeria still na treason.

sections.title: Instigating invasion of Nigeria
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text: Any person who instigates any foreigner to invade Nigeria with an armed force is guilty of treason, and is liable to the punishment of death.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey instigate foreigner to invade Nigeria with armed force. E don commit treason. Di punishment na death.

sections.title: Provision as to juvenile offenders and pregnant women
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
(1) Where an offender who, in the opinion of the court, had not attained the age of seventeen years at the time the offence was committed, has been found guilty of an offence against either section 37 or 38 of this Code, such offender shall not be sentenced to death but shall be ordered to be detained during the pleasure of the President and upon such an order being made the provisions of Part 44 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply. [1066 No. 84. L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27. Cap. C41.]
(2) Where a woman who has been convicted of an offence against either section 37 or 38 of this Code alleges she is pregnant, or where the judge before whom she is convicted considers it advisable to have inquiries made as to whether or not she be pregnant, the procedure laid down in section 376 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall first be complied with.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about young people and pregnant women for treason cases under section 37 or 38 of dis Code. If di court find person guilty of dat crime and di court believe say e never reach 17 years when e do am, di court no go sentence am to death. Dem go order make dem detain am as long as di President want, and Part 44 of di Criminal Procedure Act go apply. If woman wey di court find guilty of dat crime say she dey pregnant, or di judge feel say dem need to check whether she dey pregnant, dem must first follow di process for section 376 of di Criminal Procedure Act.

sections.title: Concealment of treason
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
Any person who- [1967 No. 27.]
(a) becomes an accessory after the fact to treason; or
(b) knowing that any person intends to commit treason, does not give information thereof with all reasonable despatch to the President or the Governor of the State or a peace officer, or use other reasonable endeavours to prevent the commission of the offence, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding treason. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e be person wey help another person hide or run after treason don happen, or if e sabi say person wan commit treason and e no give information with all reasonable speed to di President, di Governor of di State or peace officer, or e no use other reasonable effort to stop am. Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Treasonable felonies
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
Any person who forms an intention to effect any of the following purposes, that is to say- [L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
(a) to remove during his term of office otherwise than by constitutional means the President as Head of State of the Federation and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces thereof; or
(b) to likewise remove during his term of office the Governor of a State; or
(c) to levy war against Nigeria in order by force or constraint to compel the President to change his measures or counsels, or in order to put any force or constraint upon, or in order to intimidate or overawe any House of the National Assembly or any other legislature or legislative authority; or
(d) to instigate any foreigner to make any armed invasion of Nigeria or any of the territories thereof, and manifests such intention by an overt act, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
A person charged with any of the felonies defined in this section is not entitled to be acquitted on the ground that any act proved to have been committed by him constitutes the offence of treason; but a person who has been tried, and convicted or acquitted, on a charge of any such offence, cannot be afterwards prosecuted for treason in respect of the same facts.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about treasonable felonies. Person wey get intention to do any of dis ones, and show am by action (overt act), don commit felony (serious crime): remove di President, as Head of State and Commander-in-Chief of di Armed Forces, or di Governor of a State, during im term of office without constitutional means; levy war against Nigeria to force di President to change im measures or counsels, or to force or scare any House of di National Assembly or other legislature; or instigate foreigner to invade Nigeria or any of im territories with arms. Di punishment na prison for life. Di accused no go go free just because wetin e do na treason. But person wey di court don try for any of dem and find guilty or not guilty, dem no fit prosecute am again for treason for di same facts.

sections.title: Promoting inter-communal war
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text: Any person who, without lawful authority, carries on, or makes preparation for carrying on, or aids in or advises the carrying on of, or preparation for, any war or warlike undertaking with, for, by, or against, any traditional chief, or with, for, by, or against any band of citizens, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about promoting war between communities. Person wey, without authority wey di law give am, carry on, prepare for, help or advise war or warlike thing with, for, by or against any traditional chief or any group of citizens don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Time for proceeding in cases of treason, concealment of treason or promoting inter-communal war
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text: A person cannot be tried for treason, or for any of the felonies defined in the three last preceding sections, unless the prosecution is commenced within two years after the offence is committed.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say dem no fit try person for treason, or for di felonies wey di three sections before dis one define, except dem start di case within 2 years after di crime happen.

sections.title: Inciting to mutiny
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
Any person who advisedly attempts to effect any of the following purposes, that is to say- [L.N. 112 or 1964.]
(a)
(b)
(c) to seduce any person serving in any of the Armed Forces of Nigeria or any member of the Police Force from his duty and allegiance; or to incite any such persons to commit an act of mutiny or any traitorous or mutinous act; or to incite any such persons to make or endeavour to make a mutinous assembly, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about inciting to mutiny. Person wey on purpose try to lure person wey dey serve for di Armed Forces of Nigeria or member of di Police Force from im duty and loyalty; or push any of dem to commit mutiny or any traitorous or mutinous act; or push dem to make or try to make mutinous gathering, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Aiding and inciting to mutinous acts or disobedience of members of armed forces or policemen
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
Any person who- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(a) aids, abets, or is accessory to, any act of mutiny by; or
(b) incites to sedition or to disobedience to any lawful order given by a superior officer, any warrant or other officer below commissioned rank and others inferior in rank to them and by whatever name described in any of the Armed Forces of Nigeria or any Police Officer, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years and to a fine of four hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about helping or pushing members of di armed forces or police to mutinous acts or disobedience. Person wey help or be accessory to any act of mutiny by, or push to sedition or to disobey any lawful order of superior officer, any warrant officer or other officer below commissioned rank and others lower for any of di Armed Forces of Nigeria, or any Police Officer, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years and fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦400.

sections.title: Inducing such persons to desert
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
Any person who, by any means whatever, directly or indirectly- [L.N. 112 of 1964. L.N. 139 of 1963.]
(a) procures or persuades or attempts to procure or persuade to desert; or
(b) aids, abets, or is accessory to the desertion of; or
(c) having reason to believe he is a deserter, habours or aids in concealing, any warrant or other officer below commissioned rank and others inferior in rank to them and by whatever name described in any of the said armed forces or any police officer, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for six months and to a fine of one hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about pushing members of di armed forces or police to desert. Person wey, by any means, directly or indirectly, persuade or try to persuade, or help or be accessory to di desertion of, or, as e get reason to believe say e na deserter, hide or help hide, any warrant officer or other officer below commissioned rank and others lower for di armed forces, or any police officer, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 6 months and fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100.

sections.title: Causing disaffection among members of armed forces, police or prison officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text:
(1) Any person who, by any means whatever, causes or attempts to cause, or does any act calculated to cause disaffection amongst persons serving as- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(a) members of the Armed Forces of Nigeria;
(b) Police Officers; or
(c) Prison Officers, or does any act calculated to induce any person serving as aforesaid to withhold his services or to commit breaches of discipline, is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or to a fine not exceeding six hundred naira or to both such imprisonment and fine and, if a police officer or prison officer, shall forfeit all pension rights and be disqualified for being a police officer or prison officer, as the case may be.
(2) In this section, the expression "prison officer" has the same meaning as in subsection (1) of section 10 of the Prisons Act.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about causing disaffection among members of di armed forces, police or prison officers. Person wey, by any means, cause or try to cause, or do any act wey fit cause, disaffection among dem, or any act wey fit make dem withhold dia service or break discipline, don commit crime. Di punishment na prison for not more than 3 years, or fine (money wey person go pay) of not more than ₦600, or both. If di person na police officer or prison officer, e go lose all im pension rights and e no go fit be police officer or prison officer again. For dis section, prison officer get di same meaning as for section 10(1) of di Prisons Act.

sections.title: Effect of proceeding under sections 44 and 45
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text: A person who has been tried, and convicted or acquitted, on a charge of any of the offences defined in sections 44 and 45 of this Code, cannot be afterwards prosecuted for any other offence defined in this Chapter in respect of the same facts.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say person wey di court don try for any crime under section 44 and 45 of dis Code, and find guilty or not guilty, dem no fit prosecute am again for any other crime wey dis Chapter define, for di same facts.

sections.title: Assisting or allowing escape of prisoners of war
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about helping or allowing prisoners of war to escape. Person wey, as e sabi say and on purpose, help alien enemy of Nigeria wey be prisoner of war for Nigeria, whether dem keep am for prison or another place or e dey free on im parole, to escape from im prison or place, or, if e dey free on parole, to run comot Nigeria, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life. Person wey carelessly and for wrong way (against di law) allow any such person to escape don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Overt act
sections.chapter: Chapter 6: Treason and certain other offences
sections.text: In the case of any of the offences defined in this Chapter, when the manifestation by an overt act of an intention to effect any purpose is an element of the offence, every act of conspiring with any person to effect that purpose, and every act done in furtherance of the purpose by any of the persons conspiring, is deemed to be an overt act manifesting the intention.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about action wey show intention (overt act) for di crimes for dis Chapter. If showing intention by action na part of di crime, every act of planning together with another person to do dat purpose, and every act wey any of di people wey plan together do to help di purpose, count as action wey show di intention.

sections.title: Death penalty for treachery
sections.chapter: Chapter 6A: Treachery
sections.text:
(1) If, with intent to help the enemy in any war in which Nigeria may be engaged, any person does, or attempts to do, any act which is designed or likely to give assistance to the naval, military or air operations of the enemy, to impede such operations of the armed forces of Nigeria, or to endanger life, he is guilty of felony and liable on conviction to suffer death. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(2) No prosecution in respect of any offence against this section shall be instituted except by, or with the consent of, the Attorney-General or Solicitor-General of the Federation:
Provided that this subsection shall not prevent the arrest, or the issue or the execution of a warrant for the arrest, of any person in respect of any offence, or the remanding, in custody or on bail, of any person charged with such an offence, notwithstanding that the consent of the Attorney-General or Solicitor-General of the Federation to the institution of a prosecution for the offence has not been obtained.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about treachery. If person, wey wan help di enemy for any war wey Nigeria dey, do or try to do any act wey dem design or fit give help to di naval, military or air operations of di enemy, or to block such operations of di armed forces of Nigeria, or to put life for danger, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment, if di court find am guilty, na death. Dem no fit start case for dis crime except di Attorney-General or Solicitor-General of di Federation start am or agree. But dis no stop dem from arrest person, or issue or carry out arrest warrant, or remand di person for custody or on bail, even before di Attorney-General or Solicitor-General agree.

sections.title: Joinder of charges and place of trial of offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 6A: Treachery
sections.text:
(1) Notwithstanding any rule of law or practice, charges for any offences, except treason, may be joined with a charge for any offence against the preceding section in the same charge or information, if those charges are founded on the same facts, or form, or are a part of, a series of offences of the same or a similar character. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(2) A person charged with an offence against this Chapter who is in Nigeria may, whether or not the offence was committed in Nigeria or in any Nigerian ship or aircraft, be taken in custody to any place in Nigeria, and may be proceeded against, charged, tried and punished in any place in Nigeria, as if the offence had been committed in that part of Nigeria, and for all purposes incidental to or consequential on the trial or punishment of the offence it shall be deemed to have been committed in that part of Nigeria.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about joining charges and where dem fit try crimes for di Chapter on treachery. Dem fit join charge for any crime, except treason, with charge under section 49A for di same charge or information, if dem dey based on di same facts, or dey part of series of crimes wey be di same or similar kind. Person wey dem charge for dis Chapter wey dey Nigeria fit dey taken for custody to any place for Nigeria. Dem fit charge, try and punish am for any place for Nigeria, whether di crime happen for Nigeria or for any Nigerian ship or aircraft, as if di crime happen for dat part of Nigeria.

sections.title: Extent of Chapter
sections.chapter: Chapter 6A: Treachery
sections.text: The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to anything done by any person in Nigeria. [L.N. 112 of 1964.] 49D. (Deleted by L.N. 121 of 1964).
sections.pidgin: Dis section say di Chapter on treachery go apply to anything wey any person do for Nigeria.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text:
(1) In this Chapter, unless the context otherwise requires-
"import" includes- [L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
(a) to bring into Nigeria; and
(b) to bring within the inland waters of Nigeria whether or not the publication is brought ashore, and whether or not there is an intention to bring the same ashore;
"periodical publication" includes every publication issued periodically or in parts or numbers at intervals whether regular or irregular;
"publication" includes all written or printed matter and everything, whether of a nature similar to written or printed matter or not, containing any visible representation, or by its form, shape, or in any manner capable of suggesting words or ideas, and every copy and reproduction of any publication;
"seditious publication" means a publication having a seditious intention;
"seditious words" means words having a seditious intention.
(2) A "seditious intention" is an intention-
(a) to bring into hatred or contempt or excite disaffection against the person of the President or of the Governor of a State or the Government of the Federation; or
(b) to excite the citizens or other inhabitants of Nigeria to attempt to procure the alteration, otherwise than by lawful means, of any other matter in Nigeria as by law established; or
(c) to raise discontent or disaffection amongst the citizens or other inhabitants of Nigeria; or
(d) to promote feelings of ill-will and hostility between different classes of the population of Nigeria, but an act, speech or publication is not seditious by reason only that it intends-
(i) to show that the President or the Governor of a State has been misled or mistaken in any measure in the Federation or a State, as the case may be; or
(ii) to point out errors or defects in the Government or Constitution of Nigeria, or of any State thereof, as by law established or in legislation or in the administration of justice with a view to the remedying of such errors or defects; or
(iii) to persuade the citizens or other inhabitants of Nigeria to attempt to procure by lawful means the alteration of any matter in Nigeria as by law established; or
(iv) to point out, with a view to their removal, any matters which are producing or have a tendency to produce feelings of ill-will and enmity between different classes of the population of Nigeria.
(3) In determining whether the intention with which any act was done, any words were spoken, or any document was published, was or was not seditious, every person shall be deemed to intend the consequences which would naturally follow from his conduct at the time and under the circumstances in which he so conducted himself.
sections.pidgin: Dis section give meaning of words for dis Chapter on sedition, like 'import', 'publication', 'seditious publication' and 'seditious words'. E explain 'seditious intention': to bring di President, di Governor of a State or di Government of di Federation into hatred or contempt, or cause disaffection against dem; to push people to try to change any matter for Nigeria by unlawful means; to raise discontent among people for Nigeria; or to promote ill-will and hostility between different classes of people. But act, speech or publication no be seditious only because e wan show say di President or Governor don make mistake, point out errors for Government or di law, persuade people to change something by lawful means, or point out things wey dey cause ill-will so dat dem go remove dem. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sedition crimes. Person wey do or try to do, prepare, or plan together with another person to do any act with seditious intention; or talk seditious words; or print, publish, sell, offer to sell, distribute or reproduce seditious publication; or import am, except say e no get reason to believe say e seditious, don commit crime. For first crime, di punishment na prison for 2 years, or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200, or both. For later crime, na prison for 3 years. Person wey, without authority wey di law give am, get seditious publication don commit crime too. For first crime, na prison for 1 year, or fine of ₦100, or both. For later crime, na prison for 2 years. Di State go take di publication.

sections.title: Legal proceedings: evidence
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text:
(1) No prosecution for an offence under section 51 of this Code shall be begun except within six months after the offence is committed.
(2) A person shall not be prosecuted for an offence under section 51 without the written consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation or of the State concerned.
(3) No person shall be convicted of an offence under paragraph (b) of subsection (1) of section 51 of this Code on the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about legal proceedings under section 51 of dis Code. Dem must start di case within 6 months after di crime happen. Dem no fit prosecute person without written agreement of di Attorney-General of di Federation or of di State wey concern am. Dem no fit find person guilty under paragraph (b) of subsection (1) of section 51 only because one witness talk and no other evidence support am.

sections.title: Unlawful oaths to commit capital offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) administers, or is present at and consents to the administering of, any oath, or engagement in the nature of an oath, purporting to bind the person who takes it to commit any offence punishable with death; or
(2) takes any such oath or engagement, not being compelled to do so; or
(3) attempts to induce any person to take any such oath or engagement, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful oaths to commit crimes wey death dey punish. Person wey give, or dey there and agree make dem give, any oath or promise wey be like oath wey dem mean to bind person wey take am to commit crime wey death punish; or take such oath or promise without say dem force am; or try to push person to take am, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Other unlawful oaths to commit offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about other unlawful oaths to commit crimes. Person wey give, or dey there and agree make dem give, oath or promise wey be like oath wey dem mean to bind person to: join mutinous or seditious thing; commit any crime wey death no punish, apart from simple offence (small crime); disturb public peace; join any group wey dem form for dis things; no inform or give evidence against any partner or person; or no reveal any unlawful group, illegal act, or illegal oath or promise, don commit felony (serious crime). Person wey take such oath without say dem force am, or try to push person to take am, don commit di same felony. Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Compulsion: how far a defence
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text: A person who takes any such oath or engagement as is mentioned in the two last preceding sections shall not set up as a defence that he was compelled to do so, unless within fourteen days after taking, or, if he is prevented by actual force or sickness, within fourteen days after the termination of such prevention, he declares by information on oath before some peace officer, or, if he is on actual service in the armed forces of Nigeria, or in the police forces, either by such information or by information to his commanding officer, the whole of what he knows concerning the matter, including the person or persons by whom and in whose presence, and the place where, and the time when, the oath or engagement was administered or taken. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about when person fit use say dem force am as defence (reason wey di law accept) for taking oath wey sections 53 and 54 talk about. Di person no fit use am, except say within 14 days after e take am, or within 14 days after di real force or sickness wey stop am end, e declare, by information on oath before peace officer, everything wey e sabi about di matter. If e dey serve for di armed forces or police, e fit do am by such information or by information to im commanding officer. E must include di people wey give am and wey dey there, di place and di time dem give or take di oath or promise.

sections.title: Effect of prosecution
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text: A person who has been tried, and convicted or acquitted, on a charge of any of the offences in this Chapter defined, shall not be afterwards prosecuted upon the same facts for the offence of treason, or for the offence of failing, when he knows that any person intends to commit treason, to give information thereof with all reasonable despatch to a peace officer, or use other reasonable endeavours to prevent the commission of the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say person wey di court don try for any crime wey dis Chapter define, and find guilty or not guilty, dem no fit prosecute am again for di same facts for treason, or for no giving information with all reasonable speed to peace officer, or no use other reasonable effort to stop am, when e sabi say person wan commit treason.

sections.title: Unlawful drilling
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) without the permission of the President or of the Governor of the State concerned trains or drills any other person to the use of arms or the practice of military exercise, movements, or evolutions; or [L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
(b) is present at any meeting or assembly of persons, held without the permission of the President or of the Governor of the State concerned, for the purpose of training or drilling any other persons to the use of arms or the practice of military exercises, movements, or evolutions, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
(2) Any person who at any meeting or assembly held without the permission of the President or of the Governor of the State concerned is trained or drilled to the use of arms or the practice of military exercises, movements, or evolutions or who is present at any such meeting or assembly for the purpose of being so trained or drilled, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
The offender may be arrested without warrant.
(3) A prosecution for any of the offences defined in this section of this Code shall be begun within six months after the offence is committed.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful drilling. Person wey, without permission of di President or di Governor of di State wey concern am, train or drill another person to use arms or do military exercises, or dey present for meeting wey dem hold without such permission to train or drill people so, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Person wey dem train or drill so for such meeting, or dey present to dey trained, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. For dis misdemeanour, police fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). Dem must start case for any of dis crimes within 6 months after di crime happen.

sections.title: Power to prohibit importation of publications
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text:
(1) If the appropriate Minister is of opinion that the importation of any publication or series of publications would be contrary to the public interest, he may by order prohibit the importation of such publication or series of publications. [L.N. 258 of 1959. 1967 No. 27.]
(2) If the appropriate Minister is of opinion that it would be in the public interest to do so, he may by order prohibit the importation of all publications published by or on behalf of any organisation or association of persons specified in the order.
(3) An order made under the provisions of subsection (1) of this section shall, unless a contrary intention is expressed therein, have effect-
(a) with respect to all subsequent issues of such publication; and
