(b) not only with respect to any publication under the name specified in relation thereto in the order, but also with respect to any publication published under any other name if the publishing thereof is in any respect in continuation of, or in substitution for, the publishing of the publication named in the order.
(4) An order under the provisions of subsection (2) of this section shall, unless a contrary intention is expressed therein, have effect not only with respect to all publications published by or on behalf of the organisation or association of persons named therein before the date of the order, but also with respect to all publications so published on or after such date.
(5) An order made under the provisions of subsection (1) or subsection (2) of this section shall, unless a contrary intention is expressed therein, apply to any translation into any language whatsoever of the publication specified in the order.
Offences
(6) Any person who imports, publishes, sells, offers for sale, distributes or reproduces any publication, the importation of which has been prohibited under subsection (1) or (2) of this section, or any extract therefrom, is guilty of an offence and liable, on conviction, for a first offence to imprisonment for two years or to a fine of two hundred naira or to both such imprisonment and fine and for a subsequent offence to imprisonment for three years; and such publication or extract therefrom shall be forfeited to the State. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(7) Any person who without lawful excuse has in his possession any publication, the importation of which has been prohibited under subsection (1) or (2) of this section, or any extract therefrom, is guilty of an offence and liable, on conviction, for a first offence to imprisonment for one year or to a fine of one hundred naira or to both such imprisonment and fine, and for a subsequent offence to imprisonment for two years; and such publication or extract therefrom shall be forfeited to the State.
Delivery of prohibited publication to police and administrative officers
(8) (a) Any person to whom any publication, the importation of which has been prohibited under subsection (1) or (2) of this section, or any extract therefrom, is sent without his knowledge or privity or in response to a request made before the prohibition of the importation of such publication came into effect, or who has such a publication or extract therefrom in his possession at the time when the prohibition of its importation comes into effect, shall forthwith if, or as soon as, the nature of its contents has become known to him, or in the case of a publication or extract therefrom coming into the possession of such person before an order prohibiting its importation has been made, forthwith upon the coming into effect of an order prohibiting the importation of such publication, deliver such publication or extract therefrom to the officer in charge of the nearest police station or to the nearest administrative officer, and in default thereof shall be guilty of an offence and liable, on conviction, to imprisonment for one year or to a fine of one hundred naira or to both such imprisonment and fine; and such publication or extract therefrom shall be forfeited to the State. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(b) A person who complies with the provisions of paragraph (a) of this subsection or is convicted of an offence under that subsection shall not be liable to be convicted for having imported or having in his possession the same publication or extract therefrom.
Power to examine packages
(9) (a) Any of the following officers, that is to say- [1966 No. 84. 1967 No. 27.]
(i) any officer of the Nigerian Postal Service not below the rank of Assistant Surveyor;
(ii) any officer of the Nigeria Customs Service not below the rank of Collector;
(iii) any police officer not below the rank of Assistant Superintendent of Police;
(iv) any other official authorised in that behalf by the President, may detain, open and examine any package or article which he suspects to contain any publication or extract therefrom which it is an offence under the provisions of subsection (6) to import, publish, sell, offer for sale, distribute, reproduce or possess, and during such examination may detain any person importing, distributing, or posting such package or article or in whose possession such package or article is found.
(b) If any such publication or extract therefrom is found in such package or article, the whole package or article may be impounded and retained by the officer and the person importing, distributing, or posting it, or in whose possession it is found, may forthwith be arrested and proceeded against for the commission of an offence under subsection (6) or (8), as the case may be.
sections.pidgin: Dis section give di appropriate Minister power to ban di import of any publication, or all publications from any organisation wey e name, if e believe say e go be for public interest. Di ban cover later issues and translations. If person import, publish, sell, distribute or reproduce banned publication, e don commit crime. First time, di punishment na prison for 2 years, or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200, or both. Later time, na prison for 3 years. If person get am without authority wey di law give am, first time na prison for 1 year, or fine of ₦100, or both; later time na prison for 2 years. Person wey get banned publication must give am to police or administrative officer, or e go face prison for 1 year, or fine of ₦100, or both. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Publication of false news with intent to cause fear and alarm to the public
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text:
(1) Any person who publishes or reproduces any statement, rumour or report which is likely to cause fear and alarm to the public or to disturb the public peace, knowing or having reason to believe that such statement, rumour or report is false, is guilty of a misdemeanour and liable on conviction to imprisonment for three years.
(2) It shall be no defence to a charge under subsection (1) of this section that he did not know or did not have reason to believe that the statement, rumour or report was false unless he proves that, prior to publication, he took reasonable measures to verify the accuracy of such statement, rumour or report.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false news. Person wey publish or reproduce statement, rumour or report wey fit cause fear and alarm to di public or disturb public peace, as e sabi say or get reason to believe say e false, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. E no be defence (reason wey di law accept) say di person no know or no get reason to believe say e false, except e prove say before e publish am, e take reasonable steps to check say e correct.

sections.title: Defamation of persons exercising sovereign authority over a State
sections.chapter: Chapter 7: Sedition and the importation of seditious or undesirable publications
sections.text: Any person who, without such justification or excuse as would be sufficient in the case of the defamation of a private person, publishes anything intended to be read, or any sign or visible representation, tending to expose to hatred or contempt in the estimation of the people of any foreign State any person exercising sovereign authority over that State, is guilty of a misdemeanour, and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defamation of person wey get sovereign authority over foreign State. Person wey, without justification or excuse wey go reach for defamation of private person, publish anything wey dem mean to read, or any sign or visible representation, wey fit make people of dat foreign State hate or look down on such person don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Interference with executive or legislative power
sections.chapter: Chapter 8: Offences against the executive and legislative power
sections.text:
Any person who advisedly does any unlawful act calculated to interfere with the free exercise by the President or a Governor of the duties or authority of his office or with the free exercise by a member of the Federal Executive Council, or a State Executive Council of his duties as such member, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for three years. [L.N. 2 of 1960. L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.] The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
A prosecution for an offence under this section shall not be instituted except by or with the consent of a law officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about interference with executive or legislative power. Person wey on purpose do any act for wrong way (against di law) wey fit disturb di President or Governor from di free use of di duties or authority of im office, or disturb member of di Federal Executive Council or State Executive Council from di free use of im duties as member, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). Dem no fit start case for dis crime except law officer start am or agree.

sections.title: Definition of society and unlawful society
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text:
(1) A society includes any combination of ten or more persons whether the society be known by any name or not. [L.N. 258 of 1959. 1967 No. 27.]
(2) A society is an unlawful society-
(i) if formed for any of the following purposes-
(a) levying war or encouraging or assisting any person to levy war on the Government or the inhabitants of any part of Nigeria; or
(b) killing or injuring or encouraging the killing or injuring of any person; or
(c) destroying or injuring or encouraging the destruction or injuring of any property; or
(d) subverting or promoting the subversion of the Government or of its officials; or
(e) committing or inciting to acts of violence or intimidation; or
(f) interfering with, or resisting, or encouraging interference with or resistance to the administration of the law; or
(g) disturbing or encouraging the disturbance of peace and order in any part of Nigeria; or
(ii) if declared by an order of the President to be a society dangerous to the good government of Nigeria or of any part thereof.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk wetin society and unlawful society mean. Society na any group of 10 or more people, whether e get name or no. Society na unlawful society if dem form am to levy war or help person levy war against di Government or people of any part of Nigeria; kill or injure person or encourage am; destroy or injure property or encourage am; subvert di Government or im officials; commit or push to violence or intimidation; interfere with or resist administration of di law; or disturb peace and order for any part of Nigeria. E also be unlawful society if di President declare by order say e dangerous to di good government of Nigeria or any part of am.

sections.title: Unlawful societies in a State
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text: Without prejudice to the provisions of section 62 of this Code, a society is an unlawful society if it is declared by an order of the President to be a society dangerous to the good government of Nigeria or of any part thereof, and for such purpose the consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation referred to in section 65 of this Code shall be construed as a reference to the consent of the Attorney-General of the State. [L.N. 148 of 1959. L.N. 22 of 1960.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section say, without touching section 62 of dis Code, society na unlawful society if di President declare by order say e dangerous to di good government of Nigeria or any part of am. For dis purpose, di Attorney-General of di Federation wey section 65 of dis Code mention go mean di Attorney-General of di State.

sections.title: Managing an unlawful society
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text: Any person who manages or assists in the management of an unlawful society is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about managing an unlawful society. If person manage or help manage unlawful society, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Members of unlawful society: persons permitting an unlawful society to meet on their premises
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) is a member of an unlawful society; or
(b) knowingly allows a meeting of an unlawful society, or of members of an unlawful society, to be held in any house, building, or place belonging to, or occupied by, him or over which he has control, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about members of unlawful society and place wey dem hold meeting. If person be member of unlawful society, or as e sabi say allow meeting of unlawful society, or of im members, hold for any house, building or place wey belong to am, wey im dey occupy or wey e control, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Provisions relating to prosecution for offences under sections 63 and 64
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text:
(1) A prosecution for an offence under the two last preceding sections shall not be instituted except with the consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation: [L.N. 148 of 1959.] Provided that a person charged with such an offence may be arrested or a warrant for his arrest may be issued and executed, and any such person may be remanded in custody or on bail, notwithstanding that the consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation to the institution of a prosecution for the offence has not been obtained, but no further or other proceedings shall be taken until that consent has been obtained.
(2) In any prosecution for an offence under sections 63 and 64 of this Code it shall not be necessary to prove that the society consisted of ten or more members; but it shall be sufficient to prove the existence of a combination of persons, and the onus shall then rest with the accused to prove that the number of members of such combination did not amount to ten.
(3) Any person who attends a meeting of an unlawful society shall be presumed, until and unless the contrary is proved, to be a member of the society.
(4) Any person who has in his possession or custody or under his control any of the insignia, banners, arms, books, papers, documents, or other property belonging to an unlawful society, or wears any of the insignia or is marked with any mark of the society, shall be presumed, unless and until the contrary is proved, to be a member of the society.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about how dem go prosecute crimes under sections 63 and 64. Dem no fit start case without agreement of di Attorney-General of di Federation. But dem fit arrest di person, issue and carry out arrest warrant, and remand am for custody or on bail before di agreement, but no other proceedings go happen until dem get am. Dem no need prove say di society get 10 or more members; e dey enough to prove say group of people dey, and di accused go prove say dem no reach 10. Person wey attend meeting of unlawful society, or get or control im insignia, banners, arms, books, papers, documents or other property, or wear im insignia or get im mark on am, dem go presume say e be member, until e prove another thing.

sections.title: Powers of peace officers in relation to unlawful societies
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text: Any peace officer, and any officer authorised in writing by a peace officer, may enter with or without assistance any house or building or into any place in which he has reason to believe that a meeting of an unlawful society, or of persons who are members of an unlawful society, is being held, and to arrest or cause to be arrested all persons found therein and to search such house, building, or place, and seize or cause to be seized all insignia, banners, arms, books, papers, documents and other property which he may have reasonable cause to believe to belong to any unlawful society or to be in any way connected with the purpose of the meeting.
sections.pidgin: Dis section give power to peace officer, or officer wey peace officer authorise in writing, to enter, with or without help, any house, building or place wey e get reason to believe say meeting of unlawful society dey happen. E fit arrest all person wey e see there, search di place, and seize insignia, banners, arms, books, papers, documents and other property wey e get reasonable cause to believe say belong to unlawful society or connect to di purpose of di meeting.

sections.title: Disposition of property of society declared to be an unlawful society
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk wetin go happen when di President declare by order say society na unlawful society. Di society property for Nigeria go pass quick to officer wey di President appoint. Di officer go wind up di society affairs, pay all debts, liabilities and costs, and if money remain, e go prepare scheme and send am to di President for how to use am. Di President fit change di scheme, and e approve am by signed memorandum; di remaining assets go dey held as di scheme talk. For di winding up, di officer get di powers wey magistrate get to find and sell debtor property. Di President fit suspend dis section for any time wey e see fit so dat society fit wind up im own affairs. Dis no cover property wey dem seize under section 66 of dis Code.

sections.title: Forfeiture
sections.chapter: Chapter 9: Unlawful societies
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of section 67 of this Code, the insignia, banners, arms, books, papers, documents and other property belonging to an unlawful society shall be forfeited to the State and shall be dealt with in such manner as the President may direct. [L.N. 257 of 1959. L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section say, subject to section 67 of dis Code, di insignia, banners, arms, books, papers, documents and other property of unlawful society go pass to di State, and dem go handle am as di President direct.

sections.title: Definitions: Unlawful assembly. Riot
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text:
When three or more persons, with intent to carry out some common purpose, assemble in such a manner or, being assembled, conduct themselves in such a manner as to cause persons in the neighbourhood to fear on reasonable grounds that the persons so assembled will tumultuously disturb the peace, or will by such assembly needlessly and without any reasonable occasion provoke other persons tumultuously to disturb the peace, they are an unlawful assembly.
It is immaterial that the original assembling was lawful if, being assembled; they conduct themselves with a common purpose in such a manner as aforesaid.
An assembly of three or more persons who assemble for the purpose of protecting any house against persons threatening to break and enter the house in order to commit a felony or misdemeanour therein is not an unlawful assembly.
When an unlawful assembly has begun to act in so tumultuous a manner as to disturb the peace, the assembly is called a riot, and the persons assembled are said to be riotously assembled.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain unlawful assembly and riot. 3 or more people wey gather to do common purpose, and gather or behave so dat people for di area fit reasonably fear say dem go disturb di peace with noise and violence, or say dem go, without reason, push other people to do so, na unlawful assembly. E no matter if di gathering start well, if dem behave so after dem don gather with common purpose. Gathering of 3 or more people to protect house from people wey wan break in to commit felony (serious crime) or misdemeanour (small crime) no be unlawful assembly. When unlawful assembly start to act so disturb di peace, dem call am riot, and di people na riotously assembled.

sections.title: Punishment of unlawful assembly
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who takes part in an unlawful assembly is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful assembly. Person wey take part for unlawful assembly don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Punishment of riot
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who takes part in a riot is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about riot. Person wey take part for riot don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Making proclamation for rioters to disperse
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any magistrate or, in his absence, any police officer, of or above the rank of assistant superintendent, or any commissioned officer in the Naval, Military or Air Forces of Nigeria in whose view a riot is being committed, or who apprehends that a riot is about to be committed by persons assembled within his view, may make or cause to be made a proclamation in the name of the Federal Republic in such form as he thinks fit, commanding the rioters or persons so assembled to disperse peaceably. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about order for rioters to disperse. Any magistrate or, if e no dey, any police officer wey be assistant superintendent or above, or any commissioned officer for di Naval, Military or Air Forces of Nigeria, wey see riot dey happen or fear say e wan happen among people wey gather for im view, fit make proclamation, or cause make dem make am, for di name of di Federal Republic, for any form wey e see fit. Di proclamation go command di rioters or di people wey gather to disperse peaceably.

sections.title: Dispersion of rioters after proclamation made
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: If upon the expiration of a reasonable time after such proclamation is made, or after the making of such proclamation has been prevented by force, twelve or more persons continue riotously assembled together, any person authorised to make proclamation, or any police officer, or any other person acting in aid of such person or police officer, may do all things necessary for dispersing the persons so continuing assembled, or for apprehending them or any of them, and, if any person makes resistance, may use all such force as is reasonably necessary for overcoming such resistance, and shall not be liable in any criminal or civil proceeding for having, by the use of such force, caused harm or death to any person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk wetin dem fit do after dem make proclamation. If after reasonable time, or after force stop dem from making di proclamation, 12 or more people still dey riotously gathered, any person wey fit make di proclamation, any police officer, or person wey dey help dem fit do all things wey need to disperse or arrest di people. If person resist, dem fit use all force wey reasonably need to overcome am. Dem no go face criminal or civil proceeding for causing harm or death to any person by dat force.

sections.title: Rioting after proclamation
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: If proclamation is made, commanding the persons engaged in a riot, or assembled with the purpose of committing a riot, to disperse, every person who, at or after the expiration of a reasonable time from the making of such proclamation, takes or continues to take part in the riot or assembly is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about rioting after proclamation. If dem make proclamation to command people wey dey riot, or gather to riot, to disperse, any person wey take part or continue to take part for di riot or gathering when reasonable time don pass don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 5 years.

sections.title: Preventing or obstructing the making of proclamation
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who forcibly prevents or obstructs the making of such proclamation as is in section 75 of this Code, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for ten years; and if the making of the proclamation is so prevented, every person who, knowing that it has been so prevented, takes or continues to take part in the riot or assembly is liable to imprisonment for five years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping or blocking di proclamation. Person wey use force to stop or block di proclamation wey section 75 of dis Code mention don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 10 years. If dem stop di proclamation so, every person wey sabi say dem don stop am and take part or continue to take part for di riot or gathering go face prison for 5 years.

sections.title: Rioters demolishing buildings, machinery, railway, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any persons who, being riotously assembled together, unlawfully pull down or destroy, or begin to pull down or destroy any building, railway, machinery or structures are guilty of a felony and each of them is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about rioters wey pull down or destroy buildings, railway, machinery or structures. People wey riotously gather and for wrong way (against di law) pull down or destroy, or begin to pull down or destroy, any building, railway, machinery or structure don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment for each of dem na prison for life.

sections.title: Rioters injuring buildings, machinery, railway, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any persons who, being riotously assembled together, unlawfully damage any of the things in section 77 of this Code, are guilty of a felony and each of them is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about rioters wey damage buildings, railway, machinery or structures. People wey riotously gather and for wrong way (against di law) damage any of di things wey section 77 of dis Code mention don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment for each of dem na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Smuggling or rescuing goods under arms
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about smuggling or rescuing goods under arms. 3 or more people wey gather with firearms, bows and arrows, spears, swords, knives, or other dangerous or offensive weapons to do or help do any of dis don commit felony (serious crime): load, unload, move or carry away, for wrong way (against di law), goods wey dem ban from import or wey customs duties never pay or secure; rescue or take such goods from person wey get authority to seize dem, or from im helper or di place wey e put dem; rescue person wey dem arrest for customs crime; or stop arrest of person wey commit such crime or wey help do any of dis. Di punishment for each of dem na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Smuggling under arms or in disguise
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any persons who are found assembled together, to the number of six or more, having with them any goods liable to forfeiture under any law relating to the customs, and carrying firearms, bows and arrows, spears, swords, knives, or other dangerous or offensive weapons, or disguised, are guilty of a felony and each of them is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about smuggling under arms or in disguise. 6 or more people wey dem see gather together with goods wey fit forfeit under any customs law, and dey carry firearms, bows and arrows, spears, swords, knives, or other dangerous or offensive weapons, or dey disguise, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment for each of dem na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Going armed so as to cause fear
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who goes armed in public without lawful occasion in such a manner as to cause terror to any person is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years and his arms may be forfeited.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about going armed to cause fear. Person wey carry arms for public, without di law allow am, for way wey cause terror to any person, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years, and dem fit forfeit im arms.

sections.title: Forcible entry
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text:
Any person who, in a manner likely to cause a breach of the peace or reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace, enters on land which is in actual and peaceable possession of another, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
It is immaterial whether he is entitled to enter on the land or not.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about forcible entry. Person wey enter land wey another person dey actually and peacefully possess, for way wey fit cause breach of di peace or reasonable fear of am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. E no matter whether di person get right to enter di land or no.

sections.title: Forcible detainer
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who, being in actual possession of land without colour of right, holds possession of it, in a manner likely to cause a breach of the peace or reasonable apprehension of a breach of the peace, against a person entitled by law to the possession of the land, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about forcible detainer. Person wey dey actually possess land without any right and hold am for way wey fit cause breach of di peace or reasonable fear of am, against person wey di law give right to di land, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Affray
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who takes part in a fight in a public place is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about affray. Person wey take part for fight for public place don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Challenge to fight a duel
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who challenges another to fight a duel, or attempts to provoke another to fight a duel, or attempts to provoke any person to challenge another to fight a duel, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about challenge to fight duel. Person wey challenge another person to fight duel, or try to provoke person to fight duel, or try to provoke person to challenge another to fight duel, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Prize fight
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any person who fights in a prize fight, or subscribes to or promotes a prize fight, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about prize fight. Person wey fight for prize fight, or contribute to am, or promote am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Threatening violence
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) with intent to intimidate or annoy any person, threatens to break or injure a dwelling-house; or
(2) with intent to alarm any person in a dwelling-house, discharges loaded firearms or commits any other breach of the peace, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
If the offence is committed in the night the offender is guilty of a felony and IS liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about threatening violence. Person wey wan scare or annoy person and threaten to break or injure dwelling-house, or wey wan alarm person wey dey dwelling-house and fire loaded firearms or commit any other breach of di peace, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. But if di person do am for night, e don commit felony (serious crime) and go face prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Assembling for the purpose of smuggling
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text: Any persons who assemble together, to the number of three or more, for the purpose of unshipping, carrying or concealing, any goods subject to customs duty and liable to forfeiture under any law relating to the customs, are guilty of a misdemeanour and each of them is liable to a fine not exceeding two hundred naira or to imprisonment for six months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about assembling to smuggle. 3 or more people wey gather to unload, carry or hide goods wey get customs duty and fit forfeit under any customs law don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment for each of dem na fine (money wey person go pay) wey no pass ₦200, or prison for 6 months.

sections.title: Unlawful processions
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text:
(1) Any persons who assemble together, to the number of three or more, under any of the following circumstances-
(a) bearing or wearing or having amongst them any firearms, bows and arrows, spear, sword, knife, or other offensive weapon; or
(b) publicly exhibiting any banner, emblem, flag, or symbol, the displaying of which is calculated to promote animosity between persons of different religious faiths or different factions; or
(c) being accompanied by any music, beating of drums, or other noise calculated to promote such animosity, and, being so assembled, join in any parade or procession for the purpose of celebrating or commemorating any festival, anniversary, or event relating to or connected with any religious or other distinction or difference between persons residing in Nigeria or of demonstrating any such religious or other distinction or difference, are guilty of an offence and each of them is liable to imprisonment for one month.
If the offender is himself bearing or wearing firearms, a bow and arrows, spear, sword, knife or any other offensive weapon he is liable to imprisonment for six months.
(2) When three or more persons are so assembled together it is the duty of a peace officer to make or cause to be made a command in the name of the President, in such words as he thinks fit, to the persons assembled to disperse peaceably.
Any persons who, being so assembled, continue together to the number of three or more, and do not disperse themselves within the space of a quarter of an hour after the giving of the command, are guilty of an offence and each of them is liable to imprisonment for three years.
(3) A judicial officer may issue a warrant in the first instance for the arrest of any such offender, either on the oath of a credible person or on his own view.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful processions. 3 or more people wey gather and carry or wear firearms or other offensive weapon; or show banner, emblem, flag or symbol wey fit cause animosity between people of different religious faiths or factions; or dey with music, drumbeat or noise wey fit cause such animosity, and join parade or procession to celebrate or show religious or other difference between people for Nigeria, don commit crime. Di punishment for each na prison for 1 month, or 6 months if di person carry or wear di weapon imself. Peace officer must command dem for di name of di President to disperse peaceably. Any of dem wey remain 3 or more and no disperse within quarter of an hour go face prison for 3 years. Judicial officer fit issue arrest warrant first. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Provoking breach of peace by offensive publication
sections.chapter: Chapter 10: Unlawful assemblies: breaches of the peace
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) in any manner or form publishes or displays or offers to the public the pictorial representation of any person living or dead in a manner likely to provoke any section of the community; or [1966 No. 44.]
(b) publishes or circulates publications either in the form of newspapers, or leaflets, periodicals, pamphlets or posters, if such publications are likely to provoke or bring into disaffection any section of the community; or
(c) sings songs, plays any instrument or recording of sounds, or sells, lends, or lets on hire any record of sounds, the words of which are likely to provoke any section of the community, is guilty of an offence for which he may be arrested without warrant by any police officer or member of the armed forces in uniform, and upon conviction is liable to a fine of one hundred naira or to imprisonment for a term of three months, or to both such fine and imprisonment; and the court convicting may order confiscation of any material (including records) used for purposes contemplated by this section and of any instrument used in connection therewith.
(2) Where any person is subsequently convicted of the like or any other offence under this section of this Code, the penalty shall be the maximum prescribed for the offence.
(3) It shall be a defence to any person charged under this section of this Code with selling, lending or letting on hire of any record that after reasonable inquiry was made by him before the sale, lending or hiring out as the case may be, (the proof of which inquiry shall lie upon the person charged with the offence), he was unaware of the possibility that it might be used for purposes mentioned in subsection (1) of this Code, and thereafter withdrew the record from sale or recalled any record lent or hired out by him.
(4) This section of this Code shall have effect notwithstanding any other penalty which may be prescribed for an offence of a similar nature in any criminal code or penal code in force in Nigeria.
Interpretation
(5) In this section, unless the context otherwise requires-
"pictorial representation" includes any photograph, and any plate or film, positive or negative;
"recorded" means sounds collected or stored by means of any tape, disc, cylinder or other means whatsoever where the sounds are capable of being reproduced or are intended for reproduction by electrical or mechanical means at any time or from time to time thereafter, and includes the matrix,and cognate expressions shall have the like meaning; "sounds" includes speech and mere noise.
Part 3 OFFENCES AGAINST THE ADMINISTRATION OF LAW AND JUSTICE AND AGAINST PUBLIC AUTHORITY
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about provoking breach of peace by offensive publication. Person wey show or offer to di public picture of any person, publish or circulate newspapers, leaflets, pamphlets or posters, or sing songs, play or sell recordings, wey fit provoke any section of di community, don commit crime. Police officer or uniformed member of di armed forces fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100, or prison for 3 months, or both, and di court fit confiscate di materials. If e commit di crime again, e go get di maximum. Dis section work even if another law set another penalty. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept) for person wey sell, lend or hire record: e must prove say e make reasonable inquiry, no know say dem fit use am so, and withdraw or recall am.

sections.title: Disclosure of official secrets
sections.chapter: Chapter 11: Disclosure of official secrets and abstracting document
sections.text:
(1) Any person who, being employed in the public service, publishes or communicates any fact which comes to his knowledge by virtue of his office, and which it is his duty to keep secret, or any document which comes to his possession by virtue of his office and which it is his duty to keep secret, except to some person to whom he is bound to publish or communicate it, is guilty of a misdemeanour, and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
Public servant abstracting, etc., documents
(2) Any person who, being employed in the public service, without proper authority abstracts, or makes a copy of, any document the property of his employer is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
Restriction on prosecutions
(3) A prosecution for an offence under the provisions of this section of this Code shall not be commenced except by, or with the consent of, a law officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about disclosing official secrets. Person wey dey work for public service and publish or tell any fact or document wey e get because of im office and wey im duty na to keep secret, except to person wey e must tell, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Person wey dey work for public service and, without proper authority, take away or copy any document wey belong to im employer don also commit misdemeanour. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Dem no fit start case except law officer start am or agree.

sections.title: Official corruption: public official inviting bribes, etc., on account of own actions
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
(1) Any public official (as defined in section 98D) who-
(a) corruptly asks for, receives or obtains any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person; or [1966 No. 84.]
(b) corruptly agrees or attempts to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person, on account of-
(i) anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person, by himself in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs or business of a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which he is serving as a public official; or
(ii) anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour; or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person, by himself in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any such matter as aforesaid, is guilty of the felony of official corruption and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
(2) If in any proceedings for an offence under this section of this Code it is proved that any property or benefit of any kind, or any promise thereof, was received by a public official, or by some other person at the instance of a public official, from a person-
(a) holding, or seeking to obtain, a contract, licence or permit from a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which that public official is serving as such; or
(b) concerned, or likely to be concerned, in any proceeding or business transacted, pending or likely to be transacted before or by that public official or a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which that public official is serving as such, or by or from any person acting on behalf of or related to such a person, the property, benefit or promise shall, unless the contrary is proved, be deemed to have been received corruptly on account of such a past or future act, omission, favour or disfavour as is mentioned in subsection (1) (i) or (ii) of this section.
(3) In any proceedings for an offence under this section to which subsection (1) (ii) of this section is relevant it shall not be a defence to show that the accused-
(a) did not subsequently do, make or show the act, omission, favour or disfavour in question; or
(b) never intended to do, make or show it.
(4) Without prejudice to subsection (3) of this section, where a police officer or other public official whose official duties include the prosecution, detention or punishment of offenders, is charged with an offence under this section of this Code in connection with-
(a) the arrest, detention or prosecution of any person for an alleged offence; or
(b) an omission to arrest, detain or prosecute any person for an alleged offence; or
(c) the investigation of an alleged offence, it shall not be necessary to prove that the accused believed that the offence mentioned in paragraph (a),
(b) or (c) of subsection (4) of this section, or any other offence, had been committed.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about public official (as section 98D define) wey take bribe because of im own actions. If e corruptly ask for, receive or get property or benefit for imself or another person, or corruptly agree or try to do so, because of wetin e don do or go do, or favour e don show or go show, e don commit di felony (serious crime) of official corruption. Di punishment na prison for 7 years. If person wey get or want contract, licence or permit from im office, or get matter before am, give di property or promise, di court go presume say dem give am corruptly, until e prove another thing. E no be defence (reason wey di law accept) say di official no do di thing later. For police officer or official wey prosecute or punish offenders, dem no need prove say e believe say crime happen.

sections.title: Official corruption: person giving bribes, etc., on account of actions of public official
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
(1) Any person who- [1966 No. 84.]
(a) corruptly gives, confers or procures any property or benefit of any kind to, on or for a public official (as defined in section 98D) or to, on or for any other person; or
(b) corruptly promises or offers to give or confer or to procure or attempt to procure any property or benefit of any kind to, on or for a public official or to, on or for any other person, on account of any such act, omission, favour or disfavour on the part of the public official as is mentioned in section 98 (1) (i) or (ii) of this Code, is guilty of the felony of official corruption and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
(2) If in any proceedings for an offence under this section of this Code it is proved that any property or benefit of any kind, or any promise thereof, was given to a public official, or to some other person at the instance of a public official, by a person-
(a) holding, or seeking to obtain, a contract, licence or permit from a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which that public official is serving as such; or
(b) concerned, or likely to be concerned, in any proceeding or business transacted, pending or likely to be transacted before or by that public official or a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which that public official is serving as such, or by or from any person acting on behalf of or related to such a person, the property, benefit, or promise shall, unless the contrary is proved, be deemed to have been given corruptly on account of such a past or future act, omission, favour or disfavour as is mentioned in section 98 (1) (i) or (ii) of this Code.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey give bribe because of actions of public official. Person wey corruptly give, confer or procure, or promise or offer to give, property or benefit of any kind to or for public official (as section 98D define) or another person, because of any act, omission, favour or disfavour wey section 98 (1) (i) or (ii) of dis Code mention, don commit di felony (serious crime) of official corruption. Di punishment na prison for 7 years. If person wey get or want contract, licence or permit from official office, or get matter before am, give di property or promise, di court go presume say e give am corruptly, until e prove another thing.

sections.title: Official corruption: person inviting bribes, etc., on account of actions of public official
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
(1) Any person who- [1966 No. 84.]
(a) corruptly asks for, receives or obtains any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person; or
(b) corruptly agrees or attempts to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person, on account of-
(i) anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person, by a public official (as defined in section 98D of this Code) in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs or business of a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which the public official is serving as such; or
(ii) anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person, by a public official in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any such matter as aforesaid, is guilty of the felony of official corruption and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
(2) In any proceedings for an offence under this section of this Code it shall not be necessary to prove-
(a) that any public official counselled the commission of the offence; or
(b) that in the course of committing the offence the accused mentioned any particular public official; or
(c) that (in a case to which subsection (1) (ii) of this section is relevant) the accused believed that any public official would do, make or show the act, omission, favour or disfavour in question; or
(d) that the accused intended to give the property or benefit in question, or any part thereof, to a public official.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey ask for bribe because of actions of public official. Person wey corruptly ask for, receive or get property or benefit for imself or another person, or corruptly agree or try to do so, because of wetin public official (as section 98D define) don do or no do, or go do or no do later, don commit di felony (serious crime) of official corruption. Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Dem no need prove say any public official counsel di crime, say di accused mention any particular official, say e believe say official go do di thing, or say e wan give di property or benefit to public official.

sections.title: Restrictions on arrest and prosecution of judicial officers for offences under sections 98 to 98B
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about arrest and prosecution of judicial officer for crimes under sections 98 to 98B. Police no fit arrest judicial officer without court paper (warrant) for dem. Dem no fit start case against judicial officer except by complaint or information wey di Attorney-General of di Federation, or di Attorney-General of di State where di crime happen, sign or wey dem sign for am. For dis section, judicial officer include, apart from wetin section 1 (i) of dis Code talk, member of customary court or juvenile court; arbitrator, umpire or referee; assessor; member of jury; member of tribunal of inquiry under di Tribunals of Inquiry Act; and any person wey fit take evidence on oath before am under any law for Nigeria.

sections.title: Meaning of "public official" in sections 98 to 98B
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: In sections 98 to 98B of this Code, "public official" means any person employed in the public service (within the meaning of that expression as defined in section 1 (i) or any judicial officer within the meaning of section 98C of this Code.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin 'public official' mean for sections 98 to 98B. E mean any person wey dey work for di public service, as section 1 (i) define, or any judicial officer as section 98C define.

sections.title: Extortion by public officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: Any person who, being employed in the public service, takes, or accepts from any person, for the performance of his duty as such officer, any reward beyond his proper pay and emoluments, or any promise of such reward, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about extortion by public officers. Person wey dey work for public service and take or accept from any person, for doing im duty, any reward apart from im proper pay and emoluments, or any promise of such reward, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Public officers interested in contracts
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
Any person who, being employed in the public service, knowingly acquires or holds, directly or indirectly, otherwise than as a member of a registered joint stock company consisting of more than twenty persons, a private interest in any contract or agreement which is made on account of the public service with respect to any matter concerning the department of the service in which he is employed, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years and to be fined at the discretion of the court.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about public officers wey get interest for contracts. Person wey dey work for public service and as e sabi say get or hold, directly or indirectly, private interest for any contract or agreement wey dem make for public service about matter wey concern im department, except as member of registered joint stock company wey get more than 20 persons, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years and fine (money wey person go pay) wey di court decide. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Officers charged with administration of property of a special character or with special duties
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: Any person who, being employed in the public service, and being charged by virtue of his employment with any judicial or administrative duties respecting property of a special character, or respecting the carrying on of any manufacture, trade, or business of a special character, and having acquired or holding, directly or indirectly, a private interest in any such property, manufacture, trade, or business, discharges any such duties with respect to the property, manufacture, trade or business in which he has such interest, or with respect to the conduct of any person in relation thereto, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about officers wey handle property or business of special kind. Person wey dey work for public service, and im job give am judicial or administrative duties about property, or about manufacture, trade or business of special kind, and e get or hold, directly or indirectly, private interest for am, but still do dem duties about am or about conduct of any person wey concern am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: False claims by officials
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: Any person who, being employed in the public service in such a capacity as to require him or to enable him to furnish returns or statements touching any sum payable or claimed to be payable to himself or to any other person, or touching any other matter required to be certified for the purpose of any payment of money or delivery of goods to be made to any person, makes a return or statement touching any such matter which is, to his knowledge, false in any material particular, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false claims by officials. Person wey dey work for public service for position wey need or fit make am give returns or statements about any sum wey dem suppose pay or claim say dem suppose pay to imself or another person, or about any other matter wey dem need certify for payment of money or delivery of goods, and make return or statement wey, as e sabi say, false for any material way, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Abuse of office
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
Any person who, being employed in the public service, does or directs to be done in abuse of the authority of his office, any arbitrary act prejudicial to the rights of another, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
If the act is done or directed to be done for purposes of gain he is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
A prosecution for any offence under this or any of the last three preceding sections shall not be instituted except by or with the consent of a law officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about abuse of office. Person wey dey work for public service and, abusing di authority of im office, do or order any arbitrary act wey harm another person right don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. If e do am or order am for gain, e don commit felony (serious crime) and go face prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). Dem no fit start case for dis or any of di last three sections before am except law officer start am or agree.

sections.title: False certificates by public officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: Any person who, being authorised or required by law to give any certificate touching any matter by virtue whereof the rights of any person may be prejudicially affected, gives a certificate which is, to his knowledge, false in any material particular, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false certificates by public officers. Person wey di law authorise or require to give certificate about any matter wey fit harm person rights, and e give certificate wey, as e sabi say, false for any material way, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Administering extra-judicial oaths
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: Any person who administers an oath or takes a solemn declaration or affirmation or affidavit touching any matter with respect to which he has not by law any authority to do so, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year. This section does not apply to an oath, declaration, affirmation, or affidavit, administered or taken before a peace officer in any matter relating to the preservation of the peace or the punishment of offences, or relating to inquiries respecting sudden death; nor to an oath, declaration, affirmation, or affidavit, administered or taken for some purpose which is lawful under the laws of another country, or for the purpose of giving validity to an instrument in writing which is intended to be used in another country.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about administering extra-judicial oaths. Person wey administer oath, or take solemn declaration, affirmation or affidavit about matter wey di law no give am authority to do so don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. But dis section no cover oath, declaration, affirmation or affidavit wey dem administer or take before peace officer about keeping peace or punishing crimes, or about inquiries on sudden death, or wey dem take for purpose wey di laws of another country allow, or to give validity to written document wey dem wan use for another country.

sections.title: False assumption of authority
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) not being a judicial officer, assumes to act as a judicial officer; or
(b) without authority assumes to act as a person having authority by law to administer an oath or take a solemn declaration or affirmation or affidavit, or to do any other act of a public nature which can only be done by persons authorised by law to do so; or
(c) represents himself to be a person authorised by law to sign a document testifying to the contents of any register or record kept by lawful authority, or testifying to any fact or event, and signs such document as being so authorised, when he is not, and knows that he is not, in fact, so authorised, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false assumption of authority. Person wey no be judicial officer but act as judicial officer; or without authority act as person wey di law allow to administer oath or take solemn declaration, affirmation or affidavit, or do any other public act wey only authorised person fit do; or say e dey authorised to sign document wey show wetin dey for register or record wey lawful authority keep, or any fact or event, and sign am, as e sabi say e no get dat authority, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Personating public officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) personates any person employed in the public service on an occasion when the latter is required to do any act or attend in any place by virtue of his employment; or
(2) falsely represents himself to be a person employed in the public service, and assumes to do any act or to attend in any place for the purpose of doing any act by virtue of such employment, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about personating public officers. Person wey pretend to be person wey dey work for public service when di person need to do any act or attend any place because of im work, or falsely say e dey work for public service, and act or go any place to do act because of dat work, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Personating members of armed forces or police
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
Any person who, not being a person serving in the armed forces of Nigeria nor a member of the police forces and with intent that he may be taken to be such a person or member as aforesaid- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(a) wears any part of the uniform of; or
(b) wears any garb resembling any part of the uniform of, a person serving in the armed forces of Nigeria, or a member of the police forces, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about personating members of armed forces or police. Person wey no dey serve for di armed forces of Nigeria and no be police member, and wey, so dat people go take am as one of dem, wear any part of dia uniform or any garb wey resemble any part of am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Unlawfully wearing the uniform of the armed forces
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text:
Any person who- [L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
(1) not being a person serving in any of the armed forces of Nigeria, wears the uniform or any part of the uniform of such forces, or any dress having the appearance or bearing any of the regimental or other distinctive marks of such uniforms; or
(2) not being a person holding any office or authority under the Government of Nigeria or of any part thereof, wears any uniform or distinctive badge or mark or carries any token calculated to convey the impression that such person holds any office or authority under the government, is guilty of an offence and is liable to imprisonment for one month or to a fine of ten naira, unless he proves that he had the permission of the President or of the Governor of a State to wear such uniform or dress, badge or mark or to carry such token:
Provided that this section of this Code shall not apply to the wearing of any uniform or dress in the course of a stage play or in any bona fide public entertainment.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wearing uniform or badge wey person no get right to. Person wey no dey serve for any armed forces of Nigeria and wear dia uniform or any part of am, or dress wey look like am; or wey no hold office or authority under di Government of Nigeria or any part, and wear uniform, badge or mark or carry token wey fit make people think say e hold such office, don commit crime. Di punishment na prison for 1 month or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦10. But e get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di person fit prove say di President or di Governor of a State give am permission. Dis section no cover wearing uniform or dress for stage play or genuine public entertainment.

sections.title: Selling, etc., uniform, etc., to unauthorised persons
sections.chapter: Chapter 12: Corruption and abuse of office
sections.text: Any person who sells or gives any uniform, or part of a uniform, or any dress, badge or mark, as in section 110 of this Code to any person who is not authorised to wear the same, is guilty of an offence and is liable to the penalties prescribed in the said section.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about selling uniform to people wey no get authority. Person wey sell or give any uniform, or part of uniform, or any dress, badge or mark wey section 110 of dis Code talk about to person wey no get authority to wear am don commit crime and go face di penalties wey dat section set.

sections.title: Bargaining for offices in public service
sections.chapter: Chapter 13: Selling and trafficking in offices
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) corruptly asks, receives, or obtains, or agrees or attempts to receive or obtain, any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person on account of anything already done or omitted to be done, or to be afterwards done or omitted to be done, by him or any other person, with regard to the appointment or contemplated appointment of any person to any office or employment in the public service, or with regard to any application by any person for employment in the public service; or
(2) corruptly gives, confers, or procures, or promises or offers to give or confer, or to procure or attempt to procure, to, upon, or for, any person any property or benefit of any kind on account of any such act or omission, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about bargaining for offices for public service. Person wey corruptly ask for, receive or get, or agree or try to receive or get, property or benefit for imself or another person because of wetin im or another person don do or no do, or go do or no do later, about appointment or planned appointment of any person to office or job for public service, or about any application for job for public service; or corruptly give, confer or procure, or promise or offer to give, confer or procure, property or benefit to or for any person because of any such act or omission, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Definition of judicial proceeding
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: In this Chapter, the term "judicial proceeding" includes any proceeding had or taken in or before any court, tribunal, commission of inquiry, or person, in which evidence mayor may not be taken on oath.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin 'judicial proceeding' mean for dis Chapter. E include any proceeding wey dem do for or before any court, tribunal, commission of inquiry or person, whether dem take evidence on oath or no.

sections.title: Perjury
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who, in any judicial proceeding, or for the purpose of instituting any judicial proceeding, knowingly gives false testimony touching any matter which is material to any question then pending in that proceedings, or intended to be raised in that proceeding, is guilty of an offence which is called perjury, It is immaterial whether the testimony is given on oath or under any other sanction authorised by law.
The forms and ceremonies used in administering the oath or in otherwise binding the person giving the testimony to speak the truth are immaterial, if he assent to the forms and ceremonies actually used.
It is immaterial whether the false testimony is given orally or in writing.
It is immaterial whether the court or tribunal is properly constituted, or is held in the proper place, or not, if it actually acts as a court or tribunal in the proceeding in which the testimony is given.
It is immaterial whether the person who gives the testimony is a competent witness or not, or whether the testimony is admissible in the proceeding or not.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about perjury. Person wey, for any judicial proceeding or to start one, as e sabi say give false testimony about matter wey important to any question wey dey pending or wey dem wan raise for di proceeding don commit crime wey dem call perjury. E no matter if dem give di testimony on oath or under another thing wey law authorise; no matter di forms or ceremonies wey dem use to bind person to speak truth, if di person agree to dem; no matter whether e dey spoken or written; no matter if court or tribunal no properly constituted or no dey proper place, if e actually act as court or tribunal; and no matter whether di person na competent witness or di testimony admissible. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Punishment of perjury
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who commits perjury is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
If the offender commits the offence in order to procure the conviction of another person for an offence punishable with death or with imprisonment for life he is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about punishment for perjury. Di punishment na prison for 14 years. But if di person do am to make di court find another person guilty of crime wey death or prison for life dey punish, e go face prison for life.

sections.title: Evidence on charge of perjury
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: A person cannot be convicted of committing perjury, or of counselling or procuring the commission of perjury, upon the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say di court no fit find person guilty of perjury, or of counselling or procuring perjury, only because one witness testify and no other evidence support am.

sections.title: Fabricating evidence
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to mislead any tribunal in any judicial proceeding-
(1) fabricates evidence by any means other than perjury or counselling or procuring the commission of perjury; or
(2) knowingly makes use of such fabricated evidence, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about fabricating evidence. Person wey wan mislead any tribunal for judicial proceeding and fabricate evidence by any means apart from perjury or counselling or procuring perjury, or as e sabi say use such fabricated evidence, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Corruption of witnesses
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) gives, confers, or procures, or promises or offers to give or confer, or to procure or attempt to procure, any property or benefit of any kind to, upon, or for, any person, upon any agreement or understanding that any person called or to be called as a witness in any judicial proceeding shall give false testimony or withhold true testimony; or
(2) attempts by any other means to induce a person called or to be called as a witness in any judicial proceeding to give false testimony or to withhold true testimony; or
(3) asks, receives or obtains, or agrees or attempts to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person, upon any agreement or understanding that any person shall as a witness in any judicial proceeding give false testimony or withhold true testimony, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about corruption of witnesses. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e give, confer or procure, or promise or offer to give, property or benefit to or for any person under agreement say person wey dem call or go call as witness for judicial proceeding go give false testimony or hold back true testimony; or try by other means to push such witness to do so; or ask for, receive or get, or agree or try to get, property or benefit under agreement say any person go give false testimony or hold back true testimony as witness. Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Deceiving witnesses
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who practises any fraud or deceit, or knowingly makes or exhibits any false statement, representation, token, or writing, to any person called or to be called as a witness in any judicial proceeding, with intent to affect the testimony of such person as a witness, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about deceiving witnesses. Person wey use fraud or deceit, or as e sabi say make or show false statement, representation, token or writing, to person wey dem call or go call as witness for judicial proceeding, so dat e go affect im testimony, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Destroying evidence
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who, knowing that any book, document, or other thing of any kind, is or may be required in evidence in a judicial proceeding, wilfully removes, conceals or destroys it or renders it illegible or undecipherable or incapable of identification, with intent thereby to prevent it from being used in evidence, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about destroying evidence. Person wey sabi say book, document or other thing dey required or fit dey required as evidence for judicial proceeding, and on purpose remove, hide or destroy am, or make am no fit read, understand or identify, so dat dem no go use am as evidence, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Preventing witnesses from attending
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: Any person who wilfully prevents or attempts to prevent any person who has been duly summoned to attend as a witness before any court or tribunal from attending as a witness or from producing anything in evidence pursuant to the subpoena or summons, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping witnesses from attending. Person wey on purpose stop or try to stop person wey dem don properly summon to attend as witness before court or tribunal from attending, or from producing anything as evidence as di subpoena or summons talk, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Conspiracy to bring false accusation
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who conspires with another to charge any person or cause any person to be charged with any offence, whether alleged to have been committed in Nigeria or elsewhere, knowing that such person is innocent of the alleged offence or not believing him to be guilty of the alleged offence, is guilty of a felony.
If the offence is such that a person convicted of it is liable to be sentenced to death or to imprisonment for life, the offender is liable to imprisonment for life.
If the offence is such that a person convicted of it is liable to be sentenced to imprisonment, but for a term less than life, the offender is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
In any other case the offender is liable to imprisonment for seven years. The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about plan together to bring false accusation. Person wey plan together with another person to charge any person, or make dem charge any person, with crime, whether e happen for Nigeria or elsewhere, as e sabi say di person no guilty or e no believe say e guilty, don commit felony (serious crime). If di crime na one wey di person fit get death or prison for life, di punishment na prison for life. If na one wey di person fit get prison for less than life, di punishment na prison for 14 years. For any other case, di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Making false statement to public officers with intent
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
(1) Any individual who gives any information which he knows or believes to be false to any person employed in the public service with the intention of causing such person-
(a) to do or omit to do anything which such person ought not to do or ought not to omit to do if the true facts concerning the information given were known to such person; or
