(b) to exercise or use his lawful powers as a person employed in the public service to the injury or annoyance of any other person, is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment for one year.
(2) A prosecution for an offence under this section of this Code shall not be instituted-
(a) without the consent of a superior police officer; or
(b) where in any division an administrative officer has been duly appointed to have charge of the police therein under the provisions of subsection (1) of section 7 of the Police Act, [Cap. P19.] without the consent of that administrative officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about making false statement to public officers. Any individual wey give information wey e sabi or believe say false to person wey dey work for public service, so dat di person go do or no do something wey e no suppose do or no suppose omit if e know di true facts, or use im lawful powers to injure or annoy another person, don commit crime. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Dem no fit start case without agreement of superior police officer, or, where administrative officer don dey duly appointed to handle police for di division under section 7 (1) of di Police Act, without im agreement.

sections.title: Perverting justice
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
(1) Any person who conspires with another to obstruct, prevent, pervert, or defeat the course of justice is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
(2) Any person who attempts, in any way not specially defined in this Code, to obstruct, prevent, pervert, or defeat, the course of justice, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about perverting justice. Person wey plan together with another person to obstruct, prevent, pervert or defeat di course of justice don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). Person wey try, for any way wey dis Code no specially define, to obstruct, prevent, pervert or defeat di course of justice don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Compounding felonies
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who asks, receives, or obtains, or agrees or attempts to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person upon any agreement or understanding that he will compound or conceal a felony, or will abstain from, discontinue, or delay a prosecution for a felony, or will withhold any evidence thereof, is guilty of an offence.
If the felony is such that a person convicted of it is liable to be sentenced to death or imprisonment for life, the offender is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
In any other case the offender is liable to imprisonment for three years. The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about compounding felonies. Person wey ask for, receive or get, or agree or try to get, property or benefit for imself or another person under agreement say e go hide felony (serious crime), or go stop, drop or delay prosecution for felony, or hold back evidence of am, don commit crime. If di felony na one wey di person fit get death or prison for life, e don commit felony and di punishment na prison for 7 years. For any other case, di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Compounding penal actions
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: Any person who, having brought, or under pretence of bringing an action against another person upon a penal Act, law or statute in order to obtain from him a penalty for any offence committed or alleged to have been committed by him, compounds the action without the order or consent of the court in which the action is brought or is to be brought, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about compounding penal actions. Person wey bring, or pretend to bring, action against another person under penal Act, law or statute to get penalty for crime wey e commit or dem say e commit, and settle di action without order or agreement of di court wey dem bring am or go bring am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Advertising a reward for the return of stolen or lost property
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) publicly offers a reward for the return of any property which has been stolen or lost, and in the offer makes use of any words purporting that no question will be asked, or that the person producing such property will not be seized or molested; or
(2) publicly offers to return to any person who may have bought or advanced money by way of loan upon any stolen or lost property the money so paid or advanced, or any other sum of money or reward for the return of such property; or
(3) prints or publishes any such offer, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of one hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about advertising reward for return of stolen or lost property. Person wey publicly offer reward for return of stolen or lost property and use words wey show say dem no go ask question or no go seize or disturb di person wey bring am; or publicly offer to return to person wey buy am or lend money on top am di money wey e pay or lend, or any other money or reward, for return of di property; or print or publish any such offer, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100.

sections.title: Delay to take person arrested before a court
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: Any person who, having arrested another upon a charge of an offence, wilfully delays to take him before a court to be dealt with according to law, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about delay to take arrested person to court. Person wey arrest another person for charge of crime and on purpose delay to take am to court to be dealt with as di law talk don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Bringing fictitious action on penal Act, law or statute
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: Any person who, in the name of a fictitious plaintiff, or in the name of a real person but without his authority, brings an action against another person upon a penal Act, law or statute for the recovery of a penalty for any offence committed or alleged to have been committed by him, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about bringing fictitious action on penal Act, law or statute. Person wey, for name of fictitious plaintiff, or for name of real person without im authority, bring action against another person under penal Act, law or statute to recover penalty for crime wey e commit or dem say e commit don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Inserting advertisement without authority of court
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text: Any person who, without authority, or knowing the advertisement to be false in any material particular inserts or causes it to be inserted in the Federal Gazette, or a State Gazette, or in any newspaper an advertisement purporting to be published under the authority of any court or tribunal, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about inserting advertisement without authority of court. Person wey, without authority, or as e sabi say di advertisement false for any material way, put or cause make dem put for Federal Gazette, State Gazette or any newspaper, advertisement wey say court or tribunal authorise am don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Contempt of court
sections.chapter: Chapter 14: Offences relating to the administration of justice
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) within the premises in which any judicial proceeding is being had or taken, or within the precincts of the same, shows disrespect, in speech, or manner, to or with reference to such proceeding, or any person before whom such proceeding is being had or taken; or
(2) having been called upon to give evidence in a judicial proceeding, fails to attend or, having attended, refuses to be sworn or to make an affirmation, or, having been sworn or affirmed, refuses without lawful excuse to answer a question, or to produce a document, or prevaricates, or remains in the room in which such proceeding is being had or taken, after the witnesses have been ordered to leave such room; or
(3) causes an obstruction or disturbance in the course of a judicial proceeding; or
(4) while a judicial proceeding is pending, makes use of any speech or writing, misrepresenting such proceeding, or capable of prejudicing any person in favour of or against any party to such proceeding, or calculated to lower the authority of any person before whom such proceeding is being had or taken; or
(5) publishes a report of the evidence taken in any judicial proceeding which has been directed to be held in private; or
(6) attempts wrongfully to interfere with or influence a witness in a judicial proceeding, either before or after he has given evidence, in connection with such evidence; or
(7) dismisses a servant because he has given evidence on behalf of a certain party to a judicial proceeding; or
(8) re-takes possession of land from any person who has recently obtained possession by a writ of court; or
(9) commits any other act of intentional disrespect to any judicial proceeding, or to any person before whom such proceeding is being had or taken, is guilty of a simple offence and liable to imprisonment for three months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about contempt of court. Person don commit simple offence (small crime) if e do any of dis: show disrespect by speech or manner for court premises or to di proceeding or person handling am; fail to attend as witness, refuse to swear or affirm, refuse without lawful excuse to answer question or produce document, or remain for room after dem order witnesses to comot; cause obstruction or disturbance; use speech or writing wey misrepresent pending proceeding or fit prejudice person for or against any party; publish evidence from proceeding wey dem order make dem hold for private; try wrongly to influence witness; dismiss servant because e give evidence for one party; retake land from person wey recently get am by writ of court; or do any other intentional act of disrespect. Di punishment na prison for 3 months. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Rescue
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text:
(1) Any person who by force rescues or attempts to rescue from lawful custody any other person-
(a) is, if the last-named person is under a sentence of death or penal servitude or imprisonment for life, or charged with an offence punishable with death, or penal servitude or imprisonment for life, guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life; and
(b) is, in any other case, guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
(2) If the person rescued is in the custody of a private person, the offender must have notice of the fact that the person rescued is in such custody.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about rescue. Person wey use force to rescue or try to rescue another person from lawful custody don commit felony (serious crime). If di rescued person dey under sentence of death or penal servitude or prison for life, or dem charge am for crime wey death or penal servitude or prison for life dey punish, di punishment na prison for life. For any other case, di punishment na prison for 7 years. If di rescued person dey custody of private person, di person wey rescue am must get notice say e dey such custody.

sections.title: Escape
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text:
Any person who, being in lawful custody, escapes from such custody-
(a) is, if he is charged with, or has been convicted of a felony or misdemeanour, guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years, with or without whipping; and
(b) is, in any other case, guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about escape. Person wey dey lawful custody and escape from am don commit crime. If dem charge am with, or di court don find am guilty of, felony (serious crime) or misdemeanour (small crime), di punishment na prison for 7 years, with or without whipping, and e don commit felony. For any other case, e don commit misdemeanour and di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Aiding prisoners to escape
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) aids a prisoner in escaping or attempting to escape from lawful custody; or
(2) conveys anything or causes anything to be conveyed into a prison with intent to facilitate the escape of a prisoner, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about aiding prisoners to escape. Person wey help prisoner to escape or try to escape from lawful custody, or carry or cause make dem carry anything enter prison so dat e go help prisoner escape, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Permitting escape
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text:
Any person who, being an officer of a prison, or a member of a police force, wilfully permits any other person within his lawful custody to escape-
(a) is, if such last-named person is charged with an offence punishable by death, or penal servitude or imprisonment for life, guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years; and
(b) is, in any other case, guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about permitting escape. Prison officer or police member wey on purpose allow person wey dey im lawful custody to escape don commit felony (serious crime). If di person dem charge with crime wey death, or penal servitude or prison for life dey punish, di punishment na prison for 7 years. For any other case, di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Negligently permitting escape
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text: Any person who, being an officer of a prison, or a member of a police force, negligently permits a person within his lawful custody to escape, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about negligently permitting escape. Prison officer or police member wey carelessly allow person wey dey im lawful custody to escape don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Prison officers accessory to breaches of discipline
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text: If any prison officer or person in charge of any convicted prisoner knowingly permits or suffers such prisoner to receive any tobacco, food, money, or other article, or to enter any house, yard, or premises not being the place appointed for the labour of such prisoner he is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for six months and to a fine of one hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about prison officers wey help prisoners break discipline. If prison officer or person wey dey charge of convicted prisoner, as e sabi say, allow or permit di prisoner to receive tobacco, food, money or other article, or to enter any house, yard or premises wey no be place wey dem appoint for di prisoner labour, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 6 months and fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100.

sections.title: Rescuing insane persons
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) rescues any person during his conveyance as an insane person to a hospital, lunatic asylum, or a reception house for the insane or to a house licensed under the laws relating to insane persons for the reception of patients, or to a prison, rescues any person during his confinement as an insane person in any such place; or
(b) being in charge of a person during his conveyance as an insane person to any such place, wilfully permits him to escape from custody; or
(c) being a superintendent of, or person employed in any such place, wilfully permits a person confined therein as an insane person to escape therefrom; or
(d) conceals any such person as aforesaid, who has, to his knowledge, been rescued during such conveyance or confinement, or has, to his knowledge, escaped during such conveyance, or from such confinement, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about rescuing insane persons. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e rescue person while dem dey carry am as insane person go hospital, lunatic asylum, reception house for insane or licensed house for patients, or prison, or rescue person during im confinement as insane person for any such place; if e dey charge of person during conveyance, and on purpose allow am escape; if na superintendent or worker for such place and on purpose allow confined person escape; or if e hide such person wey e sabi say dem don rescue or wey don escape. Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Removing, etc., property under lawful seizure
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text: Any person who, when any property has been attached or taken under the process or authority of any court, knowingly, and with intent to hinder or defeat the attachment or process, receives, removes, retains, conceals, or disposes of such property, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about removing property wey dem seize lawfully. When court don attach or take property under im process or authority, person wey as e sabi say, and wey wan block or defeat di attachment or process, receive, remove, keep, hide or dispose of di property don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Obstructing officers of courts of justice
sections.chapter: Chapter 15: Escapes; rescues; obstructing officers of court
sections.text: Any person who wilfully obstructs or resists any person lawfully charged with the execution of an order or warrant of any court, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year or to a fine of two hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about obstructing officers of courts. Person wey on purpose obstruct or resist person wey di law charge to carry out order or warrant of any court don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.pidgin: Dis section give meaning of words for dis Chapter on coins. E explain 'counterfeit' coin, 'current' coin, 'gold' and 'silver' coin, 'metal', 'nickel coin', 'silver coin' and 'utter'. Counterfeit coin na coin wey no genuine but resemble genuine coin or dem wan make am pass as genuine, and e include genuine coin wey dem prepare or alter to look like higher coin, or wey dem clip, file or reduce and hide am. 'Utter' include to use, deal with or act on di thing as if e genuine, or try to do so. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Counterfeiting gold and silver coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
(1) Any person who makes or begins to make any counterfeit current gold or silver coin is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
(2) Where a person has ten or more unfinished counterfeit coins in his possession the court may presume that he has made them or has been a participant in the act of making them unless he proves the contrary.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about counterfeiting gold and silver coin. Person wey make or begin to make counterfeit current gold or silver coin don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life. If person get 10 or more unfinished counterfeit coins, di court fit presume say e make dem or take part to make dem, unless e prove another thing.

sections.title: Preparation for coining gold and silver coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) gilds or silvers any piece of metal of a fit size or figure to be coined, with intent that it shall be coined into counterfeit gold or silver coin; or
(2) makes any piece of metal into a fit size or figure to facilitate the coining from it of any counterfeit gold or silver coin, with intent that such counterfeit coin shall be made from it; or
(3) without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him-
(a) buys, sells, receives, pays, or disposes of, any counterfeit gold or silver coin at a lower rate than it imports or is apparently intended to import, or offers to do any such thing; or
(b) makes or mends, or begins or prepares to make or mend, or has in his possession, or disposes of, any stamp or mould which is adapted to make the resemblance of both or either of the sides of any gold or silver coin, or any part of either side thereof, knowing the same to be such a stamp or mould or to be so adapted; or
(c) makes or mends, or begins or prepares to make or mend, or has in his possession, or disposes of, any tool, instrument, or machine, which is adapted and intended to be used for marking coin round the edges with marks or figures apparently resembling those on the edges of any gold or silver coin, knowing the same to be so adapted and intended; or
(d) makes or mends, or begins or prepares to make or mend, or has in his possession, or disposes of, any press for coinage, or any tool, instrument, or machine, which is adapted for cutting round blanks out of gold, silver, or other metal, knowing such press, tool, instrument, or machine to have been used or to be intended to be used for making any counterfeit gold or silver coin; or
(e) knowingly conveys out of any mint within the Commonwealth any stamp, mould, tool, instrument, machine, or press, used or employed in coining, or any useful part of any of such thing, or any coin, bullion, or metal, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about preparing to make counterfeit gold and silver coin. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e gild or silver metal piece wey fit coin, or make metal into fit size or shape, wey wan make counterfeit coin from am; or, without lawful authority or excuse (e must prove am), buy, sell, receive, pay or dispose of counterfeit gold or silver coin for lower rate than e show, or offer to; make, mend, begin or prepare to make or mend, keep or dispose of stamp, mould, tool, instrument, machine or press wey fit make coins or counterfeit coins, as e sabi say; or as e sabi say carry out of any mint within di Commonwealth any stamp, mould, tool, instrument, machine, press, coin, bullion or metal wey dem use for coining. Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Unlawful inquiries with the object of making counterfeit coins
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
(1) Any person who without authority or excuse, the proof whereof lies on him, either orally or in writing makes any inquiry of any other person whether such last-mentioned person be in Nigeria or at any place not in Nigeria-
(a) as to obtaining or supplying or as to the cost of obtaining or supplying any machine, stamp, tool, instrument, metal or material which is adapted or is intended to be used-
(i) to make the resemblance of both or either sides of any current coin or any part of either side thereof; or
(ii)
(iii) to mark any coin or disc resembling coin or intended to resemble coin round the edges with marks, figures or letters apparently resembling those on the edges of any current coin; or to cut round blanks out of metal or other substance, knowing such machine, stamp, tool, instrument, metal or material to have been adapted or intended to be used for making any counterfeit coin or for performing any process in the manufacture of counterfeit coin; or
(a) as to making, obtaining or supplying or as to the cost of making, obtaining or supplying any counterfeit coin, is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment for one year.
(2) In the case of written inquiries in connection with any of the matters or subjects to which subsection (1) of this section relates, the fact that such inquiries were reduced into writing shall be sufficient proof of an attempt to commit the offence and the offender shall be subject to a like penalty as if he had committed the offence.
149. Clipping Any person who deals with any current gold or silver coin in such a manner as to diminish its weight with intent that when so dealt with it may pass as current gold or silver coin, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful inquiries to make counterfeit coins. Person wey without authority or excuse (e must prove am), by mouth or writing, ask any person, for Nigeria or outside, about how to get or supply, or di cost of, machine, stamp, tool, instrument, metal or material wey fit make di resemblance of current coin, or mark or cut coin discs, as e sabi say, or about how to make, get or supply counterfeit coin or di cost, don commit crime. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. If di inquiries dey writing, e dey enough as proof say e try to commit di crime, and di person go face di same penalty as if e commit am.

sections.title: Possession of clippings
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully has in his possession or disposes of any filings, or clippings of gold or silver, or any gold or silver in bullion, dust, solution, or any other state, obtained by dealing with current gold or silver coin in such a manner as to diminish its weight, knowing the same to have been so obtained, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about possession of filings or clippings from gold or silver coin. Person wey for wrong way (against di law) get or dispose of filings or clippings of gold or silver, or any gold or silver for any form wey dem get from current gold or silver coin by dealing with am so dat e lose weight, as e sabi say dem get am so, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Uttering counterfeit current gold or silver coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who utters any counterfeit current gold or silver coin knowing it to be counterfeit, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about uttering (using or dealing with) counterfeit current gold or silver coin. Person wey utter counterfeit current gold or silver coin as e sabi say e counterfeit don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Repeated uttering of counterfeit current gold or silver coin, or possession of several such coins
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) utters any counterfeit gold or silver coin, knowing it to be counterfeit, and at the time of such uttering has in his possession any other counterfeit gold or silver coin; or
(b) utters any counterfeit gold or silver coin, knowing it to be counterfeit, and either on the same day or on any of the ten days next ensuing, utters any other counterfeit current gold or silver coin, knowing it to be counterfeit; or
(c) has in his possession three or more pieces of counterfeit current gold or silver coin, knowing them to be counterfeit, and with intent to utter any of them, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for ten years.
(2) Where a person has ten or more counterfeit coins in his possession, the court may presume an intent to utter unless he proves the contrary.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about repeated uttering of counterfeit gold or silver coin, or having several of dem. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e utter (use or deal with) counterfeit gold or silver coin as e sabi say e counterfeit, and at dat time e get another counterfeit gold or silver coin; or utter am as e sabi say, and on di same day or any of di 10 days wey follow utter another counterfeit current gold or silver coin as e sabi say; or get 3 or more pieces of counterfeit current gold or silver coin, as e sabi say, wey wan utter any of dem. Di punishment na prison for 10 years. If person get 10 or more counterfeit coins, di court fit presume say e wan utter dem, unless e prove another thing.

sections.title: Offences after previous conviction
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text: Any person who commits any of the offences defined in sections 151 and 152 of this Code, after having been previously convicted of any of those offences committed with respect to current coin, or of any felony committed with respect to current coin, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about crime after earlier conviction. Person wey commit any of di crimes wey sections 151 and 152 of dis Code define, after di court don find am guilty before of any of dem about current coin, or of any felony (serious crime) about current coin, don commit felony. Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Counterfeiting nickel coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) makes, or begins to make, any counterfeit current nickel coin; or
(b) without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, knowingly makes or mends, or begins, or prepares to make or mend, or has in his possession, or disposes of, any tool, instrument, or machine, which is adapted and intended for making any counterfeit current nickel coin; or
(c) buys, sells, receives, pays, or disposes of, any counterfeit current nickel coin at a lower rate of value than it imports, or was apparently intended to import, or offers to do any such act, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about counterfeiting nickel coin. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e make or begin to make counterfeit current nickel coin; or, without authority or excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am), as e sabi say make, mend, begin or prepare to make or mend, get or dispose of tool, instrument or machine wey dem adapt and mean for making counterfeit current nickel coin; or buy, sell, receive, pay or dispose of counterfeit current nickel coin for lower value than e show, or offer to do so. Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Uttering base nickel coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) utters any counterfeit current nickel coin, knowing it to be counterfeit; or
(b) has in his possession three or more pieces of counterfeit current nickel coin, knowing them to be counterfeit, and with intent to utter any of them, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
(2) Where a person has ten or more counterfeit coins in his possession, the court may presume an intent to utter unless he proves the contrary.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about uttering base nickel coin. Person wey utter (use or deal with) counterfeit current nickel coin as e sabi say e counterfeit, or get 3 or more pieces of am as e sabi say wey wan utter any of dem, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant). If person get 10 or more counterfeit coins, di court fit presume say e wan utter dem, unless e prove another thing.

sections.title: Defacing coin by stamping words thereon
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who defaces any current coin by stamping thereon any name or word, whether the weight of the coin is or is not thereby diminished, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defacing coin by stamping words on am. Person wey deface any current coin by stamping any name or word on am, whether di coin weight reduce or no, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Uttering foreign coin, medals, etc., as current coin with intent to defraud
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud, utters as and for current gold or silver coin-
(a) any coin which is not current coin; or
(b) any metal or pieces of metal, whether a coin or not, which is of less value than the current coin as and for which it is uttered, is guilty of a misdemeanour, and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about uttering foreign coin, medals or other things as current coin to cheat. Person wey wan cheat and utter as current gold or silver coin any coin wey no be current coin, or any metal or piece of metal, coin or no coin, wey get less value than di current coin wey e take dey pass am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Exporting counterfeit current coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, exports or puts on board of a vessel or vehicle of any kind for the purpose of being exported from Nigeria, any counterfeit current coin whatever, knowing it to be counterfeit, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about exporting counterfeit current coin. Person wey, without authority or excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am), export, or put for vessel or vehicle of any kind to export from Nigeria, any counterfeit current coin, as e sabi say e counterfeit, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Unlawfully importing counterfeit coin
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, imports or receives into Nigeria any counterfeit coin whatever, knowing it to be counterfeit, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawfully importing counterfeit coin. Person wey, without authority or excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am), import or receive into Nigeria any counterfeit coin, as e sabi say e counterfeit, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years. Police fit arrest person wey dem see dey commit di crime without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Tender of defaced coin not legal tender: penalty for uttering
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text:
Any person who utters any current coin which is defaced by the stamping of any name or word thereon, is guilty of an offence and is liable to a fine of four naira.
A prosecution for any such offence cannot be commenced without the consent of a law officer. A tender of payment in money made in any coin so defaced is not a legal tender.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about tender of defaced coin and punishment for uttering am. Person wey utter any current coin wey dem deface by stamping name or word on am don commit crime. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦4. Dem no fit start case without agreement of law officer. Payment in money wey dem make with such defaced coin no be legal tender.

sections.title: Making, issue and circulation of promissory notes payable to bearer on demand, without authority
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text: Any person, other than the Central Bank of Nigeria, who makes or issues within Nigeria promissory notes payable to bearer on demand or circulates within Nigeria any promissory note payable to bearer on demand, is guilty of a misdemeanour and liable on conviction to a fine equal to double the value of any promissory note unlawfully made, issued or circulated or to imprisonment for a term of twelve months, or to both such imprisonment and fine. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about promissory notes wey dem must pay to bearer on demand. Person, apart from di Central Bank of Nigeria, wey make or issue for Nigeria promissory notes wey dem must pay to bearer on demand, or circulate any such note for Nigeria, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) wey equal double di value of any note wey dem make, issue or circulate for wrong way (against di law), or prison for 12 months, or both.

sections.title: Portrayal of Nigerian notes and coins
sections.chapter: Chapter 16: Offences relating to the currency
sections.text: Any person who, without the written permission of the Minister of the Federation charged with responsibility for matters relating to finance, makes or sells, or exposes or offers for sale, or uses for the purpose of advertising any material or document on or in which is portrayed a note or coin in any way resembling a currency note, bank note or coin current in Nigeria, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year or to a fine of two hundred naira. [49 of 1960.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about portrayal of Nigerian notes and coins. Person wey, without written permission of di Minister of di Federation wey handle finance matters, make or sell, or show or offer for sale, or use for advertising any material or document wey show note or coin wey resemble currency note, bank note or coin wey dey current for Nigeria, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200.

sections.title: Stopping mails
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who stops a mail with intent to search or rob postal matter is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping mails. Person wey stop mail wey wan search or rob postal matter don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Intercepting telegrams or postal matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully secretes or destroys any postal matter or telegram or any part of any such thing, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years, and if any such postal matter so secreted or destroyed shall contain any money or chattel whatsoever, or any valuable security, such person is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding or destroying telegrams or postal matter. Person wey for wrong way (against di law) hide or destroy any postal matter or telegram, or any part of am, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. But if di postal matter wey e hide or destroy get any money, chattel or valuable security inside, di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Tampering with telegrams or postal matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who, being employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service, does with respect to any postal matter or telegram any act which he is not authorised to do by virtue of his employment, or knowingly permits any other person to do any such act with respect to any such thing, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about tampering with telegrams or postal matter. Person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service and do any act about postal matter or telegram wey im work no authorise am to do, or as e sabi say allow another person do any such act, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Wilful misdelivery of telegrams or postal matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who, being charged by virtue of his employment or by virtue of any contract, with the delivery of any postal matter or telegram, wilfully delivers it to a person other than the person to whom it is addressed, or his authorised agent in that behalf, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wilful misdelivery of telegrams or postal matter. Person wey im work or contract charge with delivering postal matter or telegram, and wey on purpose deliver am to person wey no be di person wey dem address am to, or im authorised agent, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Obtaining telegrams or postal matter by false pretences
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who by means of any false pretence induces any person employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service or any telegraph official to deliver to him any postal matter or telegram which is not addressed to him, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about getting telegrams or postal matter by false pretences. Person wey, by false pretence, make person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service or any telegraph official deliver to am postal matter or telegram wey dem no address to am don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Secreting letters and telegrams
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who wilfully secretes or detains any postal matter or telegram which is found by him, or which is wrongly delivered to him, and which, in either case, ought to his knowledge, to have been delivered to another person, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding letters and telegrams. Person wey on purpose hide or hold postal matter or telegram wey e find, or wey dem deliver wrongly to am, and wey, as e sabi say, suppose go to another person, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Fraudulent issue of money orders and postal orders
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who, being employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service, and being charged by virtue of his employment with any duty in connection with the issue of money orders or postal orders, unlawfully, and with intent to defraud, issues a money order or postal order, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for seven years. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about fraudulent issue of money orders and postal orders. Person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service, wey im work charge with duty about issue of money orders or postal orders, and wey for wrong way (against di law) and wey wan cheat issue money order or postal order, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Fraudulent messages respecting money orders
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who, being employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service, and being charged by virtue of his employment with any duty in connection with money orders, sends to any other person, with intent to defraud, any false or misleading letter, telegram, or message concerning a money order, or concerning any money payable under a money order, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years. [1966 No.84.] The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about fraudulent messages about money orders. Person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service, wey im work charge with duty about money orders, and wey wan cheat, send to another person any false or misleading letter, telegram or message about money order or money wey dem go pay under money order, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Unlawful franking of letters
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who, being empowered under the provisions of any enactment or authorised by the Minister charged with responsibility for postal matter to frank postal matter, superscribes any postal matter- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(a) which does not relate to the business of his office or department; or
(b) into which there has been inserted any letter or other thing which does not relate to such business, with intent to avoid payment of the postage on such postal matter or other letter or thing inserted as aforesaid into such postal matter, is guilty of an offence, and is liable to a fine of two hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful franking of letters. Person wey enactment or di Minister wey handle postal matter authorise to frank postal matter, and wey superscribe postal matter wey no concern di business of im office or department, or wey get letter or other thing inside wey no concern such business, so dat e go avoid to pay di postage, don commit crime. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200.

sections.title: Sending dangerous or obscene things by post
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who knowingly sends, or attempts to send by post anything which-
(a) encloses anything, whether living or inanimate, of such a nature as to be likely to injure any other thing in the course of conveyance or to injure any person; or
(b) encloses an indecent or obscene print, painting, photograph, lithograph, engraving, book, card, or article, or which has on it, or in it, or on its cover, any indecent, obscene, or grossly offensive words, marks, or designs, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sending dangerous or obscene things by post. Person wey as e sabi say send, or try to send by post, anything wey get inside anything, living or no living, wey fit injure another thing for di way or injure person; or wey get indecent or obscene print, painting, photograph, book, card or article, or wey get indecent, obscene or grossly offensive words, marks or designs on am or inside am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Retarding delivery of telegrams or postal matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who, being required by law or by virtue of his employment to do any act with respect to the receipt, despatch, or delivery, of any postal matter or telegram- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(a) neglects or refuses to do such act; or
(b) wilfully detains or delays, or permits the detention or delay of any such thing; or
(c) opens, or procures or suffers to be opened, any postal matter, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to a fine of two hundred naira or to imprisonment for one year:
Provided always that nothing herein contained shall extend to the opening or detaining of any postal matter or telegram returned by reason that the person to whom the same shall be directed is dead, or cannot be found, or shall have refused the same, or shall have refused or neglected to pay the postage thereof or any charges payable in respect thereof, nor to the opening or detaining or delaying of any postal matter or telegram under the authority of any Act or in obedience to an express warrant in writing under the hand of the Minister charged with responsibility for postal matter.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about delaying delivery of telegrams or postal matter. Person wey law or im work require to do act about receipt, despatch or delivery of postal matter or telegram, and wey neglect or refuse to do am; or on purpose hold or delay am, or permit di holding or delay; or open, or cause or allow make dem open, any postal matter, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200 or prison for 1 year. But dis no cover opening or holding of postal matter or telegram wey dem return because di person dem address am to don die, or dem no see am, or e refuse am, or e refuse or neglect to pay postage or charges, or opening, holding or delaying under authority of any Act or express written warrant of di Minister wey handle postal matter.

sections.title: Obstructing mails
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who wilfully obstructs or delays the conveyance or delivery of postal matter, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of one hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about obstructing mails. Person wey on purpose obstruct or delay conveyance or delivery of postal matter don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100.

sections.title: Penalty on loitering, carelessness in delivery of mails, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
(1) Any person who, being employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service to conveyor deliver postal matter whilst so employed-
(a) allows any postal matter bag or postal matter out of his possession; or
(b) suffers any unauthorised person to interfere with any such postal matter bag or postal matter; or
(c) is guilty of any neglect whereby any such postal matter bag or postal matter is endangered; or
(d) loiters on the road; or
(e) wilfully misspends or loses time; or
(f) is under the influence of intoxicating liquor; or
(g) does not convey postal matter at the speed fixed by the Postmaster-General for the conveyance thereof, unless prevented by some cause beyond his control, the proof, whereof lies on the person charged, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of twenty naira.
(2) Any person who, being employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service, negligently loses any postal mater or telegram or negligently detains or delays, or permits the detention or delay of, any postal matter or telegram, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of twenty naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about loitering and carelessness for delivery of mails. Person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service to carry or deliver postal matter, and wey, while e dey do am, allow postal matter bag or postal matter comot im possession; allow unauthorised person interfere with am; neglect am so dat e dey for danger; loiter for road; on purpose waste or lose time; dey under influence of intoxicating liquor; or no carry am at speed wey Postmaster-General fix, except cause wey e no control stop am (e must prove am), don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦20. Person wey dey work for di service and carelessly lose or delay postal matter or telegram, or permit di delay, don also commit simple offence, and di punishment na fine of ₦20.

sections.title: Fraudulently removing stamps
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud-
(1) removes from any postal matter or telegram any stamp affixed thereon; or
(2) removes from any stamp previously used any mark thereon at a postal or telegraph office; or
(3) knowingly uses a postage stamp which has been obliterated or defaced by a mark made thereon at a post or telegraph office; or
(4) knowingly tampers with a postage stamp by smearing or coating the surface with mucilage or any other substance so that it may be used again at a post or telegraph office, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year or to a fine of one hundred naira.
On the trial of a person charged with the offence of knowingly using a postage stamp which has been obliterated or defaced by a mark made thereon at a post office, proof that the person charged is the writer of the address of anything sent by post on which the stamp is affixed is sufficient evidence that he is the person who used the stamp, until the contrary is shown.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about fraudulently removing stamps. Person wey wan cheat and remove stamp from postal matter or telegram; or remove from used stamp any mark wey post or telegraph office put; or as e sabi say use postage stamp wey dem don obliterate or deface for post or telegraph office; or as e sabi say tamper with postage stamp by smearing or coating am so dat dem fit use am again, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100. If dem try person for using such stamp, proof say na im write di address of di thing wey dem send by post dey enough evidence say na im use di stamp, until e show another thing.

sections.title: Fraudulent evasion of postal laws
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) knowingly and fraudulently puts into a post office anything in or upon which, or in or upon the cover of which there is any letter, newspaper, or other thing, or any writing or mark, not allowed by law to be there placed; or
(2) wilfully subscribes on the outside of anything sent by post a false statement of its contents; or
(3) knowingly and fraudulently puts into a post office anything which falsely purports to be a thing falling within any exemption or privilege declared by the laws relating to postal matter, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of one hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about fraudulent evasion of postal laws. Person wey as e sabi say and by cheating put inside post office anything wey get letter, newspaper or other thing, or writing or mark, wey law no allow for dia; or on purpose write false statement of wetin dey inside on top something wey dem send by post; or as e sabi say and by cheating put inside post office anything wey falsely claim say e fall under exemption or privilege wey postal laws declare, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100.

sections.title: Carrying letters otherwise than by post
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about carrying letters without post. Person wey Postmaster-General no authorise, and wey send or carry letter another way apart from post, or take charge of letter to carry am, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100. Di section no cover some cases, like letter to place for Nigeria wey no get postal communication, letter wey pass di weight wey law set, letter wey private friend carry without pay, letter about goods wey dem send with am, court papers and legal documents, and letter to or from di nearest post office. But common carriers, officers of di Nigerian Postal Service and some people for vessels no get dis permission, except for some letters. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Illegally making of postal envelopes or setting up post office or office for sale of stamp, or imitating post office
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who- [1966 No. 84. L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(1) without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him-
(a) makes any envelope, wrapper, card, form, or paper, in imitation of one issued by or under the authority of the Postmaster-General or of the postal authority of any other country, or having thereon any word, letter, or mark, which signifies or implies, or may reasonably induce a person receiving it to believe, that a letter, newspaper, packet, or parcel, bearing such word, letter, or mark, is sent on State service, or on the public service of another country; or
(b) makes on any envelope, wrapper, card, form, or paper, in order to its being issued or sent by post or otherwise, any stamp or mark in imitation of a stamp or mark of any post office under the control of the Postmaster-General or of the postal authority of any other country, or any other stamp or mark, or any word or letter, which signifies or implies, or may reasonably induce a person receiving it to believe, that a letter, newspaper, packet, or parcel, bearing such stamp, mark, word, or letter, is sent on State service, or on the public service of another country; or
(c) issues or sends by post or otherwise, any envelope, wrapper, card, form, or paper, so marked; or
(2) without the authority of the Postmaster-General, the proof of which lies on the person charged, places or maintains, or permits to be placed or maintained, or to remain in, on, or near, any place under his control-
(i) the words "post office"; or
(ii) the words "letter box", accompanied with words, letters or marks which signify or imply, or may reasonably lead the public to believe, that it is a receptacle provided by the authority of the Postmaster-General for the reception of postal matter; or
(iii) any words, letters or marks which signify or imply, or may reasonably lead the public to believe, that any place is a post office, or that any such receptacle is provided by the authority of the Postmaster-General as aforesaid; or
(3) without the authority of the Postmaster-General, the proof of which lies on the person charged, places, or permits to be placed or to remain, on any vehicle or vessel under his control the words "royal mail", or any word, letter or mark, which signifies or implies, or may reasonably induce any person to believe, that the vehicle or vessel is used for the conveyance of mails; or
(4) without the licence of the Minister charged with responsibility for postal matters, the proof of which lies on the person charged-
(i) sells, or offers or exposes for sale, any postage stamp; or
(ii) places, permits to be placed or to remain, on or near to his house or premises the words
"licensed to sell stamps", or any word, letter or mark, which signifies or implies, or may reasonably induce any person to believe, that he is duly licensed to sell postage stamps, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of ten naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about illegally making postal envelopes, setting up post office or office to sell stamps, or imitating post office. Person don commit simple offence (small crime) if, without authority (e must prove am), e make or send envelope, card, form, paper, stamp or mark wey imitate wetin Postmaster-General or foreign postal authority issue, or wey make person believe say dem send am on State service; or place or keep words like 'post office' or 'letter box', or anything wey suggest say place na post office; or put words like 'royal mail' for vehicle or vessel wey e control; or, without licence of di Minister wey handle postal matters, sell stamps or put words like 'licensed to sell stamps'. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦10. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Destroying or damaging letter box
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who wilfully destroys or damages any receptacle provided by authority of the Postmaster- General for the receipt of postal matter, or any card or notice relating to the postal or telegraph service set up by authority of the Postmaster-General, or obliterates any letter or figure on any such thing, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of one hundred naira. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about destroying or damaging letter box. Person wey on purpose destroy or damage receptacle wey Postmaster-General authorise for receiving postal matter, or any card or notice about postal or telegraph service wey Postmaster-General authorise, or rub out any letter or figure on any of dem, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100.

sections.title: Placing injurious substances in or against letter box
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who places in or against any receptacle provided by authority of the Postmaster-General for the reception of postal matter or telegrams, any fire or match, or any explosive, dangerous, noxious or deleterious substance, or any fluid or filth, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of forty naira. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about placing harmful things inside or against letter box. Person wey put inside or against any receptacle wey Postmaster-General authorise for receiving postal matter or telegrams any fire or match, or any explosive, dangerous, noxious or deleterious substance, or any fluid or filth, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦40.

sections.title: Defacing post office or letter box
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who without the licence of the Postmaster-General affixes, or attempts to affix, any placard, advertisement, notice, list, document, board, or paint, tar, or other thing to any post office or telegraph office, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of ten naira. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defacing post office or letter box. Person wey, without licence of di Postmaster-General, fix or try to fix any placard, advertisement, notice, list, document, board, or paint, tar or other thing to any post office or telegraph office don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦10.

sections.title: Obstructing post and telegraph offices
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who, by stopping or loitering opposite to or on the premises of a post office or telegraph office, obstructs the business of the office or any other person lawfully going to the office, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of ten naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about obstructing post and telegraph offices. Person wey stop or loiter opposite or for di premises of post office or telegraph office, and obstruct di office business or any other person wey dey go di office for right way (di law allow am), don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦10.

sections.title: Obstructing post and telegraph officers in the execution of duty
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who- [1966 No. 84.]
(1) wilfully obstructs a person employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service or any telegraph official in the execution of the duties of his employment; or
(2) being in a post office or telegraph office, or within any premises appertaining to a post office or telegraph office, or used therewith, wilfully obstructs the business of the office; or
(3) without the permission of a competent authority enters any part of a telegraph office to which the public are not admitted, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of four naira.
Any person employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service or any telegraph official may require any person committing any of the offences defined in this section of this Code to leave the post office, or telegraph office, or premises.
Any person who refuses or fails to comply with such request is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a further fine of ten naira, and may be removed by any person authorised to make the request; and all members of the police force are required, on demand, to remove or assist in removing such person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about obstructing post and telegraph officers for duty. Person wey on purpose obstruct person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service or any telegraph official for im duty; or, for post office or telegraph office or im premises, on purpose obstruct di office business; or enter any part of telegraph office wey public no fit enter without permission of competent authority, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦4. Postal or telegraph worker fit require di person to comot di office or premises. Person wey refuse or fail don commit simple offence and go face further fine of ₦10, and person wey dem authorise fit remove am; all police members must, on demand, remove or help remove am.

sections.title: Contravening exclusive privilege of the Nigerian Postal Services Department
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) not being authorised by or under any Act so to do, establishes or maintains any telegraph; or
(b) knowing or having reason to believe that a telegraph has been established or is maintained without such authority as aforesaid, transmits or receives any message by such telegraph or performs any service incidental thereto, or delivery of any message for transmission by such telegraph or accepts delivery of any message sent thereby, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable on a first conviction to a fine of twenty naira, and on every subsequent conviction to a fine of one hundred naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about breaking di exclusive privilege of di Nigerian Postal Services Department. Person wey no dey authorised by any Act and establish or maintain telegraph; or wey sabi or get reason to believe say telegraph dey without such authority and transmit or receive message by am, do service wey connect am, or deliver or accept message for am, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦20 for first time di court find am guilty, and ₦100 for every later time.

sections.title: Negligently injuring telegraphs
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who negligently destroys or damages any telegraph works, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of four naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about negligently injuring telegraphs. Person wey carelessly destroy or damage any telegraph works don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦4.

sections.title: Violation of secrecy
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any telegraph official who, contrary to his duty, publishes or communicates the contents or substance of a telegram, or any information relating to the despatch or receipt of any telegram, except to some person to whom he is authorised to deliver the telegram, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about violation of secrecy. Telegraph official wey, against im duty, publish or tell di contents or substance of telegram, or any information about sending or receiving telegram, except to person wey e dey authorised to deliver di telegram to, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Resisting officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text: Any person who resists a person employed by or under the Nigerian Postal Service while engaged in the execution of his duty under the laws relating to posts and telegraphs, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to imprisonment for three months, or to a fine of forty naira. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about resisting officers. Person wey resist person wey dey work for or under di Nigerian Postal Service as e dey do im duty under di laws about posts and telegraphs don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 months, or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦40.

sections.title: Laying property in postal matter and telegraph works
sections.chapter: Chapter 17: Offences relating to posts and telecommunications
sections.text:
(1) In case of any offence under this Code in respect of any postal matter bag or postal matter, or of any chattel, money, or valuable security sent by post, it shall be sufficient in any proceedings to lay the ownership in the Postmaster-General. [1966 No. 84.]
(2) In case of any offence under this Code in respect of any telegram, telegraph line or telegraph works, established under the provisions of the Wireless Telegraphs Act, or the Telegraphs Proclamation, or in respect of any form, paper, book, or other thing used for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of such Act or proclamation, it shall be sufficient in any proceedings to lay the ownership in the Postmaster-General. [Cap. W5.]
(3) In any such proceedings as aforesaid, it shall not be necessary to prove ownership, or to allege or prove any value.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about how to state ownership for postal matter and telegraph works. For crime under dis Code about postal matter bag, postal matter, or any chattel, money or valuable security wey dem send by post, e dey enough to state say di Postmaster-General na di owner. Di same dey for telegram, telegraph line or telegraph works wey dem establish under di Wireless Telegraphs Act or di Telegraphs Proclamation, and for forms, paper, books or other things wey dem use to carry out dem. Dem no need prove ownership or state or prove any value.

sections.title: False declaration as to execution of sentence of death
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who subscribes a certificate or declaration as to the execution of a sentence of death, which, in any material particular, is to his knowledge false, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false declaration about execution of sentence of death. Person wey sign certificate or declaration about execution of sentence of death wey, as e sabi say, false for any material way, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: False statements in application for passports
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who for the purpose of procuring a passport, whether for himself or any other individual, makes or causes to be made in any written application to a public officer a statement which to the knowledge of such person is false in any material particular, is guilty of an offence and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false statements for passport applications. Person wey, to get passport for imself or any other individual, make or cause make dem make for written application to public officer statement wey, as e sabi say, false for any material way, don commit crime. Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: False statements in statements required to be under oath or solemn declaration
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text:
Any person who, on any occasion on which a person making a statement touching any matter is required by law to make it on oath, or under some sanction which may by law be substituted for an oath, or is required to verify it by solemn declaration or affirmation, makes a statement touching such matter which, in any material particular, is to his knowledge false, and verifies it on oath, or under such other sanction or by solemn declaration or affirmation, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false statements wey law require make dem make on oath or solemn declaration. Person wey, when law require am to make statement on oath, or under another thing wey fit replace oath, or to verify am by solemn declaration or affirmation, make statement wey, as e sabi say, false for any material way, and verify am so, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: False declarations and statements
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text:
Any person who, on any occasion on which he is permitted or required by law to make a statement or declaration before any person authorised by law to permit it to be made before him, makes a statement or declaration before that person which, in any material particular, is to his knowledge false, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false declarations and statements. Person wey, when law permit or require am to make statement or declaration before person wey law authorise to permit am, make statement or declaration before dat person wey, as e sabi say, false for any material way, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Evidence
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: A person cannot be convicted of any of the offences defined in sections 191 and 192 of this Code upon the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say di court no fit find person guilty of any crime wey sections 191 and 192 of dis Code define only because one witness testify and no other evidence support am.

sections.title: Shooting at customs boats or officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) shoots at a vessel of any kind which is in use by a customs officer while engaged in the execution of his duty as such officer; or
(2) shoots at, wounds, or causes any grievous harm to a customs officer while engaged in the execution of his duty in the prevention of smuggling, or any person acting in aid of a customs officer while so engaged, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about shooting at customs boats or officers. Person wey shoot at any vessel wey customs officer dey use as e dey do im duty; or shoot at, wound or cause grievous harm to customs officer as e dey do im duty to prevent smuggling, or person wey dey help am, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Resisting officers engaged in preventing smuggling
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who with violence assaults, obstructs, or resists a customs officer, or any person duly employed for the prevention of smuggling, while engaged in the execution of his duty in the prevention of smuggling, or any person acting in aid of any such officer or person while so engaged, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about resisting officers wey dey prevent smuggling. Person wey use violence assault, obstruct or resist customs officer, or person wey dem duly employ to prevent smuggling, or person wey dey help dem, as dem dey do dia duty to prevent smuggling, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Resisting customs officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) assaults or obstructs a customs officer, or any person duly employed for the prevention of smuggling , while engaged in the execution of his duty under any law relating to the customs, or in the seizure of any goods claimed to be liable to forfeiture under any such law, or any person acting in aid of any such officer or person while so engaged; or
(2) rescues or attempts to rescue any goods which have been seized under any such law; or
(3) before, at, or after, the seizure of any goods under any such law, staves, breaks or destroys the goods, with intent to prevent the seizure or the securing of the goods, or attempts to do any such act, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of two hundred naira.
