sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about resisting customs officers. Person don commit simple offence (small crime) if e assault or obstruct customs officer, or person wey dem duly employ to prevent smuggling, or person wey dey help dem, as dem dey do dia duty under customs law or seize goods; rescue or try to rescue goods wey dem seize under such law; or, before, during or after seizure, damage, break or destroy di goods, or try to, so dat dem no go fit seize or secure am. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦200.

sections.title: Resisting public officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who in any manner obstructs or resists any public officer while engaged in the discharge or attempted discharge of the duties of his office under any order, Act, law, or Statute, or obstructs or resists any person while engaged in the discharge or attempted discharge of any duty imposed on him by an order, Act, law, or statute, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years. [L.N. 112 of 1964. L.N. 139 of 1965.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about resisting public officers. Person wey obstruct or resist any public officer as e dey do or try to do di duties of im office under any order, Act, law or Statute, or obstruct or resist any person as e dey do or try to do duty wey order, Act, law or statute give am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Refusal by public officer to perform duty
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who, being a person employed in the public service and being required by any order, Act, law, or statute, to do any act by virtue of his employment, perversely and without lawful excuse omits or refuses to do any such act, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years. A prosecution for any offence under this section of this Code shall not be instituted except by or with the consent of a law officer. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about public officer wey refuse to do im duty. Person wey dey work for public service, and wey order, Act, law or statute require to do act because of im work, and wey stubbornly and without excuse wey di law accept omit or refuse to do am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Dem no fit start case except law officer start am or agree.

sections.title: Neglect of peace officer to suppress riot
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who, being a peace officer and having notice that there is a riot in his neighbourhood, without reasonable excuse omits to do his duty in suppressing such riot, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about peace officer wey neglect to suppress riot. Person wey be peace officer, wey know say riot dey im area, and wey without reasonable excuse no do im duty to suppress di riot, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Neglect to aid in suppressing riot
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who, having reasonable notice that he is required to assist any peace officer in suppressing a riot, without reasonable excuse omits to do so, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about neglect to help suppress riot. Person wey get reasonable notice say dem require am to help peace officer suppress riot, and wey without reasonable excuse no do so, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Neglect to aid in arresting offenders
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who, having reasonable notice that he is required to assist any peace officer or member of the police force in arresting any person, or in preserving the peace, without reasonable excuse omits to do so, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about neglect to help arrest offenders. Person wey get reasonable notice say dem require am to help peace officer or police member arrest person, or keep di peace, and wey without reasonable excuse no do so, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Disobedience to Act, law, or statute
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text:
Any person who, without lawful excuse, the proof of which lies on him, does any act which he is by the provisions of any order, Act, law, or statute, forbidden to do, or omits to do any act which he is by the provisions of any such order, Act, law or statute, required to do, is guilty of a misdemeanour, unless some mode of proceeding against him for such disobedience is expressly provided by order, Act, law, or statute, and is intended to be exclusive of all other punishment. [L.N. 112 of 1964.] The offender is liable to imprisonment for one year.
In this section, the terms "Act" and "law" do not include an order, regulation or proclamation made under the authority of an Act or a law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about disobedience to Act, law or statute. Person wey, without excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am), do act wey any order, Act, law or statute forbid am to do, or no do act wey dem require am to do, don commit misdemeanour (small crime), except say order, Act, law or statute clearly provide another way to proceed against am for such disobedience wey dem mean to be di only punishment. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. For dis section, 'Act' and 'law' no include order, regulation or proclamation wey dem make under di authority of Act or law.

sections.title: Disobedience to lawful order issued by constituted authority
sections.chapter: Chapter 18: Miscellaneous offences against public authority
sections.text: Any person who, without lawful excuse, the proof of which lies on him, disobeys any lawful order issued by any person authorised by any order, Act, law, or statute, to make the order, is guilty of a misdemeanor, unless some mode of proceeding against him for such disobedience is expressly provided by order, Act, law, or statute, and is intended to be exclusive of all other punishment. [L.N. 112 of 1964.] The offender is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about disobedience to lawful order from constituted authority. Person wey, without excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am), disobey lawful order wey person wey order, Act, law or statute authorise make, don commit misdemeanour (small crime), except say order, Act, law or statute clearly provide another way to proceed against am for such disobedience wey dem mean to be di only punishment. Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Insult to a religion
sections.chapter: Chapter 19: Offences relating to religious worship
sections.text: Any person who does an act which any class of persons consider as a public insult on their religion, with the intention that they should consider the act such an insult, and any person who does an unlawful act with the knowledge that any class of persons will consider it such an insult, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about insult to religion. Person wey do act wey any class of people consider as public insult on dia religion, and wey wan make dem consider am so, or wey do act for wrong way (against di law) as e sabi say any class of people go consider am such insult, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Offering violence to officiating ministers of religion
sections.chapter: Chapter 19: Offences relating to religious worship
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) by threats or force prevents or attempts to prevent any minister of religion from lawfully officiating in any place of religious worship, or from performing his duty in the lawful burial of the dead in any cemetery or other burial place; or
(2) by threats or force obstructs or attempts to obstruct, any minister of religion while so officiating or performing his duty; or
(3) assaults, or, upon or under the pretence of executing any civil process, arrests any minister of religion who is engaged in, or is, to the knowledge of the offender, about to engage in, any of the offices or duties aforesaid, or who is, to the knowledge of the offender, going to perform the same or returning from the performance thereof, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about offering violence to officiating ministers of religion. Person wey use threats or force prevent or try to prevent minister of religion from officiating for right way (di law allow am) for place of religious worship, or from doing im duty for lawful burial of di dead for cemetery or other burial place; or use threats or force obstruct or try to obstruct am as e dey do so; or assault am, or arrest am under or pretending to execute civil process, when e dey, or as e sabi say about to, do such duties, or dey go or return from dem, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Disturbing religious worship
sections.chapter: Chapter 19: Offences relating to religious worship
sections.text: Any person who wilfully and without lawful justification or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, disquiets, or disturbs any meeting of persons lawfully assembled for religious worship, or assaults any person lawfully officiating at any such meeting, or any of the persons there assembled, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to imprisonment for two months or to a fine of ten naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about disturbing religious worship. Person wey on purpose and without justification or excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am) disturb meeting of people wey lawfully gather for religious worship, or assault person wey dey lawfully officiate for di meeting or any person wey gather there, don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 months or fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦10.

sections.title: Unlawful trial by ordeal: prohibited juju
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text:
(1) The trial by the ordeal of sasswood, esere-bean, or the poison, boiling oil, fire, immersion in water or exposure to the attacks of crocodiles or other wild animals, or by any ordeal which is likely to result in the death of or bodily injury to any party to the proceeding, is unlawful.
(2) The President or, as the case may be, the Governor of a State may by order prohibit the worship or invocation of any juju which may appear to him to involve or tend towards the commission of any crime or breach of peace, or to the spread of any infectious or contagious disease.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unlawful trial by ordeal and prohibited juju. Trial by ordeal of sasswood, esere-bean or poison, boiling oil, fire, immersion for water or exposure to attack of crocodiles or other wild animals, or any ordeal wey fit cause death or bodily injury to any party for di proceeding, na unlawful. Di President or di Governor of a State fit by order prohibit worship or invocation of any juju wey e think say involve or lead to crime or breach of peace, or spread of infectious or contagious disease.

sections.title: Directing, etc., unlawful trial by ordeal
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text: Any person who directs or controls or presides at any trial by ordeal which is unlawful, is guilty of a felony and is liable, when the trial which such person directs, controls or presides at results in the death of any party to the proceeding, to the punishment of death and m every other case, to imprisonment for ten years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about directing unlawful trial by ordeal. Person wey direct, control or preside at trial by ordeal wey dey unlawful don commit felony (serious crime). If di trial result for death of any party, di punishment na death. For every other case, di punishment na prison for 10 years.

sections.title: Being present at, or making poison for, unlawful trial by ordeal
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) is present at or takes part in any trial by ordeal which is unlawful; or
(b) makes, sells or assists or takes part in making or selling, or has in his possession for sale or use any poison or thing which is intended to be used for the purpose of any trial by ordeal which is unlawful, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about being present at, or making poison for, unlawful trial by ordeal. Person wey dey present at or take part for unlawful trial by ordeal; or make, sell, or help or take part to make or sell, or get for sale or use, any poison or thing wey dem mean to use for such trial, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Offences in relation to witchcraft and juju
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) by his statements or actions represents himself to be a witch or to have the power of witchcraft; or
(b) accuses or threatens to accuse any person with being a witch or with having the power of witchcraft; or
(c) makes or sells or uses, or assists or takes part in making or selling or using or has in his possession or represents himself to be in possession of any juju, drug or charm which is intended to be used or reported to possess the power to prevent or delay any person from doing an act which such person has a legal right to do, or to compel any person to do an act which such person has a legal right to refrain from doing, or which is alleged or reported to possess the power of causing any natural phenomenon or any disease or epidemic; or
(d) directs or controls or presides at or is present at or takes part in the worship or invocation of any juju which is prohibited by an order of the President or the Governor of a State; or
(e) is in possession of or has control over any human remains which are used or are intended to be used in connection with the worship or invocation of any juju; or
(f) makes or uses or assists in making or using, or has in his possession anything whatsoever the making, use or possession of which has been prohibited by an order as being or believed to be associated with human sacrifice or other unlawful practice, is guilty of misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about crimes about witchcraft and juju. Person don commit misdemeanour (small crime) if e, by statements or actions, say e be witch or get witchcraft power; accuse or threaten to accuse person say e be witch; make, sell, use or get juju, drug or charm wey dem mean or report say e fit stop or delay person from doing wetin e get legal right to do, or force person to do wetin e get legal right to refuse, or fit cause natural phenomenon, disease or epidemic; direct, control, preside at, attend or take part for worship of juju wey di President or Governor prohibit by order; get or control human remains wey dem use or mean to use for juju worship; or make, use or get anything wey order prohibit as connected to human sacrifice or other unlawful practice. Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Chiefs permitting unlawful ordeal and prohibited juju worship
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text: Any chief who directly or indirectly permits, promotes, encourages or facilitates any trial by ordeal which is unlawful, or the worship or invocation of any juju which has been prohibited by an order, or who knowing of such trial, worship or invocation, or intended trial, worship or invocation, does not forthwith report the same to an administrative officer, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years. [L.N. 257 of 1959.] The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about chiefs wey permit unlawful ordeal and prohibited juju worship. Chief wey directly or indirectly permit, promote, encourage or help any unlawful trial by ordeal, or worship of juju wey order prohibit, or wey sabi about dem or about planned one and no report am quick to administrative officer, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Destruction of place where unlawful ordeal or prohibited juju worship is held
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text: Any house, grove or place in which it has been customary to hold any trial by ordeal which is unlawful, or the worship or invocation of any juju which is prohibited by an order, may, together with all articles found therein, be destroyed or erased upon the order of any court by such persons as the court may direct. [L.N. 257 of 1959.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about destroying place wey dem hold unlawful ordeal or prohibited juju worship. Any house, grove or place wey dem dey customarily hold unlawful trial by ordeal, or worship of prohibited juju, fit dey destroyed or erased, together with all articles inside, on order of any court, by persons wey di court direct.

sections.title: Criminal charms
sections.chapter: Chapter 20: Ordeal, witchcraft, juju and criminal charms
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) makes, sells or keeps for sale or for hire or reward, any fetish or charm which is pretended or reputed to possess power to protect burglars, robbers, thieves or other malefactors, or to aid or assist in any way in the perpetration of any burglary, housebreaking, robbery or theft, or in the perpetration of any offence whatsoever, or to prevent, hinder or delay the detection of or conviction for any offence whatsoever; or
(b) is found having in his possession without lawful and reasonable excuse (the proof of which excuse shall lie on such person) any such fetish or charm as aforesaid, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about criminal charms. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e make, sell or keep for sale or hire fetish or charm wey dem pretend or report say e fit protect burglars, robbers, thieves or other wrongdoers, or help for burglary, housebreaking, robbery, theft or any crime, or stop, block or delay detection or conviction for any crime; or if dem see am get any such fetish or charm without excuse wey di law accept (e must prove am). Di punishment na prison for 5 years.

sections.title: Unnatural offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) has carnal knowledge of any person against the order of nature; or
(2) has carnal knowledge of an animal; or
(3) permits a male person to have carnal knowledge of him or her against the order of nature, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about unnatural offences. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e have carnal knowledge of any person against di order of nature; have carnal knowledge of animal; or permit male person to have carnal knowledge of am against di order of nature. Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Attempt to commit unnatural offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who attempts to commit any of the offences defined in section 214 of this Code, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to commit unnatural offences. Person wey try to commit any crime wey section 214 of dis Code define don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Indecent treatment of boys under fourteen
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully and indecently deals with a boy under the age of fourteen years, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The term "deal with" includes doing any act which, if done without consent, would constitute an assault as hereinafter defined.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about indecent treatment of boys wey never reach 14 years. Person wey for wrong way (against di law) and indecently deal with boy wey never reach 14 years don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. 'Deal with' include any act wey go be assault if dem do am without agreement (say 'yes').

sections.title: Indecent practices between males
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any male person who, whether in public or private, commits any act of gross indecency with another male person, or procures another male person to commit any act of gross indecency with him, or attempts to procure the commission of any such act by any male person with himself or with another male person, whether in public or private, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about indecent practices between males. Male person wey, for public or private, commit act of gross indecency with another male person, or procure another male person to commit such act with am, or try to procure di commission of such act by any male person with am or with another male person, don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Defilement of girls under thirteen
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who has unlawful carnal knowledge of a girl under the age of thirteen years is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life, with or without caning. [30 of 1960.] Any person who attempts to have unlawful carnal knowledge of a girl under the age of thirteen years is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years, with or without caning.
A prosecution for either of the offences defined in this section of this Code shall be begun within two months after the offence is committed.
A person cannot be convicted of either of the offences defined in this section of this Code upon the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defilement of girls wey never reach 13 years. Person wey get unlawful carnal knowledge of girl wey never reach 13 years don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life, with or without caning. Person wey try to get unlawful carnal knowledge of girl wey never reach 13 years don also commit felony, and di punishment na prison for 14 years, with or without caning. Dem must start case for either crime within 2 months after di crime happen. Di court no fit find person guilty of either crime only because one witness testify and no other evidence support am.

sections.title: Householder permitting defilement of young girls on his premises
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who, being the owner or occupier of any premises, or having, or acting, or assisting in the management or control of any premises, induces or knowingly permits any girl of such age as is in this section of this Code mentioned to resort to or be in or upon such premises for the purpose of being unlawfully carnally known by any man, whether a particular man or not, is guilty of an offence.
If the girl is of or above thirteen and under sixteen years of age, he is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years, with or without caning.
If the girl is under the age of thirteen years, he is guilty of felony, and is liable to imprisonment for life, without caning.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about owner or occupier wey permit defilement of young girls for im premises. Person wey own or occupy premises, or manage or control am or help for am, and wey induce or as e sabi say permit girl of di ages wey dis section mention to go or dey for di premises so dat any man, particular or no, go get unlawful carnal knowledge of her, don commit crime. If di girl na 13 years or more but never reach 16 years, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime) and di punishment na prison for 2 years, with or without caning. If di girl never reach 13 years, e don commit felony (serious crime) and di punishment na prison for life, without caning.

sections.title: Defence to charge under preceding section
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text: *It is a defence to a charge of any of the offences defined in section 219 of this Code to prove that the accused person believed, on reasonable grounds, that the girl was of or above the age of sixteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defence to charge under section 219 of dis Code. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di accused fit prove say e believe, on reasonable grounds, say di girl na 16 years or more.

sections.title: Defilement of girls under sixteen and above thirteen, and of idiots
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) has or attempts to have unlawful carnal knowledge of a girl being of or above thirteen years and under sixteen years of age; or [1960 No. 30.]
(2) knowing a woman or girl to be an idiot or imbecile, has or attempts to have unlawful carnal knowledge of her, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years, with or without caning. *It is a defence to a charge of either of the offences firstly defined in this section of this Code to prove that the accused person believed, on reasonable grounds, that the girl was of or above the age of sixteen years.
A prosecution for any of the offences defined in this section of this Code shall be begun within two months after the offence is committed.
A person cannot be convicted of any of the offences defined in this section of this Code upon the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defilement of girls wey be 13 years or more but never reach 16 years, and of idiots. Person don commit misdemeanour (small crime) if e get or try to get unlawful carnal knowledge of girl wey be 13 years or more but never reach 16 years; or, as e sabi say woman or girl na idiot or imbecile, get or try to get unlawful carnal knowledge of her. Di punishment na prison for 2 years, with or without caning. Dem must start case within 2 months after di crime happen, and di court no fit find person guilty only because one witness testify and no other evidence support am. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept) for di first kind: di accused fit prove say e believe, on reasonable grounds, say di girl na 16 years or more.

sections.title: Indecent treatment of girls under sixteen
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully and indecently deals with a girl under the age of sixteen years is guilty of a misdemeanour, and is liable to imprisonment for two years, with or without caning. [20 of 1960.] If the girl is under the age of thirteen years, he is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years, with or without caning. *It is a defence to a charge of the offence defined in this section to prove that the accused person believed, on reasonable grounds, that the girl was of or above the age of sixteen years.
The term "deal with" includes doing any act which, if done without consent, would constitute an assault as hereinafter defined.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about indecent treatment of girls wey never reach 16 years. Person wey for wrong way (against di law) and indecently deal with girl wey never reach 16 years don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years, with or without caning. If di girl never reach 13 years, e don commit felony (serious crime) and di punishment na prison for 3 years, with or without caning. 'Deal with' include any act wey go be assault if dem do am without agreement (say 'yes'). E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di accused fit prove say e believe, on reasonable grounds, say di girl na 16 years or more.

sections.title: Causing or encouraging the seduction or prostitution of a girl under sixteen
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
(1) Whoever, having the custody, charge or care of a girl under the age of sixteen years, causes or encourages the seduction, unlawful carnal knowledge or prostitution of, or the commission of an indecent assault upon, such a girl, shall be liable to imprisonment for two years.
(2) For the purposes of this section, a person shall be deemed to have caused or encouraged the seduction, unlawful carnal knowledge or prostitution of, or the commission of an indecent assault upon, a girl who has been seduced, unlawfully carnally known, or indecently assaulted, or who has become a prostitute, if he has knowingly allowed her to consort with, or to enter or continue in the employment of, any prostitute or person of known immoral character.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about causing or encouraging di seduction or prostitution of girl wey never reach 16 years. Person wey get custody, charge or care of girl wey never reach 16 years and cause or encourage her seduction, unlawful carnal knowledge or prostitution, or indecent assault on her, go face prison for 2 years. Dem go count person say e cause or encourage am if girl don dey seduced, unlawfully carnally known, indecently assaulted, or don become prostitute, and e as e sabi say allow her to dey with, or enter or continue work with, any prostitute or person of known immoral character.

sections.title: Allowing person under sixteen to be in brothels
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
(1) Whoever, having the custody, charge or care of a child or young person who has attained the age of four years and is under the age of sixteen years, allows that child or young person to reside in or frequent a brothel, is liable to a fine of one hundred naira or to imprisonment for six months or to both such fine and imprisonment.
(2) If, upon the trial of a person charged with an offence against section 219 of this Code, the facts proved in evidence authorise a conviction for an offence against this section of this Code, the person charged may be convicted of the offence against this section of this Code although he was not charged with that offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about allowing person wey never reach 16 years to dey brothels. Person wey get custody, charge or care of child or young person wey be 4 years or more but never reach 16 years and allow am to live for or dey regularly go brothel go face fine (money wey person go pay) of ₦100, or prison for 6 months, or both. If, for trial of person wey dem charge under section 219 of dis Code, di facts wey dem prove allow conviction under dis section, di court fit find am guilty under dis section even if dem no charge am with am.

sections.title: Restriction on defence of reasonable belief
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text: Notwithstanding anything contained in sections 220, 221 and 222, it shall only be a defence to a charge of any of the offences defined in sections 219, 221 (1) and 222 of this Code to prove that the accused person believed, on reasonable grounds, that the girl was of or above the age of sixteen years if the accused person was under the age of 21 years at the time when the offence is alleged to have been committed and has not previously been charged with any of such offences.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say, despite sections 220, 221 and 222, e go be defence (reason wey di law accept) to charge under section 219, 221 (1) or 222 of dis Code, to prove say di accused believe, on reasonable grounds, say di girl na 16 years or more, only if di accused never reach 21 years when di crime happen and dem never charge am before with any of such crimes.

sections.title: Procuration
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who
(1) procures a girl or woman who is under the age of eighteen years to have unlawful carnal connection with any other person or persons either in Nigeria or elsewhere; or
(2) procures a woman or girl to become a common prostitute either in Nigeria or elsewhere; or
(3) procures a woman or girl to leave Nigeria with intent that she may become an inmate of a brothel elsewhere; or
(4) procures a woman or girl to leave her usual place of abode in Nigeria, with intent that she may, for the purposes of prostitution, become an inmate of a brothel either in Nigeria or elsewhere, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
A person cannot be convicted of any of the offences defined in this section of this Code upon the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
The offender may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about procuration. Person wey procure girl or woman wey never reach 18 years to get unlawful carnal connection with another person or persons, for Nigeria or elsewhere; or procure woman or girl to become common prostitute, for Nigeria or elsewhere; or procure woman or girl to leave Nigeria so dat she go become inmate of brothel elsewhere; or procure woman or girl to leave her usual place of abode for Nigeria so dat she go, for prostitution, become inmate of brothel for Nigeria or elsewhere, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Di court no fit find person guilty only because one witness testify and no other evidence support am. Police fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Procuring defilement of woman by threats or fraud, or administering drugs
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) by threats or intimidation of any kind procures a woman or girl, to have unlawful carnal connection with a man either in Nigeria or elsewhere; or
(2) by any false pretence procures a woman or girl to have unlawful carnal connection with a man either in Nigeria or elsewhere; or
(3) administers to a woman or girl, or causes a woman or girl, to take, any drug or other thing with intent to stupefy or overpower her in order to enable any man, whether a particular man or not, to have unlawful carnal knowledge of her, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
A person cannot be convicted of any of the offences defined m this section upon the uncorroborated testimony of one witness.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey use threats or lie to make woman or girl have sex with man for wrong way (against di law), for Nigeria or anywhere else. E also cover person wey give woman or girl any drug or other thing, or make her take am, so dat e go make her weak or no fit resist, so dat any man go fit have sex with her for wrong way. Dis na misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. But di court no fit find person guilty of any of dis crimes if na only one witness give evidence and nobody else support am.

sections.title: Abduction of girl under eighteen with intent to have carnal knowledge
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent that an unmarried girl under the age of eighteen years may be unlawfully carnally known by any man, whether a particular man or not, takes her or causes her to be taken out of the custody or protection of her father or mother, or other person having the lawful care or charge of her, and against the will of such father or mother or other person, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
It is a defence to a charge of any of the offences defined in this section of this Code to prove that the accused person believed, on reasonable grounds, that the girl was of or above the age of eighteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey take unmarried girl wey never reach 18 years comot from her father, mother or person wey di law say dey look her, against dia will, so dat any man go fit have sex with her for wrong way (against di law). E don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di accused fit show say e believe, with good reason, say di girl don reach 18 years or pass am.

sections.title: Persons trading in prostitution
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
(1) Every male person who- [30 of 1960.]
(a) knowingly lives wholly or in part on the earnings of prostitution; or
(b) in any public place persistently solicits or importunes for immoral purposes, is liable to imprisonment for two years, and in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, shall, in addition to any term of imprisonment awarded, be liable to caning.
(2) Any magistrate who is satisfied, by evidence upon oath, that there is reason to suspect that any premises or any part of any premises are or is used by a female for purposes of prostitution, and that any male person residing in or frequenting the premises is living wholly or in part of the earnings of the prostitute, may issue a warrant under his hand authorising any constable to enter and search the premises and to arrest that male person.
(3) Where a male person is proved to live with or to be habitually in the company of a prostitute or is proved to have exercised control, direction, or influence over the movements of a prostitute in such a manner as to show that he is aiding, abetting, or compelling her prostitution with any other person or generally, he shall, unless he can satisfy the court to the contrary, be deemed to be knowingly living on the earnings of prostitution.
(4) Every female who is proved to have, for the purposes of gain, exercised control, direction or influence over the movements of a prostitute in such a manner as to show that she is aiding, abetting or compelling her prostitution with any person or generally, is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about people wey dey gain from prostitution. Man wey sabi say e dey live wholly or partly on money from prostitution, or wey dey call people again and again for public place for immoral purposes, go face prison for 2 years. If di court find am guilty for second time or more, e fit also get caning. If man dey live with prostitute, or dey control her movement to help or force her prostitution, di court go take am say e sabi say e dey live on her money, unless e show say no be so. Woman wey control prostitute movement for gain to help or force her prostitution go face prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Keeping a brothel
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Whoever-
(a) keeps or manages or assists in the management of a brothel; or
(b) being the tenant, lessee, or occupier or person in charge of any premises, knowingly permits such premises or any part thereof to be used as a brothel or for the purposes of habitual prostitution; or
(c) being the lessor or landlord of any premises, or the agent of such lessor or landlord, lets the same or any part thereof with the knowledge that such premises or some part thereof are or is to be used as a brothel, or is wilfully a party to the continued use of such premises or any part thereof as a brothel, is liable-
(i) to a fine of one hundred naira or to imprisonment for six months; and
(ii) on a second or subsequent conviction, to a fine of three hundred naira or to imprisonment for one year, or in either case, to both such fine and imprisonment.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about keeping brothel. E cover person wey keep, manage or help manage brothel; tenant, occupier or person in charge of premises wey as e sabi say allow am to dey used as brothel or for habitual prostitution; and landlord, lessor or dia agent wey let premises as e sabi say dem go use am as brothel, or on purpose join to continue di use. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 100 naira or prison for 6 months. For second time or more, di punishment na fine of 300 naira or prison for 1 year. For either case, di court fit give both fine and prison.

sections.title: Unlawful detention with intent to defile, or in a brothel
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) detains a woman or girl against her will in or upon any premises in order to her being unlawfully carnally known by any man, whether a particular man or not; or
(2) detains a woman or girl against her will in a brothel, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
When a woman or girl is in or upon any premises in order to her being unlawfully carnally known by any man, whether a particular man or not, or is in a brothel, a person is deemed to detain such woman or girl in or upon such premises in order to her being so unlawfully carnally known or to detain her in such brothel if, with intent to compel or induce her to remain in or upon the premises or in the brothel, he withholds from her any wearing apparel or other property belonging to her, or if, after wearing apparel has been lent or otherwise supplied to the woman or girl by or by the direction of such person or any other person, he threatens the woman or girl with legal proceedings if she takes away with her the wearing apparel so lent or supplied.
It is lawful for a woman or girl to take any such wearing apparel as may be necessary to enable her to leave a brothel or any premises in or upon which she is in order to her being unlawfully carnally known by any man.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about holding woman or girl against her will. If person hold her for any premises so dat any man go fit have sex with her for wrong way (against di law), or hold her for brothel, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Di law say person dey hold her if e hide her clothes or other property wey be hers to make her stay, or if e threaten her with legal case if she carry clothes wey dem lend or give her. But e dey for right way (di law allow am) for her to take di clothes wey she need to comot from di brothel or premises.

sections.title: Conspiracy to defile
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who conspires with another to induce any woman or girl, by means of any false pretence or other fraudulent means, to permit any man to have unlawful carnal knowledge of her, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about people wey plan together to lie or cheat so dat woman or girl go allow man have sex with her for wrong way (against di law). E don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Attempts to procure abortion
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to procure miscarriage of a woman, whether she is or is not with child, unlawfully administers to her or causes her to take any poison or other noxious thing, or uses any force of any kind, or uses any other means whatever, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to cause miscarriage for woman. If person wey wan make woman lose her pregnancy, whether she dey pregnant or not, give her poison or any bad thing for wrong way (against di law), or use any force or any other way, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Attempt to procure own miscarriage
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text: Any woman who, with intent to procure her own miscarriage, whether she is or is not with child, unlawfully administers to herself any poison or other noxious thing, or uses any force of any kind, or uses any other means whatever, or permits any such thing or means to be administered or used to her is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about woman wey try cause her own miscarriage. If woman wey wan lose her pregnancy, whether she dey pregnant or not, take poison or any bad thing for wrong way (against di law), or use force or any other way on herself, or allow person do am to her, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Supplying drugs or instruments to procure abortion
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully supplies to or procures for any person any thing whatever, knowing that it is intended to be unlawfully used to procure the miscarriage of a woman, whether she is or is not with child is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about giving person anything wey dem go use cause miscarriage. If person for wrong way (against di law) give or get anything for another person, as e sabi say dem wan use am cause miscarriage for woman for wrong way, whether she dey pregnant or not, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Indecent acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) wilfully and without lawful excuse does any indecent act in any public place; or
(2) wilfully does any indecent act in any place with intent to insult or offend any person, is guilty of a misdemeanour and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about indecent acts. If person on purpose do indecent act for public place without good reason, or on purpose do indecent act for any place so dat e go insult or upset another person, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Knowledge of age immaterial
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text: Except as otherwise expressly stated, it is immaterial, in the case of any of the offences defined in this Chapter committed with respect to a woman or girl under a specified age, that the accused person did not know that the woman or girl was under that age or believed that she was not under that age.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain say for di crimes for dis Chapter wey concern woman or girl wey never reach one particular age, e no matter if di accused no sabi say she never reach dat age, or e think say she don reach am. But if di law talk another thing clearly for dat section, dat one go apply.

sections.title: Deportation of non-citizens of Nigeria
sections.chapter: Chapter 21: Offences against morality
sections.text:
(1) Any person not being a citizen of Nigeria shall, upon conviction of an offence against section 219, 222A, 222B, 223, 225A, or 225B of this Code, be liable to be deported by order of the Minister, and the provisions of the Immigration Act shall apply, mutatis mutandis, in the case of a deportation under this section. [L.N. 139 of 1965.1967 No. 27.1963 No.6. Cap. 11.]
(2) Where any person being a citizen of Nigeria is deported from any British possession to Nigeria under the provisions of any law of such possession and for offences similar to the offences contained in section 219, 222A, 222B, 223, 225A, or 225B of this Code, such person may, on arrival in Nigeria, be kept temporarily in custody and returned under police escort to the place in Nigeria to which such person belongs.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sending away people wey no be citizen of Nigeria. If person wey no be citizen of Nigeria, di court find am guilty of crime under section 219, 222A, 222B, 223, 225A or 225B of dis Code, di Minister fit order make dem deport am, and di Immigration Act go apply with di changes wey dey needed. If Nigerian citizen dem deport comot from any British possession come Nigeria for crime wey resemble dem, dem fit keep am for custody for small time when e reach Nigeria, then police escort am go di place for Nigeria wey e belong.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 21A: Obscene publications
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin some words mean for dis Chapter. 'Article' mean anything wey person fit look at or read, and e include film or record of picture, and sound recording. 'Distribute' include to share around, lend, sell, give for hire, or offer to sell or hire. 'Projects', for article wey person go look at or hear, include to show or play am.

sections.title: Test of obscenity
sections.chapter: Chapter 21A: Obscene publications
sections.text:
(1) An article shall be deemed to be obscene for the purposes of this Chapter if its effect taken as a whole is such as to tend to deprave and corrupt persons who are likely, having regard to all relevant circumstances, to read, see or hear the matter contained or embodied in it. [1961 No. 51.]
(2) The provisions of this section of this Code shall extend to any article of two or more distinct items the effect of anyone of which is such as to tend to deprave and corrupt; but nothing in this section shall apply to exhibitions in private houses to which the public are not admitted or to anything done in the course of television or sound broadcasting.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about how to know if article dey obscene. Article dey obscene if, as one whole, e fit make people wey likely go read, see or hear am spoil dia good behaviour. If article get two or more separate items, and any one of dem fit do dat kind thing, di rule still apply. But e no apply to shows for private houses wey public no fit enter, or to anything wey dem do for television or radio broadcast.

sections.title: Prohibition of publication of obscene matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 21A: Obscene publications
sections.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Chapter, any person who, whether for gain or not, distributes or projects any article deemed to be obscene for the purposes of this Chapter, commits an offence punishable on conviction by a fine not exceeding four hundred naira or by imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or by both. [1961 No. 51.]
(2) A person shall not be convicted of an offence against this section of this Code if he proves that he had not examined the article in respect of which he is charged and had no reasonable cause to suspect that it was such that his publication of it would make him liable to be convicted of an offence against this section of this Code.
(3) In any proceedings against a person under this section of this Code, the question whether an article is obscene shall be determined without regard to any publication by another person unless it could reasonably have been expected that the publication by the other person would follow from publication by the person charged.
(4) No prosecution for an offence against this section of this Code shall be commenced more than two years after the commission of the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sharing or showing obscene things. If person, for gain or not, share or show article wey dem count as obscene, e don commit crime. Di punishment na fine of not more than 400 naira, or prison for not more than 3 years, or both. No case fit start for dis crime after 2 years since e happen. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di person fit show say e never check di article and no get good reason to suspect say e go put am for trouble.

sections.title: Power of search and seizure
sections.chapter: Chapter 21A: Obscene publications
sections.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Chapter, if a magistrate is satisfied by information on oath that there is reasonable ground for suspecting that articles deemed to be obscene for the purposes of this Chapter are, or are from time to time, kept for publication for gain in any premises or on any stall or vehicle in the State, the magistrate may issue a warrant under his hand empowering any constable to enter (if need be by force) and search the premises, or to search the stall or vehicle, within fourteen days from the date of the warrant, and to seize and remove any articles found therein or thereon which the constable has reason to believe to be obscene articles for the purposes of this Chapter and to be kept for publication for gain. [1961 No. 51.]
(2) A warrant under subsection (1) of this section shall, if any obscene articles are seized under the warrant, also empower the seizure and removal of any documents found in the premises or, as the case may be, on the stall or vehicle which relate to a trade or business carried on at the premises or from the stall or vehicle.
(3) Articles seized under subsection (1) of this section may, be brought before the magistrate who issued the warrant or before any other magistrate and the magistrate before whom the articles are brought may thereupon issue a summons to the occupier of the premises, or as the case may be, the user of the stall or vehicle, to appear on a day specified in the summons before a magistrate's court, to show cause why the articles or any of them should not be forfeited. If the court is satisfied, as respects any of the articles, that at the time when they were seized they were obscene articles kept for publication for gain, the court shall order those articles to be forfeited; but no order shall be made under this subsection in default of appearance by the person summoned unless service of the summons is proved.
(4) In addition to the person summoned, any other person being the owner, author or maker of any of the articles brought before the court, or any other person through whose hand they had passed before being seized, shall be entitled to appear before the court on the day specified in the summons to show cause why they should not be forfeited.
(5) Where an order is made under this section of this Code for the forfeiture of any articles, any person who appeared, or was entitled to appear, to show cause against the making of the order, may appeal to the High Court; and no such order shall take effect until the expiration of fourteen days after the day on which the order is made, or, if before the expiration thereof notice of appeal is duly given, until the final determination or abandonment of the proceedings on the appeal.
(6) If, as respects any articles brought before it, the court does not order forfeiture, the court may if it thinks fit, order the person on whose information the warrant for the seizure of the articles was issued to pay such costs as the court thinks reasonable to any person who has appeared before the court to show cause why those articles should not be forfeited; and costs ordered to be paid under this subsection shall be enforceable as a civil debt.
(7) For the purposes of this section of this Code, the question whether an article is obscene shall be determined on the assumption that copies of it would be published in any manner likely having regard to the circumstances in which it was found, but in no other manner.
(8) Nothing in this section shall be construed to preclude the making of any order for the purposes of section 263 of the Criminal Procedure Act (which relates to disposal of property produced before a court). [Cap. C41.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about power to search for and seize obscene articles. If magistrate believe, from information wey person swear for oath, say dem dey keep obscene articles for publication for gain for any premises, stall or vehicle for di State, e fit give warrant make constable enter (with force if need be), search within 14 days, and seize di articles and documents about di trade or business. Magistrate fit summon di occupier or user to court to show why dem no go forfeit (take comot) di articles. Owner, author, maker or anybody wey handle di articles fit also appear. If court order forfeiture, person fit appeal to High Court, and di order no go work until 14 days pass or di appeal finish. If court no order forfeiture, e fit order di person wey give information to pay reasonable costs. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Defence of public good
sections.chapter: Chapter 21A: Obscene publications
sections.text:
(1) No person shall be convicted of an offence against this Chapter, and no order for forfeiture shall be made if it is proved that the publication of the article in question is justified as being for the public good on the ground that it is in the interests of science, literature, art or learning, or of other objects of general concern. [1961 No. 51.]
(2) It is hereby declared that the opinion of experts as to the literary, artistic, scientific or other merits of an article may be admitted in any proceedings under this Chapter either to establish or to negative the said ground.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defence (reason wey di law accept) of public good for obscene publications. Nobody go be found guilty of crime under dis Chapter, and court no go order forfeiture, if e dey proved say to publish di article na for public good, because e help science, literature, art or learning, or other things wey concern everybody. Experts fit give dia opinion for court about di literary, artistic, scientific or other value of di article, to support or reject dis reason.

sections.title: Common nuisances
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) obstructs any highway, by any permanent work or erection thereon or injury thereto, which renders the highway less commodious to the public than it would otherwise be; or
(b) prevents the public from having access to any part of a highway by an excessive and unreasonable temporary use thereof, or by so dealing with the land in the immediate neighbourhood of the highway as to prevent the public from using and enjoying it securely; or
(c) does not repair a highway which he is bound to repair; or
(d) does not repair a bridge which he is bound to repair; or
(e) wilfully diverts or obstructs the course of any navigable river so as to appreciably diminish its convenience for purposes of navigation; or
(f) does any act not warranted by law, or omits to discharge any legal duty, which act or omission obstructs or causes inconvenience or damage to the public in the exercise of rights common to the public, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
It is immaterial whether the act complained of is convenient to a larger number of the public than it inconveniences, but the fact that the act complained of facilitates the lawful exercise of their rights by a part of the public, may show that it is not a nuisance to any of the public.
The owner of a vessel wrecked in a navigable river is not guilty of a common nuisance because he does not remove it.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about common nuisance. Person don commit misdemeanour (small crime) if e block highway with permanent work or damage; stop public from using any part of highway by too much temporary use; no repair highway or bridge wey e suppose repair; on purpose block or turn navigable river so dat ships no fit use am well; or do any act wey law no allow, or no do legal duty, wey block public or cause dem trouble or damage for rights wey everybody share. Di punishment na prison for 2 years. E no matter if di act help more people pass di ones wey e disturb. Owner of vessel wey wreck for navigable river no commit nuisance because e no remove am.

sections.title: Gaming houses
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
(1) A person being the owner or occupier, or having the use of, any house, room or place, who shall open, keep or use the same for the purpose of unlawful gaming being carried on therein, and any person who, being the owner or occupier of any house, room or place, shall knowingly and wilfully permit the same to be opened, kept or used by any other person for the purpose aforesaid, and any person having the care or management of or in any manner assisting in conducting the business of any house, room or place opened, kept or used for the purpose aforesaid, is said to keep a common gaming house.
Unlawful gaming
(2) In this section, "unlawful gaming" includes roulette, every game of dice except backgammon, every game of card which is not a game of skill, the game known as chacha and other games of cowries, and any game the chances of which are not alike favourable to all the players, including the banker or other person or persons by whom the game is managed or against whom the other players stake, play or bet.
(3) Any person who keeps a common gaming house is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to a fine of one thousand naira or to imprisonment for two years or to both such fine and imprisonment.
(4) Any person other than the persons mentioned in subsection (1) of this section who is found in a common gaming house shall be deemed, unless the contrary is proved, to be there for the purpose of unlawful gaming and is guilty of an offence and liable to a fine of ten naira for the first offence and for each subsequent offence to a fine of forty naira or imprisonment for three months or to both such fine and imprisonment.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about gaming houses. Person wey own, occupy or use house, room or place and open, keep or use am for unlawful gaming, or as e sabi say and on purpose allow another person do am, or manage or help run di business, dey keep common gaming house. Unlawful gaming include roulette, dice games except backgammon, card games wey no be game of skill, chacha and other cowrie games, and any game wey chances no equal for all players. Person wey keep common gaming house don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 1000 naira, or prison for 2 years, or both. Any other person wey dem find inside don commit crime: fine of 10 naira for first time, and next time fine of 40 naira or prison for 3 months or both.

sections.title: Police may be authorised to enter gaming houses, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
(1) A superior police officer or an administrative officer in charge of police, if he has reasonable grounds for believing that any house, room or place is kept as a common gaming house, may by order in writing authorise any police officer to enter and search such house, room or place at any time and if necessary, to use force for the purpose of effecting such entry, whether by breaking open doors or otherwise, and to arrest all persons who shall be found therein, and to seize all instruments of gaming found in such house or premises and to seize all money found therein.
Obstructing entry of police to be evidence of unlawful gaming
(2) Where a police officer so authorised to enter any house, room or place is wilfully prevented from or obstructed or delayed in entering the same or any part thereof, or where any external or internal door of, or means of access to, any such house, room or place shall be found to be fitted or provided with any bolt, bar, chains or any means or contrivance for the purpose of preventing, delaying or obstructing the entry into the same or any part thereof of any police officer authorised as aforesaid or for giving an alarm in the case of such entry, or if any such house, room or place is found fitted or provided with any means or contrivance for unlawful gaming or with any means of contrivance for concealing, removing or destroying any instruments of gaming, it shall be evidence until the contrary be proved, that such house, room or place is used as a common gaming house within the meaning of section 236 of this Code and that the persons found therein were unlawfully playing therein.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about police power to enter gaming houses. Superior police officer or administrative officer in charge of police wey believe, with good reason, say place na common gaming house fit order police officer to enter and search am any time, use force if need be, arrest everybody inside, and seize all gaming instruments and money. If dem block or delay di officer on purpose, or di doors get bolts, bars or chains to block am, or di place get tools for unlawful gaming, dat one na evidence, until person prove otherwise, say na common gaming house under section 236 of dis Code.

sections.title: Indemnity of witnesses
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text: Any person who shall be called to give evidence against any other person charged under the provisions of section 236 of this Code shall be freed from all criminal prosecution in respect of the offence with which such other person is charged or any other offence under section 236 of this Code.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell say person wey dem call to give evidence against another person wey dem charge under section 236 of dis Code, no go face prosecution for di crime wey dem charge di other person with, or for any other crime under section 236 of dis Code.

sections.title: Betting houses
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
Any house, room, or place, which is used for any of the following purposes-
(1) for the purpose of bets being made therein between persons resorting to the place and-
(a) the owner, occupier, or keeper of the place, or any person using the place; or
(b) any person procured or employed by or acting for or on behalf of any such owner, occupier, or keeper, or person using the place; or
(c) any person having the care or management, or in any manner conducting the business, of the place; or
(2) for the purpose of any money or other property, being paid or received therein by or on behalf of any such owner, occupier, or keeper, or person using the place as, or for the consideration-
(a) for an assurance, undertaking, promise, or agreement, express or implied, to payor give thereafter any money or other property on any event or contingency of or relating to any horse race, or other race, fight, game sport, or exercise; or
(b) for securing the paying or giving by some other person of any money or other property on any such event or contingency, is called a common betting house.
Any person who, being the owner or occupier of any house, room, or place, knowingly and wilfully permits it to be opened, kept, or used, as a common betting house by another person, or who has the use or management, or assists in conducting the business of a common betting house, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year, and to a fine of one thousand naira:
Provided always that nothing herein contained shall make illegal the use of a totalisator by a race club recognised by the Government, at a race meeting, with the approval in each case, of the superintendent of police in charge of the area where the meeting is held. In this proviso "totalisator" means and includes the instrument, machine, or contrivance, commonly known as the totalisator, and any other instrument, machine, or contrivance of a like nature, or any scheme for enabling any number of persons to make bets with one another on the like principles.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin common betting house be and di punishment. House, room or place na common betting house if dem use am for people to bet with di owner, occupier, keeper or person wey use di place, or with person wey dey act for dem; or for money or property to dey paid or received for promise to pay on horse race, other race, fight, game, sport or exercise. Owner or occupier wey as e sabi say and on purpose allow another person use di place as common betting house, or wey use, manage or help run am, don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year and fine (money wey person go pay) of 1000 naira. But e no be crime if race club wey Government recognise use totalisator for race meeting. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Pool betting
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
(1) (Inserted by 44 of 1958 repealed by 1961 No. 69).
(2) (Inserted by 44 of 1958 repealed by 1961 No. 69).
(3) For the purpose of section 239 of this Code any house, room or place which is used for the purpose of a licensed pool betting business shall not be deemed to be a common betting house by reason only that it is so used. [44 of 1958.1961 No. 69.]
(4) (Inserted by 44 of 1958 repealed by 1961 No. 69).
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about pool betting. For di purpose of section 239 of dis Code, house, room or place wey dem use for licensed pool betting business no go be common betting house just because dem use am for dat. Di other parts of dis section don dey removed.

sections.title: Definitions: lottery: lottery ticket: public lottery
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin some words mean for dis Chapter. 'Lottery' include any game, way or thing wey dem use share or give money or money worth by chance or lot. 'Lottery ticket' include any paper, ticket, token or other thing wey give person, or look like say e give person, right to collect money or money worth when any event connected with public lottery happen. 'Public lottery' na lottery wey public or any group of di public fit join, and dem go count every lottery as public lottery until person prove say no be so.

sections.title: Offences relating to lotteries
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) gives or sells or offers for sale or delivers any lottery ticket or pays or receives directly or indirectly any money or money's worth for or in respect of any chance in or event or contingency connected with a public lottery; or
(b) draws, throws, declares or exhibits, expressly or otherwise, the winner or winning number, ticket, lot, figure, design, symbol, or other result of any public lottery; or
(c) writes, prints, publishes, or causes to be written, printed, or published, any lottery ticket, or any announcement relating to a public lottery; or
(d) advances, furnishes, or receives money for the purpose of a public lottery; or
(e) in any manner carries on, or assists in carrying on, or invites or solicits any person to take part in, a public lottery, is liable to a fine not exceeding one hundred naira or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wetin person no fit do for public lottery. E cover person wey give, sell, offer to sell or deliver lottery ticket, or pay or receive money or money worth for chance for public lottery; or draw, declare or show di winner, winning number or any result; or write, print or publish lottery ticket or announcement about public lottery, or cause am; or give, supply or receive money for public lottery; or run, help run, invite or ask anybody to join public lottery. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of not more than 100 naira, or prison for not more than 6 months.

sections.title: Recovery of money paid for lottery tickets
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text: Any money or money's worth paid or deposited for or in respect of the purchase of a lottery ticket shall be recoverable as money had and received to the use of the person by whom the same was paid or deposited.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about getting back money wey person pay for lottery ticket. Any money or money worth wey person pay or put down to buy lottery ticket, di person wey pay fit collect am back.

sections.title: Contracting for sale of lottery ticket void
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text: Every sale or contract for the sale of a lottery ticket is hereby declared to be void, and no action shall be maintainable by any person in respect of any such sale or contract, except by the purchaser for the return of the money or other consideration (if any) paid thereon.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say any sale or contract to sell lottery ticket no get force for law (void). Nobody fit take case to court about am, except di buyer wey wan get back di money or other thing wey e pay for am.

sections.title: Saving of certain race club lotteries and sweepstakes
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
(1) Nothing in this Chapter contained shall apply to any lottery or sweepstake organised and controlled by any race club in Nigeria to which a minister may by notice in the Federal Gazette extend the provisions of this section of this Code, at or in connection with any race meeting held under the auspices of any club or association. [L.N. 257 of 1959.]
(2) Nothing in this Chapter contained shall apply to or prevent the sale by raffle or lottery of articles exposed for sale at any bazaar or fancy fair held for raising funds in aid of any institution of a public character, provided that permission for such sale shall have been given in writing by the Minister.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about lotteries wey dis Chapter no apply to. First, di Chapter no apply to lottery or sweepstake wey race club for Nigeria organise and control for race meeting, if minister don extend dis section to dat club by notice for di Federal Gazette. Second, di Chapter no stop sale by raffle or lottery of things wey dem put for sale for bazaar or fancy fair to raise money for public institution, if di Minister don give permission for writing before.

sections.title: Lotteries carried on in clubs with approval of Minister
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
(1) A Minister may grant to any club a licence authorising a lottery to be promoted and carried on, subject to any conditions contained in the licence, as an incident of entertainment by members of the club on the premises of the club. [L.N. 257 of 1959.]
(2) It shall be a condition of every licence granted to a club under subsection (1) of this section in respect of a lottery that only members of the club and their guests introduced in accordance with the rules of the club shall have access to the lottery.
(3) A lottery promoted and carried on in a club in accordance with the terms of a licence issued under this section of this Code shall not be deemed to be a public lottery.
(4) When any condition of a licence granted under this section of this Code is contravened, every person concerned in the promotion or carrying on of the lottery is guilty of an offence, unless he proves that the contravention was committed without his knowledge, and liable on summary conviction to a fine of forty naira or to imprisonment for four months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about licence for clubs to run lottery. Minister fit give club licence to run lottery, with di conditions wey dey inside di licence, as part of entertainment by members for di club premises. Di licence must say say na only club members and dia guests wey dem bring according to di club rules fit join. Lottery wey dem run for dis way no be public lottery. If any condition of di licence no dey followed, everybody wey dey involved for di lottery don commit crime, unless e prove say e happen without im knowledge. If di court find am guilty, di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 40 naira or prison for 4 months.

sections.title: Acting as keeper of brothels, gaming houses and betting houses
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text: Any person who appears, acts, or behaves, as master or mistress, or as the person having the care or management of any such premises, house, room, set of rooms, or place, as is mentioned in section 225B, 236 or 239 of this Code, is to be taken to be the keeper thereof, whether he is or is not the real keeper.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about who dem go count as keeper of brothel, gaming house or betting house. Person wey appear, act or behave like master or mistress, or like person wey dey look after or manage any place mentioned for section 225B, 236 or 239 of dis Code, dem go take am as di keeper, even if no be im be di real keeper.

sections.title: Misconduct with regard to corpses
sections.chapter: Chapter 22: Nuisances: gaming houses; lotteries; misconduct relating to corpses
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) without lawful justification or excuse, the proof of which lies on him-
(a) neglects to perform any duty imposed upon him by law, or undertaken by him, whether for reward or otherwise, touching the burial or other disposition of a human body or human remains; or
(b) improperly or indecently interferes with, or offers any indignity to, any dead human body or human remains, whether buried or not;
(2) eats or receive for the purpose of eating any part of a dead human body, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wrong things wey person do with dead body. If person, without good reason wey e must prove, no do duty wey law give am or wey e take on, with pay or without pay, about di burial or other handling of dead human body or remains; or improperly or indecently touch or disrespect dead human body or remains, buried or not buried; or eat, or collect to eat, any part of dead human body, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Exposing for sale things unfit for food or drink
sections.chapter: Chapter 23: Offence against public health
sections.text:
(1) Any person who sells, as food or drink, or has in his possession with intent to sell it as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale
