(2) Any person who adulterates any article of food or drink, so as to make such article noxious as food or drink, intending to sell such article as food or drink or knowing it to be likely that the same will be sold as food or drink, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about selling food or drink wey no good. If person sell as food or drink, or keep to sell as food or drink, anything wey don turn harmful or wey no fit be food or drink, as e sabi say or get reason to believe say e dey so, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Person wey mix anything for food or drink to make am harmful, wey wan sell am or sabi say dem fit sell am, don also commit misdemeanour. Di punishment for each one na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Dealing in diseased meat
sections.chapter: Chapter 23: Offence against public health
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) knowingly takes into a slaughter-house used for the slaughter of any animals intended for the food of man the whole or any part of the carcass of any animal which has died of any disease; or
(2) knowingly sells the whole or part of the carcass of any animal which has died of any disease or which was diseased when slaughtered, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about diseased meat. If person as e sabi say carry di whole or part of body of animal wey die from sickness enter slaughter-house wey dem use to kill animals for people to eat, or as e sabi say sell di whole or part of body of animal wey die from sickness or wey get sickness when dem kill am, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Fouling water
sections.chapter: Chapter 23: Offence against public health
sections.text: Any person who corrupts or fouls the water of any spring, stream, well, tank, reservoir, or place, so as to render it less fit for the purpose for which it is ordinarily used, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for six months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about spoiling water. If person spoil or dirty di water for spring, stream, well, tank, reservoir or any place so dat e no good again for wetin dem normally use am for, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 6 months.

sections.title: Burials in houses
sections.chapter: Chapter 23: Offence against public health
sections.text: Any person who without the consent of the President or the Governor buries or attempts to bury any corpse in any house, building premises, yard, garden, compound, or within a hundred yards of any dwelling-house, or in any open space situated within a township, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for six months. [L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about burying dead body for wrong place. If person, without agreement (say 'yes') of di President or di Governor, bury or try to bury corpse for any house, building, yard, garden or compound, or within 100 yards of any dwelling-house, or for any open space inside township, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 6 months.

sections.title: Noxious acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 23: Offence against public health
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) vitiates the atmosphere in any place so as to make it noxious to the health of persons in general dwelling or carrying on business in the neighbourhood or passing along a public way; or
(b) does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, whether human or animal, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for six months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about noxious acts. If person spoil di air for any place so dat e go dey harmful to health of people wey dey stay or do business near am, or pass di public way, or do any act wey e sabi or get reason to believe say fit spread infection of disease wey fit kill, for human or animal, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 6 months.

sections.title: Sale of matches made with white phosphorus: use of white phosphorus in manufacture of matches
sections.chapter: Chapter 23: Offence against public health
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) sells or has in his possession for the purposes of sale any matches made with white (yellow) phosphorus; or
(b) uses white (yellow) phosphorus in the manufacture of matches, is guilty of an offence and liable to a fine of twenty naira, and any matches in respect of which the offence shall have been committed shall be forfeited.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about matches wey dem make with white phosphorus. If person sell, or keep to sell, matches wey dem make with white (yellow) phosphorus, or use white (yellow) phosphorus to make matches, e don commit crime. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 20 naira, and dem go take di matches wey dey involved.

sections.title: Idle and disorderly persons
sections.chapter: Chapter 24: Idle and disorderly persons; rogues and vagabonds; bringing contempt on uniform
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about who dem count as idle and disorderly persons. Dem be: common prostitute wey dey behave for disorderly or indecent way for public place, or dey hang around and keep calling people for prostitution; person wey dey go about for public place or stay there to beg, or cause or encourage child or children to do am; person wey dey play game of chance for money or money worth for public place; and person wey, for public place, behave for way wey fit cause breach of di peace. Police fit arrest dem without court paper (warrant). Dem don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 month.

sections.title: Rogues and vagabonds
sections.chapter: Chapter 24: Idle and disorderly persons; rogues and vagabonds; bringing contempt on uniform
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about who dem count as rogues and vagabonds. Dem include: person wey di court find guilty under section 249 of dis Code after dem don find am guilty before as idle and disorderly person; person wey use wounds or body deformity to collect alms; person wey collect alms or charity contribution with lie or cheating; suspected person or known thief wey no get visible way to live and no fit give good account of imself; person wey control prostitute movement to help or control her prostitution; and person wey dem find for place or time wey show say e dey there for illegal or disorderly purpose. Dem don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 months for first time, and 1 year for each next time. Police fit arrest dem without court paper (warrant). Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Bringing contempt on uniform
sections.chapter: Chapter 24: Idle and disorderly persons; rogues and vagabonds; bringing contempt on uniform
sections.text: Any person who, not being a person serving in any of the armed or police forces of Nigeria, wears the uniform of any of these forces, or any dress having the appearance or bearing any of the regimental or other distinctive marks of any such uniform, in such manner or in such circumstances as to be likely to bring contempt on that uniform, or employs any other person so to wear such uniform or dress, is guilty of a simple offence, and is liable to imprisonment for three months or to a fine of forty naira. [L.N. 112 of 1964.] Part 5 Offences against the person and relating to marriage and parental rights and duties, and against the reputation of individuals
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wearing police or army uniform for way wey bring disrespect. If person wey no dey serve for di armed forces or police forces of Nigeria wear dia uniform, or any dress wey look like am or get dia marks, for way wey fit make people disrespect di uniform, or hire another person to wear am like dat, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 months or fine (money wey person go pay) of 40 naira.

sections.title: Definition of assault
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
A person who strikes, touches, or moves, or otherwise applies force of any kind to the person of another, either directly or indirectly, without his consent, or with his consent, if the consent is obtained by fraud, or who by any bodily act or gesture attempts or threatens to apply force of any kind to the person of another without his consent, in such circumstances that the person making the attempt or threat has actually or apparently a present ability to effect his purpose, is said to assault that other person, and the act is called an assault.
The term "applies force" includes the case of applying heat, light, electrical force, gas, odour, or any other substance of thing whatever, if applied in such a degree as to cause injury or personal discomfort.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin assault mean. Person dey assault another person if e hit, touch, move or use any force on am, directly or indirectly, without agreement (say 'yes'), or if di agreement come by cheating. E also be assault if person use body act or sign to try or threaten to use force on another person without agreement, and e get power, or e look like say e get power, to do am for dat time. To use force include to use heat, light, electricity, gas, smell or any other thing, if e reach level wey fit cause injury or discomfort.

sections.title: Assaults unlawful
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
An assault is unlawful and constitutes an offence unless it is authorised or justified or excused by law.
The application of force by one person to the person of another may be unlawful, although it is done with the consent of that other person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about assault wey no dey allowed. Assault na crime for wrong way (against di law) unless law allow, justify or excuse am. Even if another person agree (say 'yes'), to use force on person body fit still be for wrong way.

sections.title: Execution of sentence
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for a person who is charged by law with the duty of executing or giving effect to the lawful sentence of a court (including a customary and an area court) to execute or give effect to that sentence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about carrying out court sentence. Person wey di law give duty to carry out di lawful sentence of court, including customary court and area court, fit do am for right way (di law allow am).

sections.title: Execution of process
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for a person who is charged by law with the duty of executing the lawful process of a court (including a customary and an area court) and who is required to arrest or detain another person under such process, and for every person lawfully assisting a person so charged, to arrest or detain that other person according to the terms of the process.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about carrying out court process. Person wey di law give duty to carry out lawful process of court, including customary court and area court, and wey dem require to arrest or hold another person under am, fit arrest or hold dat person as di process talk, for right way (di law allow am). Di same go for every person wey lawfully help am.

sections.title: Execution of warrant
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for a person who is charged by law with the duty of executing a lawful warrant issued by any court (including customary and an area court) or judicial officer, or other person having jurisdiction to issue it, and who is required to arrest or detain another person under such warrant, and for every person lawfully assisting a person so charged, to arrest or detain that other person according to the directions of the warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about carrying out warrant. Person wey di law give duty to carry out lawful warrant wey any court (including customary court and area court), judicial officer or other person wey get power give, and wey dem require to arrest or hold another person under am, fit arrest or hold dat person as di warrant talk, for right way (di law allow am). Di same go for every person wey lawfully help am.

sections.title: Erroneous sentence or process or warrant
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: If the sentence was passed, or the process was issued, by a court (including a native tribunal) having jurisdiction under any circumstances to pass such a sentence or to issue such process, or if the warrant was issued by a court (including a customary and an area court) or judicial officer or other person having authority in any circumstances to issue such a warrant, it is immaterial whether the court or judicial officer or person had or had not authority to pass the sentence or issue the process or warrant in the particular case; unless the person executing the same knows that the sentence or process or warrant, was in fact passed or issued without authority.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sentence, process or warrant wey get error. If court (including native tribunal) wey fit pass such sentence or issue such process for any situation pass am, or if court, judicial officer or other person wey fit issue such warrant for any situation issue am, e no matter whether di court or person get power for dat particular case. But e go matter if di person wey dey carry am out sabi say dem pass or issue am without power.

sections.title: Sentence or process or warrant without jurisdiction
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: A person who executes or assists in executing any sentence, or process, or warrant which purports to be passed or issued by a court (including a native tribunal), judicial officer, or other person, and who would be justified, under the provisions of sections 254, 255, 256 and 257 of this Code, in executing the same if it had been passed or issued by a court (including a customary and an area court), or judicial officer, or person, having authority to pass or issue it, is not criminally responsible for any act done in such execution notwithstanding that the court, judicial officer or person, had no authority to pass the sentence or issue the process or warrant, if in such execution he acted in good faith and in the belief that the sentence, process or warrant was that of a court, judicial officer, or other person, having such authority.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sentence, process or warrant from person wey no get power. Person wey carry out or help carry out sentence, process or warrant wey dem say court, native tribunal, judicial officer or other person pass or issue, no go answer for crime for any act wey e do for di carrying out, even if dat court or person no get power. E go work if di act for right way (di law allow am) under sections 254, 255, 256 and 257 of dis Code if di court or person get power, and if e act for good faith and believe say di sentence, process or warrant come from person wey get such power.

sections.title: Arrest of wrong person
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
A person who, being duly authorised to execute a warrant to arrest one person, arrests another person, believing in good faith and on reasonable grounds that the person arrested is the person named in the warrant, is not criminally responsible for doing so to any greater extent than if the person arrested had been the person named in the warrant.
Any person who lawfully assists in making such an arrest believing that the person arrested is the person named in the warrant, or who, being required by the warrant to receive and detain the person named in it, receives and detains the person so arrested, is not criminally responsible for doing so to any greater extent than if the person arrested had been the person named in the warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about arresting wrong person. If person wey get authority to carry out warrant to arrest one person arrest another person, and e believe, for good faith and with good reason, say na di person wey di warrant name, e no go answer for crime more than if na di right person. Di same go for person wey lawfully help for dat kind arrest and believe say na di person wey di warrant name, and for person wey di warrant tell make e receive and hold di person wey dem name, if e receive and hold di person wey dem arrest.

sections.title: Irregular process or warrant
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When any process or warrant is bad in law by reason of some defect in substance or in form apparent on the face of it, a person who, in good faith and believing that it is good in law, acts in the execution of the process or warrant, is not criminally responsible for anything done in such execution to any greater extent than if the process or warrant were good in law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about process or warrant wey get fault. If process or warrant no good for law because of fault wey show for di face of am, for substance or form, person wey act to carry am out for good faith and believe say e good for law no go answer for crime for anything wey e do for di carrying out, more than if di process or warrant good for law.

sections.title: Force used in executing process or in arrest
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for a person who is engaged in the lawful execution of any sentence, process or warrant, or in making any arrest, and for any person lawfully assisting him, to use such force as may be reasonably necessary to overcome any force used in resisting such execution or arrest.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about use of force when dem dey carry out sentence, process or warrant, or dey arrest person. Person wey dey lawfully do any of dem, and any person wey lawfully help am, fit use force wey reasonably necessary to overcome force wey person use to resist am.

sections.title: Peace officer preventing escape from arrest
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When a peace officer or police officer is proceeding lawfully to arrest, with or without warrant, a person for an offence which is a felony, and is such that the offender may be arrested without warrant, and the person sought to be arrested takes to flight in order to avoid arrest, it is lawful for the peace officer or police officer and for any person lawfully assisting him, to use such force as may be reasonably necessary to prevent the escape of the person sought to be arrested, and, if the offence is such that the offender may be punished with death or with imprisonment for seven years or more, may kill him if he cannot by any means otherwise be arrested.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping person from running comot during arrest. If peace officer or police officer dey lawfully arrest person, with warrant or without warrant, for felony (serious crime) wey dem fit arrest without warrant, and di person run to avoid arrest, di officer, and any person wey lawfully help am, fit use force wey reasonably necessary to stop am from escape. If di crime na one wey dem fit punish with death or prison for 7 years or more, dem fit kill am if no other way dey to arrest am.

sections.title: Other cases of preventing escape from arrest
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
When a person who is not a peace officer or police officer is proceeding lawfully to arrest, without warrant, another person for an offence which is such that the offender may be arrested without warrant, and when any person is proceeding lawfully to arrest another person for any cause other than such an offence, and, in either case, the person sought to be arrested takes to flight in order to avoid arrest, it is lawful for the person seeking to arrest him to use such force as may be reasonably necessary to prevent his escape.
But this section of this Code does not authorise the use of force which is intended or is likely to cause death or grievous harm.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about other cases of stopping person from running comot during arrest. If person wey no be peace officer or police officer dey lawfully arrest another person without warrant for crime wey allow arrest without warrant, or any person dey lawfully arrest another person for any other cause, and di person run to avoid arrest, di one wey wan arrest am fit use force wey reasonably necessary to stop am from escape. But dis section no allow force wey dem wan use or fit use cause death or serious harm.

sections.title: Preventing escape or rescue after arrest
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
When any person has lawfully arrested another person for any offence, it is lawful for him to use such force as he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be necessary to prevent the escape or rescue of the person arrested.
But, if the offence is not one which is such that the offender may be arrested without warrant, this section of this Code shall not authorise the use of force which is intended or is likely to cause death or grievous harm.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping escape or rescue after arrest. When person don lawfully arrest another person for any crime, e fit use force wey e believe, with good reason, say e necessary to stop di person from escape or from dem rescue am. But if di crime no be one wey dem fit arrest without warrant, dis section no allow force wey dem wan use or fit use cause death or serious harm.

sections.title: Preventing a breach of the peace
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
It is lawful for any person who witnesses a breach of the peace to interfere to prevent the continuance or renewal of it, and to use such force as is reasonably necessary for such prevention and is reasonably proportioned to the danger to be apprehended from such continuance or renewal, and to detain any person who is committing or who is about to join in or to renew the breach of the peace for such time as may be reasonably necessary in order to give him into the custody of a peace officer or police officer.
It is lawful for a peace officer or police officer who witnesses a breach of the peace, and for any person lawfully assisting him, to arrest any person whom he finds committing it, or whom he believes on reasonable grounds to be about to join or renew the breach of the peace.
It is lawful for a peace officer or police officer to receive into custody and detain in custody any person given into his charge as having been a party to a breach of the peace by a person whom the peace officer or police officer believes, on reasonable grounds, to have witnessed the breach of the peace.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping breach of di peace. Any person wey see breach of di peace fit step in to stop am, use force wey reasonably necessary and wey match di danger, and hold anybody wey dey do am or wan join or repeat am for reasonable time to give am to peace officer or police officer. Peace officer or police officer wey see breach of di peace, and anybody wey lawfully help am, fit arrest person wey dem find dey do am, or wey dem believe, with good reason, say e wan join or repeat am. Dem fit also receive and hold person wey somebody give dem for dat breach.

sections.title: Suppression of riot
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for any person to use such force as is necessary to suppress a riot, and is reasonably proportioned to the danger to be apprehended from its continuance.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping riot. Any person fit use force wey necessary to stop riot and wey match di danger wey e fit cause if e continue.

sections.title: Suppression of riot by peace officers
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for a peace officer to use or order to be used such force as he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be necessary in order to suppress a riot, and is reasonably proportioned to the danger which he believes, on reasonable grounds, is to be apprehended from its continuance.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about peace officers stopping riot. Peace officer fit use, or order make dem use, force wey e believe, with good reason, say e necessary to stop riot and wey match di danger wey e believe, with good reason, say e fit cause if e continue.

sections.title: Suppression of riot by person acting under lawful orders
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for any person acting in good faith in obedience to orders, not manifestly unlawful, given by a peace officer for the suppression of a riot, to use such force as he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be necessary for carrying such orders into effect. Whether any particular order so given is or is not manifestly lawful, is a question of law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey obey orders to stop riot. Person wey act for good faith to obey order from peace officer to stop riot, if di order no clearly against di law, fit use force wey e believe, with good reason, say e necessary to carry di order out. Na question of law to decide whether any particular order dey clearly against di law or no be so.

sections.title: Suppression of riot by person acting without order in case of emergency
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When any person, whether subject to military law or not, believes, on reasonable grounds, that serious mischief will arise from a riot before there is time to procure the intervention of a peace officer, it is lawful for him to use such force as he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be necessary for the suppression of the riot, and as is reasonably proportioned to the danger which he believes, on reasonable grounds, is to be apprehended from its continuance.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping riot without order for emergency. If any person, whether e dey under military law or not, believe, with good reason, say serious trouble go come from riot before time reach to call peace officer, e fit use force wey e believe, with good reason, say e necessary to stop di riot and wey match di danger wey e believe, with good reason, say e fit cause if e continue.

sections.title: Riot: persons subject to Military Law or members of the Police Forces
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for a person who is bound by the laws in force relative to the Armed Forces of Nigeria or to the Police Forces to obey the lawful commands of his superior officer, to obey any command given him by his superior officer, in order to see the suppression of a riot, unless the command is manifestly unlawful. Whether any particular command is or is not manifestly unlawful, is a question of law. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about riot and people wey dey under Military Law or Police Forces. Person wey di laws for Armed Forces of Nigeria or Police Forces bind fit obey di lawful commands of im superior officer, including command to stop riot, unless di command clearly against di law. Na question of law to decide whether any particular command dey clearly against di law or no be so.

sections.title: Prevention of offences for which an offender may be arrested without warrant: prevention of violence by persons of unsound mind
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for any person to use such force as is reasonably necessary in order to prevent the commission of an offence which is such that the offender may be arrested without warrant; or in order to prevent any act from being done as to which he believes, on reasonable grounds, that it would, if done, amount to any such offence; or in order to prevent a person whom he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be of unsound mind, from doing violence to any person or property.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about preventing crimes wey allow arrest without warrant, and violence by person of unsound mind. Any person fit use force wey reasonably necessary to prevent crime wey di offender fit be arrested without warrant for; or to stop any act wey e believe, with good reason, say e go be dat kind crime if dem do am; or to stop person wey e believe, with good reason, say e dey of unsound mind from doing violence to any person or property.

sections.title: Defence of dwelling-house
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for any person who is in peaceable possession of a dwelling-house, and for any person lawfully assisting him or acting by his authority, to use such force as he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be necessary in order to prevent the forcible breaking and entering of the dwelling-house, either by night or day, by any person whom he believes on reasonable grounds, to be attempting to break and enter the dwelling-house with intent to commit a felony or misdemeanor therein.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defending dwelling-house. Person wey get peaceful possession of dwelling-house, and any person wey lawfully help am or dey act with im authority, fit use force wey e believe, with good reason, say e necessary to stop person from force break and enter di house, day or night, if e believe, with good reason, say di person wan break in to commit felony (serious crime) or misdemeanour (small crime) inside.

sections.title: Provocation
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
The term "provocation", used with reference to an offence of which an assault is an element, includes, except as hereinafter stated, any wrongful act or insult of such nature as to be likely, when done to an ordinary person, or in the presence of the ordinary person to another person who is under his immediate care, or to whom he stands in a conjugal, parental, filial, or fraternal relation, or in the relation of master or servant, to deprive him of the power of self-control, and to induce him to assault the person by whom the act or insult is done or offered.
When such an act or insult is done or offered by one person to another, or in the presence of another to a person who is under the immediate care of that other, or to whom the latter stands in any such relation as aforesaid, the former is said to give to the latter provocation for an assault.
A lawful act is not provocation to any person for an assault.
An act which a person does in consequence of excitement given by another person in order to induce him to do the act, and thereby to furnish an excuse for committing an assault, is not provocation to that person for an assault.
An arrest which is unlawful is not necessarily provocation for an assault, but it may be evidence of provocation to a person who knows of the illegality.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin provocation mean for crimes wey assault dey inside. Provocation na any wrong act or insult wey fit make ordinary person lose power to control imself and attack di person wey do am, if dem do am to am, or for presence of ordinary person to person wey dey under im care or wey e be husband, wife, parent, child, brother, sister, master or servant to. Lawful act no be provocation. Act wey person do because another person push am so dat e go get excuse to assault no be provocation. Unlawful arrest no necessarily be provocation, but e fit be evidence of provocation to person wey sabi say e no lawful.

sections.title: Defence of provocation
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
A person is not criminally responsible for an assault committed upon a person who gives him provocation for the assault, if he is in fact deprived by the provocation of the power of self-control, and acts upon it on the sudden and before there is time for his passion to cool; provided that the force used is not disproportionate to the provocation, and is not intended, and is not such as is likely, to cause death or grievous harm.
Whether any particular act or insult is such as to be likely to deprive an ordinary person of the power of self-control and to induce him to assault the person by whom the act or insult is done or offered, and whether, in any particular case, the person provoked was actually deprived by the provocation of the power of self-control, and whether any force used is or is not disproportionate to the provocation, are questions of fact.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defence (reason wey di law accept) of provocation. Person no go answer for crime for assault on person wey provoke am if di provocation truly make am lose power to control imself, and e act sudden before im anger cool down. But di force wey e use must no pass di provocation, and must no be force wey e wan use or fit use cause death or serious harm. Whether act or insult fit make ordinary person lose control, whether di person truly lose control, and whether di force pass di provocation, na questions of fact.

sections.title: Prevention of repetition of insult
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
It is lawful for any person to use such force as is reasonably necessary to prevent the repetition of an act or insult of such a nature as to be provocation to him for an assault:
Provided that the force used is not intended and is not such as is likely, to cause death or grievous harm.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping repeat of insult. Person fit use force wey reasonably necessary to stop repeat of act or insult wey be provocation to am for assault. But di force must no be force wey e wan use or fit use cause death or serious harm.

sections.title: Self-defence against unprovoked assault
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
When a person is unlawfully assaulted, and has not provoked the assault, it is lawful for him to use such force to the assailant as is reasonably necessary to make effectual defence against the assault:
Provided that the force used is not intended, and is not such as is likely, to cause death or grievous harm.
If the nature of the assault is such as to cause reasonable apprehension of death or grievous harm, and the person using force by way of defence believes, on reasonable ground, that he cannot otherwise preserve the person defended from death or grievous harm, it is lawful for him to use any such force to the assailant as is necessary for defence, even though such force may cause death or grievous harm.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about self-defence against assault wey person no provoke. If person dey unlawfully assaulted and e no provoke am, e fit use force wey reasonably necessary to defend imself well. But di force must no be force wey e wan use or fit use cause death or serious harm. E get one exception: if di assault make person fear, with good reason, say death or serious harm go happen, and e believe, with good reason, say no other way dey to save di person wey dem dey defend from death or serious harm, e fit use any force wey necessary to defend, even if e cause death or serious harm.

sections.title: Self-defence against provoked assault
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
When a person has unlawfully assaulted another or has provoked an assault from another, and that other assaults him with such violence as to cause reasonable apprehension of death or grievous harm, and to induce him to believe, on reasonable grounds, that it is necessary for his preservation from death or grievous harm to use force in self-defence, he is not criminally responsible for using any such force as is reasonably necessary for such preservation, although such force may cause death or grievous harm.
This protection does not extend to a case in which the person using force, which causes death or grievous harm, first began the assault with intent to kill or to do grievous harm to some person; nor to a case in which the person using force which causes death or grievous harm endeavoured to kill or to do grievous harm to some person before the necessity of so preserving himself arose; nor, in either case, unless, before such necessity arose, the person using such force declined further conflict, and quitted it or retreated from it as far as was practicable.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about self-defence when person don assault another person or provoke assault first. If another person attack am with so much violence wey make am fear, with good reason, say death or serious harm go happen, e no go answer for crime for any force wey reasonably necessary to save imself, even if e cause death or serious harm. But dis protection no cover person wey first begin di assault wey e wan kill or cause serious harm, or wey try to kill or cause serious harm before di need come. For either case, e must first refuse more fight and comot or run comot as far as e fit.

sections.title: Aiding in self-defence
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: In any case in which it is lawful for any person to use force in any degree for the purpose of defending himself against an assault, it is lawful for any other person acting in good faith in his aid to use a like degree of force for the purpose of defending such first-mentioned person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about helping person defend imself. If person fit use force of any level to defend imself against assault, any other person wey act for good faith to help am fit use di same level of force to defend am.

sections.title: Defence of movable property against trespassers
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: It is lawful for any person who is in peaceable possession of any movable property, and for any person acting by his authority, to use such force as is reasonably necessary in order to resist the taking of such property by a trespasser, or in order to retake it from a trespasser, provided that he does not do harm to the trespasser.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defending movable property from trespasser. Person wey get peaceful possession of movable property, and person wey act with im authority, fit use force wey reasonably necessary to stop trespasser from take am, or to take am back from di trespasser. But e must no do harm to di trespasser.

sections.title: Defence of movable property with claim of right
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When a person is in peaceable possession of any movable property under a claim of right, it is lawful for him, and for any person acting by his authority, to use such force as is reasonably necessary in order to defend his possession of the property, even against a person who is entitled by law to possession of the property, provided that he does not do harm to such other person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defending movable property when person claim say e get right to am. If person get peaceful possession of movable property and claim say e get right to am, e and person wey act with im authority fit use force wey reasonably necessary to defend im possession, even against person wey law say get right to possess am. But e must no do harm to dat other person.

sections.title: Defence of movable property without claim of right
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When a person who is entitled by law to the possession of movable property, attempts to take from a person who is in possession of the property, but who neither claims right to it, nor acts by the authority of a person who claims right, and the person in possession resists him, it is lawful for the person so entitled to possession to use force in order to obtain possession of the property, provided that he does not do harm to the person in possession.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about movable property when di person wey hold am no claim right to am. If person wey law say get right to possess movable property try to take am from person wey hold am, but di person wey hold am no claim right to am and no dey act for authority of person wey claim right, and di person wey hold am resist, di person wey get right fit use force to get possession. But e must no do harm to di person wey hold am.

sections.title: Defence of premises against trespassers: removal of disorderly persons
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text:
It is lawful for a person who is in peaceable possession of any land, structure, vessel or place, or who is entitled to the control or management of any land, structure, vessel, or place, and for any person acting by his authority, to use such force as is reasonably necessary in order to prevent any person from wrongfully entering upon such land, structure, vessel, or place, or in order to remove therefrom a person who wrongfully remains therein, provided that he does not do harm to such person.
It is lawful for a person who is in peaceable possession of any land, structure, vessel, or place, or who is entitled to the control or management of any land, structure, vessel, or place, and for any person acting by his authority, to use force in order to remove therefrom any person who conducts himself in a disorderly manner therein, provided that he does not do him harm.
The term "place" includes any part of an enclosure or structure, whether separated from the rest of the enclosure or structure, by a partition, fence, rope, or any other means, or not.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defending land, structure, vessel or place from trespassers, and removing disorderly persons. Person wey get peaceful possession of any land, structure, vessel or place, or get control or management of am, and person wey act with im authority, fit use force wey reasonably necessary to stop person from enter am for wrong way, or to remove person wey stay inside for wrong way. E fit also use force to remove person wey behave for disorderly way inside. For both cases, e must no do harm to di person. 'Place' include any part of enclosure or structure, whether partition, fence, rope or any other thing separate am from di rest or not.

sections.title: Defence of possession of real property or vessel with claim of right
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When a person is in peaceable possession of any land, structure, or vessel, with a claim of right, it is lawful for him, and for any person acting by his authority, to use such force as is reasonably necessary in order to defend his possession, even against a person who is entitled by law to the possession of the property provided that he does not do harm to such person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defending land, structure or vessel when person claim say e get right to am. If person get peaceful possession of any land, structure or vessel and claim say e get right to am, e and person wey act with im authority fit use force wey reasonably necessary to defend im possession, even against person wey law say get right to possess am. But e must no do harm to dat person.

sections.title: Exercise of right of way or easement
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: When a person who claims to be lawfully entitled to enter upon land for the exercise of a right of way or other easement or profit, enters upon the land for the purpose of exercising such right of way, or easement or profit, after notice that his right to use such way or take such profit is disputed by the person in possession of the land, or having entered persists in his entry after such notice, it is lawful for the person in possession, and for any person acting by his authority, to use such force as is reasonably necessary for the purpose of making the person so entering desist from the entry, provided that he does not do him harm.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about right of way or easement. If person wey claim say e get right to enter land to use right of way, easement or profit enter am after notice say di person wey hold di land dispute di right, or enter am and continue after dat notice, di person wey hold di land, and person wey act with im authority, fit use force wey reasonably necessary to make am stop di entry. But e must no do am harm.

sections.title: Correction of child, servant, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about when person fit use blow or force to correct another person. Di force must never reach wound or serious harm. Parent or guardian fit correct child or ward wey never reach 16 years for bad behaviour or disobeying lawful command. Master fit correct servant or apprentice wey never reach 16 years for bad behaviour or failing for im duty. Master of ship fit correct person for im ship wey must do manual labour. Parent or guardian fit give person wey dem trust with di child power to correct, and di law presume say schoolmaster get am unless dem clearly withhold am. But no correction dey allowed if e unreasonable for kind or level, or if di person too small to understand why dem dey do am. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Use of force for preserving order on board a vessel
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: The master of a vessel, or any person acting by his order, may justify the use of any such force against any person onboard the vessel as is necessary for suppressing any mutiny or disorder on board the vessel, whether among officers, seamen, or passengers, whereby the safety of the vessel, or of any person therein or about to enter or quitting the same, is likely to be endangered, or the master is threatened to be subjected to the commands of the other person; and may kill any person who is guilty of or abets such mutiny or disorder, if the safety of the vessel, or the preservation of any such person as aforesaid, cannot be otherwise secured.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about keeping order for vessel. Master of vessel, or person wey act on im order, fit use force wey necessary to stop mutiny or disorder for di vessel, among officers, seamen or passengers, wey fit put di safety of di vessel or any person for danger, or make di master dey under command of another person. E fit also kill any person wey do or support dat mutiny or disorder, if no other way dey to secure di safety of di vessel or save di persons wey dem mention.

sections.title: Surgical operations
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: A person is not criminally responsible for performing in good faith and with reasonable care and skill a surgical operation upon any person for his benefit, or upon an unborn child for the preservation of the mother's life, if the performance of the operation is reasonable, having regard to the patient's state at the time and to all the circumstances of the case.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about surgical operations. Person no go answer for crime if e do surgical operation on person for im benefit, or on unborn child to save di mama life, for good faith and with reasonable care and skill, if di operation reasonable considering di patient condition for dat time and all di circumstances.

sections.title: Excessive force
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: Any person authorised by law to use force is criminally responsible for any excess, according to the nature and quality of the act which constitutes the excess.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about excessive force. Person wey law allow to use force go answer for crime for any excess, based on di nature and kind of di act wey be di excess.

sections.title: Consent to death immaterial
sections.chapter: Chapter 25: Assaults and violence to the person generally: justification and excuse
sections.text: Consent by a person to the causing of his own death does not affect the criminal responsibility of any person by whom such death is caused.
sections.pidgin: Dis section say say if person agree (say 'yes') make dem cause im death, e no change di criminal responsibility of any person wey cause dat death.

sections.title: Duty to provide necessaries
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text: It is the duty of every person having charge of another who is unable by reason of age, sickness, unsoundness of mind, detention or any other cause to withdraw himself from such charge, and who is unable to provide himself with the necessaries of life, whether the charge is undertaken under a contract, or is imposed by law, or arises by reason of any act, whether lawful or unlawful, of the person who has such charge, to provide for that other person the necessaries of life; and he is held to have caused any consequences which result to the life or health of the other person by reason of any omission to perform that duty.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about duty to provide wetin person need to live. Person wey dey in charge of another person wey no fit comot from dat care because of age, sickness, unsound mind, detention or any other cause, and wey no fit provide wetin e need to live, get duty to provide am. E no matter if di care come from contract, from law, or from any act wey di person do, for right way (di law allow am) or for wrong way. If person no do dis duty, di law go take am say e cause any result wey happen to di life or health of di other person.

sections.title: Duty of head of family
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text: It is the duty of every person who, as head of a family, has charge of a child under the age of fourteen years, being a member of his household, to provide the necessaries of life for such child; and he is held to have caused any consequences which result to the life or health of the child by reason of any omission to perform that duty, whether the child is helpless or not.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about duty of head of family. Head of family wey dey in charge of child wey never reach 14 years for im household get duty to provide wetin di child need to live. If e no do am, di law go take am say e cause any result wey happen to di life or health of di child, whether di child dey helpless or no dey.

sections.title: Duty of masters
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text: It is the duty of every person who as master or mistress has contracted to provide necessary food, clothing, or lodging, for any servant or apprentice under the age of sixteen years, to provide the same; and he or she is held to have caused any consequences which result to the life or health of the servant or apprentice by reason of any omission to perform that duty.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about duty of masters. Master or mistress wey don agree by contract to provide necessary food, clothing or lodging for servant or apprentice wey never reach 16 years get duty to provide dem. If e no do am, di law go take am say e cause any result wey happen to di life or health of di servant or apprentice.

sections.title: Duty of persons doing dangerous acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text: It is the duty of every person who, except in a case of necessity, undertakes to administer surgical or medical treatment to any other person, or to do any other lawful act which is or may be dangerous to human life or health, to have reasonable skill and to use reasonable care in doing such act; and he is held to have caused any consequences which result to the life or health of any person by reason of any omission to observe or perform that duty.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about duty of person wey do dangerous act. Person wey take on to give surgical or medical treatment to another person, or to do any other lawful act wey dey or fit dey dangerous to human life or health, must get reasonable skill and use reasonable care, except for case of necessity. If e no do am, di law go take am say e cause any result wey happen to di life or health of any person.

sections.title: Duty of persons in charge of dangerous things
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text: It is the duty of every person who has in his charge or under his control anything, whether living or inanimate, and whether moving or stationary, of such a nature that, in the absence of care or precaution in its use or management, the life, safety, or health of any person may be endangered, to use reasonable care and take reasonable precautions to avoid such danger; and he is held to have caused any consequences which result to the life or health of any person by reason of any omission to perform that duty.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about duty of person wey dey in charge of dangerous things. Person wey get anything for im charge or control, living or no living, moving or no moving, wey fit put person life, safety or health for danger if dem no use am with care, must use reasonable care and take reasonable precautions to avoid di danger. If e no do am, di law go take am say e cause any result wey happen to di life or health of any person.

sections.title: Duty to do certain acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text: When a person undertakes to do any act, the omission to do which is or may be dangerous to human life or health, it is his duty to do that act; and he is held to have caused any consequences which result to the life or health of any person by reason of any omission to perform that duty.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about duty to do certain acts. If person take on to do any act wey dey or fit dey dangerous to human life or health if dem no do am, e get duty to do di act. If e no do am, di law go take am say e cause any result wey happen to di life or health of any person.

sections.title: Breach of contract of person employed in certain services
sections.chapter: Chapter 26: Duties relating to the preservation of human life
sections.text:
(1) Any person employed in any undertaking concerned in the supply of electricity or water, who maliciously breaks his contract of service, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the probable consequence of his so doing, either alone or in combination with others, will be to deprive the community or any part of thereof either wholly or to a great extent of the supply of electricity or water, is guilty of an offence.
(2) Any person who maliciously breaks a contract of service knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that the probable consequences of his so doing, either alone or in combination with others, will be to endanger human life or seriously to endanger public health, including the health of the inmates of a hospital or similar institution, or to cause serious bodily injury, or to expose valuable property, whether real or personal, to destruction or serious injury, is guilty of an offence.
(3) For the purpose of this section-
(i) "maliciously" means with the intention of producing any of the consequences set out in subsection (1) or (2) of this section, as the case may be, or with a reckless disregard of whether such consequences are produced or not, and
(ii) the termination of any contract of service, either alone or in combination with others, on less than seven days' notice of intention so to terminate, in such circumstances that the actual or probable consequences of the termination are those set out in subsection
(1) or (2) of this section, shall, where length of such notice required by any enactment, or by any contract or services, is more than seven days, be deemed to be a malicious breach of contract, and the words "maliciously breaks" in this section of this Code shall be construed accordingly.
(4) Any person guilty of an offence against any of the provisions of this section of this Code is liable, on conviction, to a fine of one hundred naira or to imprisonment for six months or to both such fine and imprisonment.
(5) No prosecution for an offence under this section of this Code shall be constituted without the written consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about breaking contract of service. Person wey work for electricity or water supply business and wey, with bad intention, break im contract, as e sabi say e go cut off di community or part of am from electricity or water, don commit crime. Any person wey, with bad intention, break contract as e sabi say e go put human life or public health for serious danger, cause serious body injury, or expose valuable property to destruction, don also commit crime. 'With bad intention' mean say e wan cause di result or no care. Ending contract with less than 7 days notice, when law or contract require more than 7 days, na bad-intention breach. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 100 naira or prison for 6 months or both. Case need written agreement of di Attorney-General of di Federation.

sections.title: Killing of a human being unlawful
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: It is unlawful to kill any person unless such killing is authorised or justified or excused by law.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about killing person. E dey for wrong way (against di law) to kill any person, unless law authorise, justify or excuse di killing.

sections.title: When a child becomes a human being
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: A child becomes a person capable of being killed when it has completely proceeded in a living state from the body of its mother, whether it has breathed or not, and whether it has an independent circulation or not, and whether the navel-string is severed or not.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about when child become person wey dem fit kill. Child become person wey dem fit kill when e don comot completely from im mama body alive. E no matter whether e don breathe or e never breathe, whether e get im own blood circulation or e no get, or whether dem don cut di navel-string or dem never cut am.

sections.title: Definition of killing
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Except as hereinafter set forth, any person who causes the death of another, directly or indirectly, by any means whatever, is deemed to have killed that other person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin killing mean. Except where di law talk another thing, person wey cause death of another person, directly or indirectly, by any means, dem go count am say e kill dat person.

sections.title: Death by acts done at childbirth
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: When a child dies in consequence of an act done or omitted to be done by any person before or during its birth, the person who did or omitted to do such acts is deemed to have killed the child.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about death for time of childbirth. If child die because of act wey person do, or fail to do, before or during im birth, dem go count di person say e kill di child.

sections.title: Causing death by threats
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: A person who, by threat or intimidation or by deceit, causes another person to do an act or make an omission which results in the death of that other person, is deemed to have killed him.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about causing death by threats. Person wey use threat, intimidation or deceit make another person do act, or fail to do act, wey cause dat person death, dem go count am say e kill am.

sections.title: Acceleration of death
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: A person who does any act or makes any omission which hastens the death of another person who, when the act is done or the omission is made, is labouring under some disorder or disease arising from another cause, is deemed to have killed that other person.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about making death come quick. Person wey do act, or fail to do act, wey make another person die quick, when dat person already get sickness or disorder from another cause, dem go count am say e kill dat person.

sections.title: When injury or death might be prevented by proper precaution
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: When a person causes bodily injury to another from which death results, it is immaterial that the injury might have been avoided by proper precaution on the part of the person injured, or that his death from that injury might have been prevented by proper care or treatment.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about injury or death wey proper precaution fit stop. If person cause body injury to another person and death follow, e no matter if di injured person fit avoid di injury with proper precaution, or if proper care or treatment fit stop di death.

sections.title: Injury causing death in consequence of subsequent treatment
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: When a person does grievous harm to another, and such other person has recourse to surgical or medical treatment, and death results either from the injury or the treatment, he is deemed to have killed that other person, although the immediate cause of death was the surgical or medical treatment, provided that the treatment was reasonably proper under the circumstances, and was applied in good faith.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about injury wey cause death because of treatment after. If person do serious harm to another person, and di other person go for surgical or medical treatment, and death come from di injury or from di treatment, dem go count am say e kill am, even if treatment na di immediate cause. But dis go work only if di treatment dey reasonably proper for di situation and dem apply am for good faith.

sections.title: Limitation as to time of death
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text:
A person is not deemed to have killed another, if the death of that other person does not take place within a year and a day of the cause of death.
Such period is reckoned inclusive of the day on which the last unlawful act contributing to the cause of death was done.
When the cause of death is an omission to observe or perform a duty, the period is reckoned inclusive of the day on which the omission ceased.
When the cause of death is in part an unlawful act, and in part an omission to observe or perform a duty, the period is reckoned inclusive of the day on which the last unlawful act was done or the day on which the omission ceased, whichever is the later.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about time limit for death. Dem no go count person say e kill another person if di death no happen within 1 year and 1 day of di cause of death. Dem count di period including di day wey di last unlawful act wey add to di cause happen. If di cause na failure to do duty, dem count including di day wey di failure stop. If di cause na part unlawful act and part failure to do duty, dem count including di day of di last unlawful act or di day di failure stop, whichever one late pass.

sections.title: Unlawful homicide
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully kills another is guilty of an offence which is called murder or manslaughter, according to the circumstances of the case.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wetin dey happen when person kill another person for wrong way. E don commit crime, and di crime fit be murder or manslaughter, e depend on how di thing happen.

sections.title: Definition of murder
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell us wetin make killing become murder. If person kill another person for wrong way (against di law), e go be murder if any of dis one happen: di person wan kill am or wan hurt am bad bad; e kill am as e dey do bad thing wey fit put life for danger; or e hurt, drug or choke am so dat e go fit commit serious crime or run comot after e don do am. E no matter if di person no wan hurt di exact person wey die. For some of dem, e fit still be murder even if di person no wan kill anybody.

sections.title: Definition of manslaughter
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: A person who unlawfully kills another in such circumstances as not to constitute murder is guilty of manslaughter.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin manslaughter be. Person wey kill another person for wrong way (against di law) for situation wey no reach murder don commit manslaughter.

sections.title: Killing on provocation
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: When a person who unlawfully kills another in circumstances which, but for the provisions of this section of this Code, would constitute murder, does the act which causes death in the heat of passion caused by grave and sudden provocation, and before there is time for his passion to cool, he is guilty of manslaughter only. [1966 No. 84.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about killing on provocation. If person kill another person for wrong way (against di law) for situation wey for normal go be murder, but e do di act wey cause death when e dey hot with anger because of serious and sudden provocation, before im anger get time to cool, e don commit manslaughter only.

sections.title: Punishment of murder: provision for juveniles: provision for pregnant women
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this section of this Code, any person who commits the offence of murder shall be sentenced to death.
Provisions for juveniles
(2) Where an offender who in the opinion of the court had not attained the age of seventeen years at the time the offence was committed, has been found guilty of murder, such offender shall not be sentenced to death but shall be ordered to be detained during the pleasure of the President and upon such an order being made the provisions of Part 44 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply. [1966 No. 84. L.N. 112 of 1964.] Provisions for pregnant women
(3) Where a woman who has been convicted of murder alleges she is pregnant or where the judge before whom she is convicted considers it advisable to have inquiries made as to whether or not she be pregnant, the procedure laid down in section 376 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall first be complied with. [Cap. C41.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for murder. Person wey commit murder go get death sentence. But if di person never reach 17 years when e do am, di court no go sentence am to death; dem go keep am for detention for as long as di President want, and Part 44 of di Criminal Procedure Act go apply. If woman wey di court find guilty of murder say she dey pregnant, or di judge feel say dem need to check am, dem must first follow di process wey section 376 of di Criminal Procedure Act talk before dem do anything.

sections.title: Attempt to murder
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) attempts unlawfully to kill another; or
(2) with intent unlawfully to kill another does any act, or omits to do any act which it is his duty to do, such act or omission being of such a nature as to be likely to endanger human life, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to murder. If person try to kill another person for wrong way (against di law), or wey wan kill another person for wrong way do any act, or no do act wey e suppose do, wey fit put human life for danger, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Attempt to murder by convict
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who, being under sentence of penal servitude or of imprisonment for three years or more, attempts to commit murder is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about murder attempt by convict. Person wey dey under sentence of penal servitude or prison for 3 years or more, and try to commit murder, go face prison for life.

sections.title: Accessory after the fact to murder
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who becomes an accessory after the fact to murder is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey help another person hide or run after murder don happen. Person wey do dis don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Written threats to murder
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who, knowing the contents thereof, directly or indirectly causes any person to receive any writing threatening to kill any person is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about written threats to kill. If person as e sabi say wetin dey inside, directly or indirectly make person receive writing wey threaten to kill any person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Conspiring to murder
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who conspires with any other person to kill any person, whether such person is in Nigeria or elsewhere, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about planning together to kill. If person plan together with another person to kill any person, whether di person dey Nigeria or another place, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Punishment of manslaughter
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who commits the offence of manslaughter, is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for manslaughter. Person wey commit manslaughter go face prison for life.

sections.title: Aiding suicide
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text:
Any person who- (1 ) procures another to kill himself; or
(2) counsels another to kill himself and thereby induces him to do so; or
(3) aids another in killing himself; is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about helping person kill imself. If person cause another person to kill imself, or advise another person to kill imself and so make am do am, or help another person kill imself, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Attempting to commit suicide
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who attempts to kill himself is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to kill imself. Person wey try to kill imself don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Offence of infanticide
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Where a woman by any wilful act or omission causes the death of her child being a child under the age of twelve months, but at the time of the act or omission the balance of her mind was disturbed by reason of her not having fully recovered from the effect of lactation consequent upon the birth of the child, then notwithstanding that the circumstances were such that but for this section of this Code the offence would have amounted to murder, she is guilty of a felony, to wit of infanticide, and may for such offence be dealt with and punished as if she had been guilty of the offence of manslaughter of the child.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about infanticide. If woman, by act wey she do on purpose or by failing to act, cause death of her child wey never reach 12 months, and for dat time her mind no balance because she never fully recover from di effect of lactation after di birth, even if e for normal go be murder, she don commit felony (serious crime) wey dem call infanticide. Dem fit punish her as if she commit manslaughter of di child.

sections.title: Killing unborn child
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who, when a woman is about to be delivered of a child, prevents the child from being born alive by any act or omission of such a nature that, if the child had been born alive and had then died, he would be deemed to have unlawfully killed the child, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about killing unborn child. If person, when woman wan deliver child, stop di child from dey born alive by act or failure to act wey, if di child don born alive and die, dem for count am say e kill di child for wrong way (against di law), e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Concealing the birth of children
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text: Any person who, when a woman is delivered of a child, endeavours, by any secret disposition of the dead body of the child, to conceal the birth, whether the child died before, at or after its birth, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding birth of child. If person, when woman deliver child, try to hide di birth by secretly dey dispose di dead body of di child, whether di child die before, during or after birth, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Unlawful possession of human head
sections.chapter: Chapter 27: Homicide; suicide; infanticide; concealment of birth; unlawful possession of human head
sections.text:
(1) Any person who receives or has in his possession a human head or skull within six months of the same having been separated from the body or skeleton with the intention that such head or skull shall be possessed by himself as a trophy, juju or charm or transferred by him to any other person as a trophy, juju or charm, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
(2) Where in any prosecution under this section of this Code it is proved that the person charged received or had in his possession a human head or skull within six months of the same having been separated from the body or skeleton, it shall be presumed that the person charged received or had in his possession such head or skull with the intention specified in subsection (1) of this section, unless the contrary is proved.
(3) A prosecution for an offence under this section of this Code shall not be instituted except by or with the consent of a law officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about having human head or skull for wrong way. If person receive or get human head or skull within 6 months after dem separate am from di body or skeleton, wey wan keep am for imself as trophy, juju or charm, or give another person as trophy, juju or charm, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 5 years. If dem prove say person receive or get di head or skull within dat 6 months, di court go presume say e get dat intention, unless e prove say no be so. Case fit start only by or with agreement of law officer.

sections.title: Disabling in order to commit felony or misdemeanour
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
