sections.text: Any person who, by any means calculated to choke, suffocate or strangle, and with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of a felony or misdemeanor, or to facilitate the flight of an offender after the commission or attempted commission of a felony or misdemeanor, renders or attempts to render any person incapable of resistance, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life, with or without caning. [30 of 1960.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about making person unable to resist so dat dem go commit crime. If person use any means wey fit choke, suffocate or strangle, wey wan commit or help commit felony or misdemeanour, or help offender run after e commit or try to commit am, and so make person unable to resist, or try to do am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life, with or without caning.

sections.title: Stupefying in order to commit felony or misdemeanour
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of a felony or misdemeanor or to facilitate the flight of an offender after the commission or attempted commission of a felony or misdemeanor, administers or attempts to administer any stupefying or overpowering drug or thing to any person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about giving drug to person so dat dem go commit crime. If person wey wan commit or help commit felony or misdemeanour, or help offender run after e commit or try to commit am, give or try to give any drug or thing wey fit make person weak or overpower am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Acts intended to cause grievous harm or prevent arrest
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to maim, disfigure or disable, any person, or to do some grievous harm to any person, or to resist or prevent the lawful arrest or detention of any person-
(1) unlawfully wounds or does any grievous harm to any person by any means whatever; or
(2) unlawfully attempts in any manner to strike any person with any kind of projectile or with a spear, sword, knife, or other dangerous or offensive weapon; or
(3) unlawfully causes any explosive substance to explode; or
(4) sends or delivers any explosive substance or other dangerous or noxious thing to any person; or
(5) causes any such substance or thing to be taken or received by any person; or
(6) puts any corrosive fluid or any destructive or explosion substances in any place; or
(7) unlawfully casts or throws any such fluid or substances at or upon any person, or otherwise applies any such fluid or substances to the person of any person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about acts wey wan cause serious harm or stop arrest. If person wey wan maim, disfigure or disable person, or do serious harm to person, or resist or stop lawful arrest or detention of anybody, do any of dis for wrong way (against di law): wound or do serious harm to person; try to hit person with projectile, spear, sword, knife or other dangerous weapon; cause explosive to explode; send or deliver explosive or other dangerous or harmful thing to person; cause person to take or receive such thing; put corrosive fluid or destructive or explosive substance for any place; or throw or put such fluid or substance on person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Preventing escape from wreck
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully-
(1) prevents or obstructs any person who is on board of, or is escaping from a vessel which is in distress or wrecked, in his endeavours to save his life; or
(2) obstructs any person in his endeavours to save the life of any person so situated, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stopping person from escape from wreck. If person for wrong way (against di law) block person wey dey vessel wey dey in distress or wey wreck, or wey dey escape from am, from trying to save im life, or block person wey dey try to save life of person like dat, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Intentionally endangering safety of person travelling by railway
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to injure or to endanger the safety of any person travelling by any railway, whether a particular person or not-
(1) places anything on the railway; or
(2) deals with the railway, or with anything whatever upon or near the railway, in such a manner as to affect or endanger the free and safe use of the railway or the safety of any such person; or
(3) shoots or throws anything at, into, or upon, or causes anything to come into contact with, any person or thing on the railway; or
(4) shows any light or signal, or in any way deals with any existing light or signal, upon or near the railway; or
(5) by any omission to do any act which it is his duty to do causes the safety of any such person to be endangered, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life, with or without caning. [30 of 1960.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about endangering person wey dey travel by railway. If person wey wan injure or put safety of person wey dey travel by railway for danger, whether particular person or not, do any of dis: put anything on di railway; do anything with di railway or things near am for way wey affect free and safe use or safety of person; shoot or throw anything at, into or on person or thing for di railway, or cause anything to touch dem; show light or signal, or tamper with existing light or signal near di railway; or fail to do act wey be im duty and so put person safety for danger, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life, with or without caning.

sections.title: Grievous harm
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully does grievous harm to another is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about serious harm. If person for wrong way (against di law) do serious harm to another person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Attempting to injure by explosive substances
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully, and with intent to do any harm to another, puts any explosive substance in any place whatever, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to hurt person with explosive. If person for wrong way (against di law), wey wan do harm to another person, put explosive for any place, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Maliciously administering poison with intent to harm
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully, and with intent to injure or annoy another, causes any poison or other noxious thing to be administered to, or taken by, any person, and thereby endangers his life, or does him some grievous harm, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about giving poison to harm person. If person for wrong way (against di law), wey wan injure or annoy another person, cause poison or other harmful thing to dey given to person or taken by am, and so put im life for danger or do am serious harm, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Wounding and similar acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) unlawfully wounds another; or
(2) unlawfully, and with intent to injure or annoy any person, causes any poison or other noxious thing to be administered to, or taken by, any person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wounding and similar acts. If person wound another person for wrong way (against di law), or for wrong way, wey wan injure or annoy any person, cause poison or other harmful thing to dey given to person or taken by am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Failure to supply necessaries
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who, being charged with the duty of providing for another the necessaries of life, without lawful excuse fails to do so, whereby the life of that other is or is likely to be endangered, or his health is or is likely to be permanently injured, is guilty of a felony and liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about failure to provide wetin person need to live. If person wey get duty to provide wetin another person need to live fail to do am without lawful excuse, so dat di other person life dey or fit dey for danger, or im health dey or fit get permanent injury, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Endangering life or health of apprentices or servants
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who, being charged as a master or mistress with the duty of providing necessary food, clothing, or lodging, for a servant or apprentice under the age of sixteen years, unlawfully fails to perform that duty, or in any other manner does any harm or causes any harm to be done to such servant or apprentice, whereby, in either case, the life of such servant or apprentice is or is likely to be endangered, or his health is likely to be permanently injured, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about danger to life or health of servants or apprentices. If master or mistress wey get duty to provide necessary food, clothing or lodging for servant or apprentice wey never reach 16 years fail to do am for wrong way (against di law), or do harm or cause harm to di servant or apprentice any other way, so dat im life dey or fit dey for danger, or im health fit get permanent injury, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Abandoning or exposing children
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully abandons or exposes a child under the age of seven years, in such a manner that any grievous harm is likely to be caused to it, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about leaving or exposing children. If person for wrong way (against di law) abandon or expose child wey never reach 7 years for way wey fit cause di child serious harm, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 5 years.

sections.title: Setting man-trap
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who sets or places any spring-gun, man-trap or other engine calculated to destroy human life or to inflict grievous harm, or causes any such thing to be set or placed with the intent that it may kill or inflict grievous harm upon a trespasser or any person coming in contact with it, or sets or places any such thing in any such place and in any such manner that it is likely to cause any such result, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
Any person who knowingly permits any such spring-gun, man-trap, or other engine, which has been set or placed by another person in any such place and in any such manner that it is likely to cause any such result, to continue to be so set or placed in any place which is then in, or afterwards comes into, his possession or occupation, is deemed to have set and placed the gun, trap, or engine, with the intent aforesaid.
This section of this Code, does not make it unlawful to set any gun or trap such as is usually set for the purpose of destroying vermin, or to set any spring-gun, man-trap, or engine, at night in a dwelling-house for the protection of the dwelling-house.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about setting man-trap. If person set or put spring-gun, man-trap or other machine wey fit kill or do serious harm, or cause am to dey set or put, wey wan kill or do serious harm to trespasser or any person wey touch am, or put am for place and for way wey e fit cause dat result, e don commit felony (serious crime). Person wey as e sabi say allow such thing wey another person set to stay for place wey dey im possession or occupation, dem go count say na im set am with di same intention. Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). But e no be crime to set gun or trap wey people normally set to kill vermin, or to set spring-gun, man-trap or machine for night inside dwelling-house to protect di house.

sections.title: Reckless and negligent acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
(1) Any person who in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life or to be likely to cause harm to any other person-
(a) drives any vehicle or rides on any public way; or
(b) navigates, or takes part in the navigation or working of, any vessel; or
(c) does any act with fire or any combustible matter, or omits to take precautions against any probable danger from any fire or any combustible matter in his possession; or
(d) omits to take precautions against any probable danger from any animal in his possession; or
(e) gives medical or surgical treatment to any person whom he has undertaken to treat; or
(f) dispenses, supplies, sells, administers, or gives away, any medicine, or poisonous or dangerous matter; or
(g) does any act with respect to, or omits to take proper precautions against any probable danger from, any machinery of which he is solely or partly in charge; or
(h) does any act with respect to, or omits to take proper precautions against any probable danger from, any explosive in his possession, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
(2) Any person who conveys or causes to be conveyed, for hire, any person by water, in a vessel in such a state or so loaded as to be unsafe, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about reckless and careless acts. If person, for way wey too rash or careless wey fit put human life for danger or cause harm to another person, drive vehicle or ride for public way; work vessel; do act with fire or combustible matter, or no take precautions against am; no take precautions against animal wey e get; give medical or surgical treatment wey e don take on; sell or give out medicine or poisonous or dangerous matter; or do act with, or no take proper precautions against, machinery or explosive wey e get or dey in charge of, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Person wey carry person for hire by water for vessel wey no safe or wey dem load wrong don also commit misdemeanour. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Negligent acts causing harm
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully does any act, or omits to do any act which it is his duty to do, not being an act or omission specified in section 343 of this Code, by which act or omission harm is caused to any person, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for six months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about careless acts wey cause harm. If person for wrong way (against di law) do act, or fail to do act wey be im duty, wey no be one of di acts wey section 343 of dis Code talk about, and harm happen to person because of am, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 6 months.

sections.title: Sending unseaworthy ship to sea
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
(1) Any person who sends or attempts to send or is party to sending or attempting to send a Nigerian ship to sea in such an unseaworthy state that the life of any person is likely to be thereby endangered, is guilty of a misdemeanor, unless he proves either that he used all reasonable means to insure her being sent to sea in a seaworthy state, or that her going to sea in such an unseaworthy state was in the circumstances reasonable and justifiable. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(2) The master of a Nigerian ship who knowingly takes the same to sea in such an unseaworthy state that the life of any person is likely to be thereby endangered, is guilty of a misdemeanor, unless he proves that her going to sea in such an unseaworthy state was in the circumstances reasonable and justifiable.
(3) Any person convicted of a misdemeanor under this section of this Code is liable to imprisonment for two years.
(4) A prosecution shall not be instituted in respect of an offence under this section of this Code otherwise than by or with the consent of a law officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about sending Nigerian ship go sea for bad state. If person send, try to send, or join to send or try to send Nigerian ship go sea for state wey no good enough, wey fit put person life for danger, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Master of Nigerian ship wey as e sabi say take am go sea for such state don also commit misdemeanour. Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Case fit start only by or with agreement of law officer. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): person fit prove say e use all reasonable means to make sure say ship go go sea for good state, or say to go for dat state dey reasonable and justifiable for di situation. Master fit prove only di second one.

sections.title: Endangering safety of persons travelling by railway
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text: Any person who, by any unlawful act, or by any omission to do any act which it is his duty to do, causes the safety of any person travelling by any railway to be endangered, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about endangering safety of person wey dey travel by railway. If person, by unlawful act or by failing to do act wey be im duty, put safety of person wey dey travel by railway for danger, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Endangering steamships by tampering with machinery
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who, being a person having actual control over a steam vessel, or over any part of the machinery of a steam vessel, does any act or makes any omission or is privy to any act or omission with respect to the machinery of the vessel, whereby to his knowledge, the safety of any person on board the vessel is or is likely to be endangered, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about harming safety of steam vessel by machinery. If person wey get actual control of steam vessel or part of im machinery do act or fail to do act, or know about am, with di machinery, wey as e sabi, put safety of person for di vessel for danger or fit put am for danger, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: The like by engineers
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who is an engineer, or one of the engineers, in charge of the machinery of a steam vessel at any time when any act is done or omitted to be done by any other person with respect to the machinery of the vessel, whereby the safety of any person on board the vessel is, or is likely to be endangered, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of two hundred naira.
It is a defence to a charge of the offence defined in this section of this Code to prove that the act or omission was done or made without the knowledge of the accused person, and without any neglect or default on his part.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about engineers for steam vessel. If person na engineer, or one of di engineers, wey dey in charge of di machinery of steam vessel when any other person do or fail to do act with di machinery wey put or fit put safety of person for di vessel for danger, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 200 naira. E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di accused fit prove say di act or failure happen without im knowledge, and without any neglect or default from am.

sections.title: Evading laws as to shipping dangerous goods
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
Any person who knowingly sends by any vessel, or carries in any vessel, any explosive substance, or any acid, or other thing of a dangerous or destructive nature, under false description of the substance or thing or with a false description of the sender thereof, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about shipping dangerous goods with false description. If person as e sabi say send by vessel, or carry for vessel, any explosive, acid or other dangerous or destructive thing, with false description of di thing or of who send am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Landing, etc., explosives Any person who-
sections.chapter: Chapter 28: Offences endangering life or health
sections.text:
(1) being charged by law with any duty respecting the shipping, unshipping, landing, putting off shore, conveyance, delivery or storage of any explosive substance, or of any acid, or other thing of a dangerous or destructive nature, from any vessel, fails to perform that duty; or
(2) being concerned in the shipping, unshipping, landing, putting off shore, conveyance, delivery or storage of any such substance, acid or thing, violates the provisions of the laws relating to such shipping, unshipping, landing, putting off shore, conveyance, delivery or storage, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
This section of this Code does not apply to any explosive, acid or other thing, the property of the State, while it is under the control of an officer of the armed forces of Nigeria.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about landing explosives and similar things. If person wey di law give duty about shipping, unshipping, landing, putting off shore, conveyance, delivery or storage of explosive, acid or other dangerous or destructive thing from vessel fail to do di duty, or person wey dey involved for any of dem break di laws about am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). But dis section no apply to explosive, acid or other thing wey be property of di State when officer of di armed forces of Nigeria dey control am.

sections.title: Punishment of assault
sections.chapter: Chapter 29: Assaults
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully assaults another is guilty of a misdemeanor, and is liable, if no greater punishment is provided, to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for assault. If person for wrong way (against di law) assault another person, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). If law no give bigger punishment, di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Assault with intent to commit unnatural offence
sections.chapter: Chapter 29: Assaults
sections.text: Any person who assaults another with intent to have carnal knowledge of him or her against the order of nature is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about assault wey wan have sex against di order of nature. If person assault another person wey wan have sex with am for way wey go against di order of nature, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Indecent assault on males
sections.chapter: Chapter 29: Assaults
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully and indecently assaults any male person is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about indecent assault on males. If person for wrong way (against di law) and indecently assault any male person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Assaults on person protecting wrecks
sections.chapter: Chapter 29: Assaults
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully assaults and uses actual violence to a peace officer or any other person while acting in the execution of his duty in or concerning the preservation of a vessel in distress, or of any vessel or goods wrecked or stranded or lying under water, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about assault on person wey dey protect wrecks. If person for wrong way (against di law) assault and use actual violence on peace officer or any other person wey dey do im duty to preserve vessel wey dey in distress, or any vessel or goods wey wreck, strand or dey under water, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Assaults occasioning harm
sections.chapter: Chapter 29: Assaults
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully assaults another and thereby does him harm, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about assault wey cause harm. If person for wrong way (against di law) assault another person and so do am harm, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Serious assaults
sections.chapter: Chapter 29: Assaults
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) assaults another with intent to commit a felony, or with intent to resist or prevent the lawful arrest or detention of himself or of any other person; or
(2) assaults, resists, or wilfully obstructs a police officer while acting in the execution of his duty, or any person acting in aid of a police officer while so acting; or
(3) unlawfully assaults, resists, or obstructs, any person engaged in the lawful execution of any process against any property, or in making a lawful distress, while so engaged; or
(4) assaults, resists, or obstructs any person engaged in such lawful execution of process, or in making a lawful distress, with intent to rescue any property lawfully taken under such process or distress; or
(5) assaults any person on account of any act done by him in the execution of any duty imposed on him by law; or
(6) assaults any person in pursuance of any unlawful conspiracy respecting any manufacture, trade, business, or occupation, or respecting any person or persons concerned or employed in any manufacture, trade, business, or occupation, or the wages of any such person or person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about serious assaults. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if e: assault another person wey wan commit felony, or wan resist or stop lawful arrest or detention of imself or anybody; assault, resist or on purpose block police officer wey dey do im duty, or person wey dey help am; for wrong way assault, resist or block person wey dey lawfully carry out process against property or dey make lawful distress; do dat wey wan rescue property wey dem lawfully take under di process or distress; assault person because of act wey e do for duty wey law give am; or assault person because of unlawful plan together about any manufacture, trade, business or work, or about person wey dey involved for am, or dia wages. Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Definition of rape
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.text: Any person who has unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl, without her consent, or with her consent, if the consent is obtained by force or by means of threats or intimidation of any kind, or by fear of harm, or by means of false and fraudulent representation as to the nature of the act, or, in the case of a married woman, by personating her husband, is guilty of an offence which is called rape.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin rape mean. If person have sex for wrong way (against di law) with woman or girl without her agreement (say 'yes'), or with her agreement if dem get am by force, by threats or intimidation of any kind, by fear of harm, or by false and cheating statement about wetin di act be, or, if she be married woman, by pretending say na her husband, e don commit crime wey dem call rape.

sections.title: Punishment of rape
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.text: Any person who commits the offence of rape is liable to imprisonment for life, with or without caning. [30 of 1960.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for rape. Person wey commit rape go face prison for life, with or without caning.

sections.title: Attempt to commit rape
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.text: Any person who attempts to commit the offence of rape is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years, with or without caning. [30 of 1960.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to commit rape. Person wey try to commit rape don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years, with or without caning.

sections.title: Indecent assaults on females
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully and indecently assaults a woman or girl is guilty of a misdemeanor, and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about indecent assault on females. If person for wrong way (against di law) and indecently assault woman or girl, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Abduction
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to marry or carnally know a female of any age, or to cause her to be married, or carnally known by any other person, takes her away, or detains her against her will, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about taking away woman or girl. If person wey wan marry or have sex with female of any age, or wey wan make her marry or have sex with another person, take her away or hold her against her will, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Abduction of girls under sixteen
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully takes an unmarried girl under the age of sixteen years out of the custody or protection of her father or mother or other person having the lawful care or charge of her, and against the will of such father or mother or other person, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about taking girl wey never reach 16 years. If person for wrong way (against di law) take unmarried girl wey never reach 16 years comot from di custody or protection of her father, mother or other person wey get lawful care of her, against dia will, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Ignorance of age of girl, or consent, no defence
sections.chapter: Chapter 30: Assaults on females: abduction
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wetin no matter for case under section 362 of dis Code. E no matter if di offender believe say di girl don reach 16 years or pass am. E no matter also if dem take di girl with her own agreement (say 'yes') or if na her own suggestion.

sections.title: Kidnapping
sections.chapter: Chapter 31: Offences against liberty: slave dealing
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) unlawfully imprisons any person, and takes him out of Nigeria without his consent; or
(2) unlawfully imprisons any person within Nigeria in such a manner as to prevent him from applying to a court for his release or from discovering to any other person the place where he is imprisoned, or in such a manner as to prevent any person entitled to have access to him from discovering the place where he is imprisoned, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for ten years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about kidnapping. If person for wrong way (against di law) lock person up and carry am comot Nigeria without im agreement (say 'yes'), or for wrong way lock person up inside Nigeria for way wey stop am from asking court to release am, or from telling anybody where dem keep am, or for way wey stop person wey get right to reach am from knowing where dem keep am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 10 years.

sections.title: Deprivation of liberty
sections.chapter: Chapter 31: Offences against liberty: slave dealing
sections.text: Any person who unlawfully confines or detains another in any place against his will, or otherwise unlawfully deprives another of his personal liberty, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about taking person liberty. If person for wrong way (against di law) lock or hold another person for any place against im will, or any other way take person liberty for wrong way, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Compelling action by intimidation
sections.chapter: Chapter 31: Offences against liberty: slave dealing
sections.text:
Subject to the provisions of the Trade Unions Act, any person who, with intent to prevent or hinder any other person from doing any act which he is lawfully entitled to do, or with intent to compel him to do any act which he is lawfully entitled to abstain from doing, or to abstain from doing any act which he is lawfully entitled to do- [Cap. Tl4.]
(a) threatens such other person with injury to his person, reputation, or property, or to the person, reputation, or property of anyone in whom he is interested; or
(b) persistently follows such other person about from place to place; or
(c) hides any tools, clothes, or other property owned or used by such other person, or deprives him of or hinders him in the use thereof; or
(d) watches or besets the house or other place where such other person resides, or works, or carries on business, or happens to be, or the approach to such house or place; or
(e) follows such other person with two or more other persons in a disorderly manner in or through any street or road; or
(f) induces or attempts to induce that person to believe that he, or any person in whom he is interested, will become an object of displeasure to the Government of Nigeria or to any person employed in the public service of Nigeria, is guilty of an offence and is liable on conviction to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about forcing person by intimidation, subject to di Trade Unions Act. If person, wey wan stop or force another person to do or no do act wey law allow am, threaten am or person wey e care about with injury to body, reputation or property; follow am about again and again; hide or stop am from using im property; watch or surround where e stay, work or dey; follow am with two or more people for disorderly way for street or road; or make am believe say e or person wey e care about go suffer displeasure of di Government of Nigeria or public servant, e don commit crime. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Compelling action by assault
sections.chapter: Chapter 31: Offences against liberty: slave dealing
sections.text: Any person who, with any of the intents in section 366 of this Code mentioned, assaults any other person or anyone in whom he is interested, is guilty of a felony and liable to imprisonment for five years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about forcing person by assault. If person assault another person, or anybody wey e care about, with any of di intentions wey section 366 of dis Code mention, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 5 years.

sections.title: Concealment of matters affecting liberty
sections.chapter: Chapter 31: Offences against liberty: slave dealing
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) being required by law to keep any record touching any matter relating to any person in confinement, refuses or neglects to keep such record, or makes in such record an entry which, in any material particular, is, to his knowledge, false; or
(2) being required by law to give any information to any person touching any person in confinement, or to show to any person, any person in confinement, or any place in which a person is confined-
(a) refuses or neglects to give such information or to show such person or place to any person to whom he is so required to give the information or show the person or place; or
(b) gives to any person to whom he is so required to give it, information touching any such matter which, in any material particular, is to his knowledge, false, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding matters about person liberty. If person wey law require to keep record about person wey dey confinement refuse or fail to keep am, or enter wetin e sabi say e false for any important part; or if person wey law require to give information, or show person wey dey confinement or place wey dem confine person, refuse or fail to do am, or give information wey e sabi say e false for any important part, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Slave dealing
sections.chapter: Chapter 31: Offences against liberty: slave dealing
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about slave dealing. Person don commit slave dealing if e: deal or trade in, buy, sell, transfer or take slave; do so to person so dat dem go hold or treat person as slave; place or receive person for servitude as pledge or security for debt, whatever name dem call am, including pawn; bring or induce person to come inside Nigeria, or send or induce person to go comot Nigeria, so dat dem go hold, deal in, sell or transfer am as slave or put am for servitude as pledge for debt; hold or possess any person as slave for Nigeria, whether e be citizen of Nigeria or not; or enter any contract or agreement, with or without payment, to do any of dem. Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Bigamy
sections.chapter: Chapter 32: Offences relating to marriage and parental rights and duties
sections.text:
Any person who, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
This section of this Code does not extend to any person whose marriage with such husband or wife has been dissolved or declared void by a court of competent jurisdiction, nor to any person who contracts a marriage during the life of a former husband or wife, if such husband or wife, at the time of the subsequent marriage, shall have been absent from such person for the space of seven years, and shall not have been heard of by such person as being alive within that time.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about bigamy. If person wey get husband or wife wey dey alive marry again for case wey di marriage no valid because di husband or wife dey alive, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. But dis section no cover person wey court wey get power don end or declare im marriage with di husband or wife void, or person wey marry again when di former husband or wife don dey absent from am for 7 years and e never hear say e dey alive for dat time.

sections.title: Child-stealing
sections.chapter: Chapter 32: Offences relating to marriage and parental rights and duties
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to deprive any parent, guardian or other person who has the lawful care or charge of a child under the age of twelve years, of the possession of such child, or with intent to steal any article upon or about the person of any such child-
(1) forcibly or fraudulently takes or entices away, or detains the child; or
(2) receives or harbours the child, knowing it to have been so taken or enticed away or detained, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
It is a defence to a charge of any of the offences defined in this section of this Code to prove t hat the accused person claimed in good faith a right to the possession of the child, or, in the case of an illegitimate child, is its mother or claimed to be its father.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stealing child wey never reach 12 years. If person take, tempt or hold dat kind child so dat im parent or di person wey dey look am no go get am again, or so dat e go steal anything wey dey di child body, e don commit felony (serious crime). Person wey receive or hide di child as e sabi say dem take am wrong way don also commit di crime. Di punishment na prison for 14 years. E get one defence: di accused fit show say e honestly believe say e get right to di child, or say na di child mama, or, if di child no get married parents, say e claim say na di papa.

sections.title: Desertion of children
sections.chapter: Chapter 32: Offences relating to marriage and parental rights and duties
sections.text: Any person who being the parent, guardian or other person having the lawful care or charge of a child under the age of twelve years, and being able to maintain such child, wilfully and without lawful or reasonable cause deserts the child and leaves it without means of support, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about leaving children. If parent, guardian or person wey get lawful care of child wey never reach 12 years, and wey fit maintain di child, on purpose and without lawful or reasonable cause leave di child and leave am without means of support, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Definition of defamatory matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
Defamatory matter is matter likely to injure the reputation of any person by exposing him to hatred, contempt, or ridicule, or likely to damage any person in his profession or trade by any injury to his reputation.
Such matter may be expressed in spoken words or in any audible sounds, or in words legibly marked on any substance whatever, or by any sign or object signifying such matter otherwise than by words, and may be expressed either directly or by insinuation or irony.
It is immaterial whether at the time of the publication of the defamatory matter, the person concerning whom such matter is published is living or dead:
Provided that no prosecution for the publication of defamatory matter concerning a dead person shall be instituted without the consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin defamatory matter mean. Defamatory matter na matter wey fit hurt person reputation by making people hate, disrespect or laugh at am, or fit damage person for im profession or trade by hurting im reputation. Dem fit express am by spoken words or any sound, by words wey dem write for any thing, or by any sign or object wey mean am, directly or by hint or irony. E no matter if di person wey dem talk about dey alive or dead when dem publish am. But if na dead person, case no fit start without agreement (say 'yes') of di Attorney-General of di Federation.

sections.title: Definition of publication
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
(1) For the purposes of this Code, the publication of defamatory matter is-
(a) in the case of spoken words or audible sounds, the speaking of such words or the making of such sounds in the hearing of the person defamed or any other person;
(b) in other cases, the exhibiting of it in public, or causing it to be read or seen, or showing or delivering it, or causing it to be shown or delivered, with intent that it may be read or seen by the person defamed or by any other person.
(2) Sounds where recorded shall, if defamatory, be deemed to be published if reproduced in any place to the hearing of persons other than the person causing it to be reproduced.
(3) In this section-
"recorded" means sounds collected or stored by means of tape, disc, cylinder or other means whatsoever, where the sounds are capable of being reproduced or are intended for reproduction by electrical or mechanical means at any time or from time to time thereafter, and includes the matrix, and cognate expressions shall have the like meaning;
"sound" includes speech and mere noise.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin publication of defamatory matter mean for dis Code. For spoken words or sounds, na to speak di words or make di sounds for di hearing of di person or any other person. For other cases, na to show am for public, or cause person read or see am, or show or deliver am, or cause am to dey shown or delivered, wey wan make di person or any other person read or see am. Recorded sound wey defamatory, if dem play am for any place for hearing of people wey no be di person wey cause am to dey played, dem go count am as published. 'Recorded' mean sounds wey dem collect or store by tape, disc, cylinder or any other way, wey fit dey played back by electrical or mechanical means, and e include di matrix. 'Sound' include speech and mere noise.

sections.title: Publication of defamatory matter
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of this Chapter, any person who publishes any defamatory matter, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year; and any person who publishes any defamatory matter knowing it to be false, is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about publishing defamatory matter. Subject to di rules for dis Chapter, person wey publish defamatory matter don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year. But if person publish am as e sabi say e false, di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Publishing defamatory matter with intent to extort
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
Any person who publishes, or threatens to publish, or offers to abstain from publishing, or offers to prevent the publication of defamatory matter, with intent to extort money or other property, or with intent to induce any person to give, confer, procure, or attempt to procure, to, upon, or for, any person, any property or benefit of any kind, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about publishing defamatory matter to force person give money or property. If person publish, threaten to publish, or offer to stop publishing or stop di publication of defamatory matter, wey wan force person give money or other property, or wey wan make person give or get any property or benefit of any kind for any person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Publication of truth for public benefit
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text: The publication of defamatory matter is not an offence if the publication is, at the time it is made, for the public benefit and if the defamatory matter is true.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about publishing truth for public benefit. To publish defamatory matter no be crime if, when dem publish am, e dey for public benefit and di matter true.

sections.title: Cases in which publication is absolutely privileged
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
The publication of defamatory matter is absolutely privileged, and no person is criminally liable in respect thereof, in the following cases- [L.N. 257 of 1959. L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 27.]
(1) if the matter is published by the President, Minister or a Governor or by order of the President, Minister or a Governor in any official document, Gazette or proceedings; or
(2) if the publication is made in a petition to the President, Minister, or a Governor; or
(3) if the publication takes place in proceedings held before or under the authority of any court, or in any inquiry held under the authority of any Act, law, statute, or order, or under the authority of the President, Minister, or a Governor; or
(4) if the publication takes place in an official report made by a person appointed to hold an inquiry under the authority of any Act, law, statute, or Order in Council, or of the President, Minister, or a Governor; or
(5) if the matter is published concerning a person subject to military discipline for the time being, and relates to his conduct as a person subject to such discipline, and is published by some person having authority over him in respect of such conduct, and to some person having authority over him in respect of such conduct. [L.N. 257 of 1959. L.N. 112 of 1964. 1967 No. 19. 1967 No. 27.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cases wey publication of defamatory matter get full protection (absolutely privileged), so no person go answer for crime. Dem be: when di President, Minister or Governor, or person wey dem order, publish am for official document, Gazette or proceedings; when dem publish am for petition to di President, Minister or Governor; when e happen for proceedings wey dey before or under authority of court, or for inquiry wey Act, law or order, or di President, Minister or Governor authorise; when e dey inside official report of person wey dem appoint to hold such inquiry; and when di matter na about person wey dey under military discipline, e concern im conduct as such, and person wey get authority over am for dat conduct publish am to person wey get authority over am for dat conduct.

sections.title: Cases in which publication is conditionally privileged
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
The publication of defamatory matter is conditionally privileged, and no person is criminally liable in respect thereof, in the following cases-
(1) if the defamatory matter consists of an extract from, or an abstract of, a petition to, or a Gazette or document published by or under the authority of, the President or a Governor of a State, or a Minister, and the publication is made without ill-will to the person defamed; or
(2) if the defamatory matter constitutes, in whole or in part, a fair report, for the information of the public, of any public proceeding of any court, whether preliminary or final; or of any public proceeding of any body, constituted, or authorised to hold such proceeding by any Act, law, statute or order; or of any public meeting so far as the public is concerned in the matter published; if in every such case the publication is made without ill-will to the person defamed; or
(3) if the publication is for the information of the public at the request of any government department or peace officer, or if the defamatory matter is any notice or report issued by such department or officer, for the information of the public, and if in every such case the publication is made without ill-will to the person defamed; or
(4) if the defamatory matter consists of fair comment either on any matter the publication of which, or on any report which, is hereinbefore in the preceding or this section referred to; or
(5) if the defamatory matter consists of fair comment upon the public conduct of any person in public affairs, or upon the public conduct of any person employed in the public service in the discharge of his public duties, or upon the character of any of such persons so far as it appears by such conduct; or
(6) if the defamatory matter consists of fair comment on any published book or other literary production, or any composition or work of art, or performance publicly exhibited, or any other communication made to the public on any subject; or of the character of the author of such book, production, composition, work of art, or the person exhibiting such performance, so far as their characters may appear therefrom respectively; or
(7) if the publication is in good faith for the purpose of seeking remedy or redress for any private or public wrong or grievance from a person who has, or is reasonably believed by the person publishing to have, the right to remedy or redress such wrong or grievance; or
(8) if the publication is made in good faith by a person having any lawful authority over another, and is made by him in the course of a censure passed by him on the conduct of that other, in matters to which such lawful authority relates; or
(9) if the publication is made on the invitation or challenge of the person defamed; or
(10) if the publication is made in order to answer or refute some other defamatory matter published by the person defamed, concerning the person making the publication or some other person; or
(11) if the defamatory matter constitutes an answer to inquiries made of the person publishing it, relating to some subject as to which the person by whom or on whose behalf the inquiry is made, has, or on reasonable grounds is believed by the person publishing to have, an interest in knowing the truth, and if the publication is made in good faith for the purpose of giving information in respect of that matter to that person; or
(12) if the defamatory matter constitutes information given to the person to whom the defamatory matter is published, with respect to some subject as to which he has, or is on reasonable grounds believed to have, such an interest in knowing the truth, as to make the conduct of the person giving the information reasonable in the circumstances:
Provided that as regards paragraphs (7), (8), (9), (10) and (11) of this section, the person making the publication honestly believes the matter published to be true, the matter published is relevant to the matters the existence of which may excuse the publication of defamatory matter, and the manner and extent of the publication do not exceed what is reasonably sufficient for the occasion; and as regards paragraphs (12) that the defamatory matter is relevant to the subject therein mentioned, and that it is either true, or is made without ill-will to the person defamed and in the honest belief, on reasonable grounds, that it is true.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cases wey publication of defamatory matter get conditional protection (conditionally privileged), so no person go answer for crime. E include: extract or summary of official petition, Gazette or document; fair report of public proceedings of court or of body wey law set up, or of public meeting; publication for public information at request of government department or peace officer; fair comment on public conduct of public officers, or on published book, art or performance; good faith publication to seek remedy for wrong; good faith censure by person wey get lawful authority; and answer to challenge, attack or inquiry. For many of dem, no ill-will must dey, or di person must honestly believe say e true, and di way and size of di publication must no pass wetin dey reasonable. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Publication in a periodical
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
(1) In this section and section 381 of this Code, the term "periodical" includes any newspaper, review, magazine, or other writing or print, published periodically.
(2) The criminal responsibility of the proprietor, editor, or publisher, of any periodical for the publication of any defamatory matter contained therein, may be rebutted by proof that such publication took place without his knowledge and without negligence on his part.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about publication for periodical. For dis section and section 381 of dis Code, 'periodical' include any newspaper, review, magazine or other writing or print wey dem publish from time to time. Di owner, editor or publisher of periodical fit clear im criminal responsibility for defamatory matter wey dey inside am by proving say di publication happen without im knowledge and without negligence from am.

sections.title: Protection of innocent sellers of books and newspapers
sections.chapter: Chapter 33: Defamation
sections.text:
The sale by any person of any book, pamphlet, or other printed or written matter, or of any number or part of any periodical, is not a publication thereof for the purposes of this Chapter, unless such person knows that such book, pamphlet, printed or written matter, or number or part, contains defamatory matter; or, in the case of any part or number of any periodical, that such periodical habitually contains defamatory matter.
Part 6
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about protecting innocent sellers of books and newspapers. To sell any book, pamphlet or other printed or written matter, or any number or part of periodical, no be publication of am for dis Chapter. But e go be publication if di seller sabi say di thing get defamatory matter, or, for periodical, say di periodical habitually get defamatory matter.

sections.title: Things capable of being stolen
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text:
Every inanimate thing whatever which is the property of any person, and which is movable, is capable of being stolen.
Every inanimate thing which is the property of any person, and which is capable of being made movable, is capable of being stolen as soon as it becomes movable, although it is made movable in order to steal it.
Every tame animal, whether tame by nature or wild by nature and tamed, which is the property of any person, is capable of being stolen: but tame pigeons are not capable of being stolen except while they are in a pigeon-house or on their owner's land.
A thing in action is capable of being stolen.
Animals wild by nature, of a kind which is not ordinarily found in a condition of natural liberty in Nigeria, which are the property of any person, and which are usually kept in a state of confinement, are capable of being stolen, whether they are actually in confinement or have escaped from confinement. [1966 No. 84.] Animals wild by nature, of a kind which is ordinarily found in a condition of natural liberty in Nigeria, which are the property of any person, are capable of being stolen while they are in confinement and while they are being actually pursued after escaping from confinement, but not at any other time.
An animal wild by nature is deemed to be in a state of confinement so long as it is in a den, cage, sty, tank, or other small enclosure, or is otherwise so placed that it cannot escape and that its owner can take possession of it at pleasure.
An ostrich on an enclosed ostrich farm is capable of being stolen. The term "animal" includes any living creature other than mankind.
Wild animals in the enjoyment of their natural liberty are not capable of being stolen, but their dead bodies are capable of being stolen.
Everything produced by or forming part of the body of an animal capable of being stolen is capable of being stolen.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about things wey fit dem steal. Any movable thing wey no get life and be person property fit dem steal, and thing wey fit dem make movable fit dem steal as soon as e become movable, even if dem make am movable to steal am. Tame animals wey be person property fit dem steal, but tame pigeons only when dem dey pigeon-house or for dia owner land. Wild animals wey no normally dey free for Nigeria and dem keep for confinement fit dem steal, whether dem dey confinement or don escape. Wild animals wey normally dey free fit dem steal only when dem dey confinement or dem dey chase dem after dem escape. Dead body of wild animals wey dey free fit dem steal. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Definition of stealing
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin stealing mean. Person steal if e take, or use for imself or another person, anything wey fit dem steal, by cheating. Dem count am as cheating if e do am to: take am from di owner or person wey get special property for am for good; use am as pledge or security; give am out on condition wey e fit no fit do; deal with am so say dem no fit return am for di same condition; or, for money, use am as e like even if e plan to pay back later. E fit still be cheating even if e no hide am. If person find lost thing and use am, e no be cheating if e no sabi who be di owner and believe, with good reason, say dem no fit find am. Person no take thing unless e move am. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Special cases
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text:
(1) When a factor or agent pledges or gives a lien on any goods or documents of title to goods entrusted to him for the purpose of sale or otherwise for any sum of money not greater than the amount due to him from his principal at the time of pledging or giving the lien, together with the amount of any bill of exchange or promissory note accepted or made by him for or on account of his principal, such dealing with the goods or document of title is not deemed to be stealing.
(2) When a servant, contrary to his master's orders, takes from his possession any food in order that it may be given to an animal belonging to or in the possession of his master, such taking is not deemed to be stealing.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about special cases wey no be stealing. If factor or agent pledge or give lien on goods or documents of title wey dem give am to sell or for other purpose, for sum wey no pass wetin im principal owe am for dat time, plus any bill of exchange or promissory note wey e accept or make for im principal, dat no be stealing. If servant, against im master order, take food from im master possession to give animal wey belong to im master or dey im master possession, dat no be stealing.

sections.title: Funds, etc., held under direction
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text:
When a person receives, either alone or jointly with another person, any money or valuable security or a power of attorney for the sale, mortgage, pledge, or other disposition, of any property, whether capable of being stolen or not, with a direction in either case that such money or any part thereof, or any other money received in exchange for it, or any part thereof, or the proceeds or any part of the proceeds of such security, or of such security, or of such mortgage, pledge, or other disposition, shall be applied to any purpose or paid to any person specified in the direction, such money and proceeds are deemed to be the property of the person from whom the money, security or power of attorney, was received until the direction has been complied with:
Provided that if the person receiving the money, security, or power of attorney, and the person from whom he receives it, ordinarily deal with each other on such terms that in the absence of any special direction all money paid to the former on account of the latter would be properly treated as an item in a debtor and creditor account between them, the former cannot be charged with stealing the money or any proceeds unless the direction is in writing.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about money wey person hold under direction. If person receive, alone or with another person, money, valuable security or power of attorney to sell, mortgage, pledge or dispose of property, with direction say make dem use di money, di proceeds or wetin e get in exchange for one purpose or pay am to one person, di law go take di money and proceeds as property of di person wey give am until di direction don dey followed. But if di two people normally deal with each other for way wey, without special direction, money wey dem pay go be item for debtor and creditor account, di person wey receive am no fit be charged with stealing am unless di direction dey for writing.

sections.title: Funds, etc., received by agents for sale
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text: When a person receives, either alone or jointly with another person, any property from another on terms authorising or requiring him to sell it or otherwise dispose of it, and requiring him to pay or account for the proceeds of the property, or any part of such proceeds, or to deliver anything received in exchange of the property, to the person from whom it is received, or some other person, then the proceeds of the property, and anything so received in exchange for it, are deemed to be the property of the person from whom the property was so received, until they have been disposed of in accordance with the terms on which the property was received, unless it is a part of those terms that the proceeds, if any, shall form an item in a debtor and creditor account between him and the person to whom he is to pay them or account for them, and that the relation of debtor and creditor only shall exist between them in respect thereof.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about money wey agent receive for sale. If person receive, alone or with another person, property from another on terms wey allow or require am to sell am or dispose of am, and to pay or account for di proceeds, or deliver anything wey e get in exchange, to di person wey give am or another person, di proceeds and anything wey e get in exchange na property of di person wey give am until dem dispose am as di terms say. But e no go be so if di terms say di proceeds go be item for debtor and creditor account between dem, and say na only debtor and creditor relationship go dey between dem.

sections.title: Money received for another
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text: When a person receives, either alone or jointly with another person, any money on behalf of another, the money is deemed to be the property of the person on whose behalf it is received, unless the money is received on the terms that it shall form an item in a debtor and creditor account, and that the relation of debtor and creditor only shall exist between the parties in respect of it.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about money wey person receive for another. If person receive money, alone or with another person, for another person, di money na property of di person wey e receive am for. But e no go be so if e receive am on terms say e go be item for debtor and creditor account, and say na only debtor and creditor relationship go dey between dem.

sections.title: Stealing by persons having an interest in the thing stolen
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text: When any person takes or converts anything capable of being stolen, in such circumstances as would otherwise amount to stealing, it is immaterial that he himself has a special property or interest therein or that he himself is the owner of the thing taken or converted subject to some special property or interest of some other person therein; or that he is lessee of the thing, or that he himself is one of two or more joint owners of the thing; or that he is a director or officer of a corporation or company or society who are the owners of it.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about stealing by person wey get interest for di thing. If person take or convert anything wey fit dem steal for way wey for normal go be stealing, e no matter if e get special property or interest for am, or if na im be di owner subject to another person special property or interest, or if e be lessee, or one of joint owners, or director or officer of corporation, company or society wey own am.

sections.title: Husband and wife
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text: A person who, while a man and his wife are living together, procures either of them to deal with anything which is, to his knowledge, the property of the other in a manner which would be stealing, if they were not married, is deemed to have stolen the thing, and may be charged with stealing it.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about husband and wife. If person, while man and im wife dey live together, cause any of dem to deal with anything wey e sabi say na property of di other for way wey go be stealing if dem no marry, dem go count am say e steal di thing and dem fit charge am with stealing am.

sections.title: Punishment of stealing
sections.chapter: Chapter 34: Stealing
sections.text:
Any person who steals anything capable of being stolen, is guilty of a felony and is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to imprisonment for three years.
Punishment in special cases Stealing wills
(1) If the thing stolen is a testamentary instrument, whether the testator is living or dead, the offender is liable to imprisonment for life.
Stealing postal matter, etc.
(2) If the thing stolen is a postal matter or any chattel, money, or valuable security, contained in any postal matter, the offender is liable to imprisonment for life.
Stealing cattle
(3) If the thing stolen is any of the things following, that it to say: a horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, bull, cow, ox, ram, ewe, wether, goat or pig, or the young of any such animal, the offender is liable on conviction to pay a fine of two hundred naira or to imprisonment for two years.
Stealing from the person; stealing goods in transit, etc.
(4) If the offence is committed in any of the following circumstances-
(a) if the thing is stolen from the person of another;
(b) if the thing is stolen in a dwelling-house, and its value exceeds ten naira, or the offender at or immediately before or after the time of stealing uses or threatens to use violence to any person in the dwelling-house;
(c) if the thing is stolen from any kind of vessel or vehicle or place of deposit used for the conveyance or custody of goods in transit from one place to another;
(d) if the thing stolen is attached to or forms part of a railway;
(e) if the thing is stolen from a vessel which is in distress or wrecked or stranded;
(f) if the thing is stolen from a public office in which it is deposited or kept;
(g) if the offender, in order to commit the offence, opens any locked room, box, or other receptacle, by means of a key or other instrument, the offender is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Stealing by persons in public service
(5) If the offender is a person employed in the public service and the thing stolen is the property of the State, or came into the possession of the offender by virtue of his employment, he is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Stealing by clerks and servants
(6) If the offender is a clerk or servant and the thing stolen is the property of his employer or came into the possession of the offender on account of his employer, he is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Stealing by directors or officers of companies
(7) If the offender is a director or officer of a corporation or company, and the thing stolen is the property of the corporation or company, he is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Stealing by agents, etc.
(8) If the thing stolen is any of the following things-
(a) property which has been received by the offender with a power of attorney for the disposition thereof;
(b) property which has been entrusted to the offender either alone or jointly with any other person for him to retain in safe custody or to apply, pay or deliver for any purpose or to any person the same or any part thereof or any proceeds thereof;
(c) property which has been received by the offender either alone or jointly with any other person for or on account of any other person;
(d) the whole or part of the proceeds of any valuable security which has been received by the offender with a direction that the proceeds thereof should be applied to any purpose or paid to any person specified in the direction;
(e) the whole or part of the proceeds arising from any disposition of any property which have been received by the offender by virtue of a power of attorney for such disposition, such power of attorney having been received by the offender with a direction that such proceeds should be applied to any purpose or paid to any person specified in the direction, the offender is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Stealing property of value of N1,000
(9) If the thing stolen is of the value of one thousand naira or upwards, the offender is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Stealing by tenants or lodgers
(10) If the thing stolen is a fixture or chattel let to the offender to be used by him with a house or lodging, and its value exceeds ten naira, he is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
(10A) If the thing stolen is a motor vehicle or motor cycle the offender shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for not less than five years but not more than seven years without the option of a fine.
Stealing after previous conviction
(11) If the offender, before committing the offence, has been convicted of any of the felonies or misdemeanors defined in this division of this Part of this Code, he is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for stealing. Person wey steal anything wey fit dem steal don commit felony (serious crime). If law no give another punishment, di punishment na prison for 3 years. For will, or postal matter or wetin dey inside am, na prison for life. For horse, ass, mule, camel, bull, cow, ox, ram, ewe, goat, pig or dia young, na fine (money wey person go pay) of 200 naira or prison for 2 years. For motor vehicle or motor cycle, na prison for not less than 5 years but not more than 7 years, without option of fine. Na prison for 7 years for special cases, like stealing from person body, dwelling-house, vessel, vehicle, railway or public office, by public servant, clerk, servant, company officer or agent, property of 1,000 naira or more, or after earlier conviction. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Concealing registers
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to defraud, conceals or takes from its place of deposit any register which is authorised or required by law to be kept for authenticating or recording the title to any property, or for recording births, baptisms, marriages, deaths, or burials, or a copy of any part of any such register which is required by law to be sent to any public officer, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding registers. If person wey wan cheat hide, or take from im place of deposit, any register wey law require make dem keep to authenticate or record title to property, or record births, baptisms, marriages, deaths or burials, or copy of any part of am wey dem must send to public officer, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Concealing wills
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to defraud, conceals any testamentary instrument, whether the testator is living or dead, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding wills. If person wey wan cheat hide any will, whether di person wey make am dey alive or dead, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Concealing deeds
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to defraud, conceals the whole or part of any document which is evidence of title to any land or estate in land, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hiding deeds. If person wey wan cheat hide di whole or part of any document wey show title to land or estate for land, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Killing animals with intent to steal
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text: Any person who kills any animal capable of being stolen with intent to steal the skin or carcass, or any part of the skin or carcass, is guilty of an offence and is liable to the same punishment as if he had stolen the animal.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about killing animals to steal. If person kill any animal wey fit dem steal wey wan steal di skin or carcass, or any part of dem, e don commit crime. Di punishment na di same as if e steal di animal.

sections.title: Severing with intent to steal
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text: Any person who makes anything movable with the intent to steal it, is guilty of an offence and is liable to the same punishment as if he has stolen the thing after it had become movable.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about making something movable to steal am. If person make anything movable wey wan steal am, e don commit crime. Di punishment na di same as if e steal di thing after e don become movable.

sections.title: Fraudulently dealing with minerals in mines
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text: Any person who takes, conceals, or otherwise disposes of, any ore of any metal or mineral in or about a mine, with intent to defraud any person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cheating with minerals for mines. If person take, hide or dispose of any ore of any metal or mineral for or near mine, wey wan cheat any person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Bringing stolen goods into Nigeria
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
