sections.text: Any person who, having at any place not in Nigeria obtained any property by any act which if it had been done in Nigeria would have constituted the offence of stealing, and which is an offence under the laws in force in the place where it was done, brings such property into the country, or has it in his possession in Nigeria, is guilty of an offence, and is liable to the same punishment as if he had stolen it in Nigeria; but so that the punishment does not exceed that which would be incurred for the same act under the laws in force in the place where the act by which he obtained the property was done.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about bringing stolen goods enter Nigeria. If person get property for place wey no be Nigeria by act wey go be stealing if e happen for Nigeria and wey be offence under di law for dat place, and e bring am enter Nigeria or get am for im possession for Nigeria, e don commit crime. Di punishment na di same as if e steal am for Nigeria. But di punishment no go pass wetin di law for di place wey e do di act go give for di same act.

sections.title: Fraudulent disposition of mortgaged goods
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text:
Any person who, being the mortgagor of mortgaged goods, removes or disposes of the goods without the consent of the mortgagee and with intent to defraud, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cheating with mortgaged goods. If person wey give goods as security for debt (mortgagor) remove or dispose of di goods without agreement (say 'yes') of di person wey hold di security (mortgagee), wey wan cheat, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Definition of mortgaged goods; consent of mortgagee
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text:
In section 398 of this Code, the term "mortgaged goods" includes any goods and chattels of any kind, and any live animals, and any progeny of any animals and any crops or produce of the earth, whether growing or severed, which are subject for the time being to the provisions of the written instrument by which a valid charge or lien is created upon them by way of security of any debt or obligation.
The consent of the mortgagee may be either express or implied from the nature of the property mortgaged.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin mortgaged goods mean for section 398 of dis Code. 'Mortgaged goods' include any goods and chattels, live animals, dia young, and crops or produce of di earth, growing or cut, wey dey under written document wey valid charge or lien dey on top dem as security for debt or obligation. Di mortgagee agreement fit dey expressed or fit show from di nature of di property.

sections.title: Fraudulent appropriation of power
sections.chapter: Chapter 35: Offences analogous to stealing
sections.text:
Any person who fraudulently abstracts or diverts to his own use or to the use of any other person any mechanical, illuminating, or electrical power derived from any machine apparatus, or substance, the property of another person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cheating to use power. If person by cheating take or divert to im own use or to use of another person any mechanical, illuminating or electrical power wey come from machine, apparatus or substance wey be another person property, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Definition of robbery
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text: Any person who steals anything and, at or immediately before or immediately after the time of stealing it, uses or threatens to use actual violence to any person or property in order to obtain or retain the thing stolen or to prevent or overcome resistance to its being stolen or retained, is said to be guilty of robbery.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin robbery mean. If person steal anything and, at or just before or just after di stealing, use or threaten to use actual violence on any person or property to get or keep di thing, or to stop or overcome resistance to di stealing or keeping, e don commit robbery.

sections.title: Punishment of robbery
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text:
(1) Any person who commits the offence of robbery shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for not less than 21 years.
(2) If-
(a) any offender mentioned in subsection (1) of this section is armed with any firearms or any offensive weapon or any obnoxious or chemical materials or is in company with any person so armed; or
(b) at or immediately before or immediately after the time of robbery the said offender wounds any person, the offender shall upon conviction be sentenced to death.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for robbery. Person wey commit robbery go get prison for not less than 21 years. But if di offender carry firearms, offensive weapon or harmful or chemical materials, or dey with person wey carry dem, or if at or just before or just after di robbery e wound any person, di court go sentence am to death.

sections.title: Punishment for attempted robbery, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text:
(1) Any person who with intent to steal anything, assaults any other person and at or immediately after the time of assault, uses or threatens to use actual violence to any other person or any property in order to obtain the thing intended to be stolen shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for not less than fourteen years but not more than twenty years. [1970 No. 47.]
(2) If-
(a) any offender mentioned in subsection (1) of this section, is armed with any firearms or any offensive weapon or is in company with any other person so armed; or
(b) at or immediately before or immediately after the time of the assault the offender wounds or uses any other personal violence to any person, the offender shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for life with or without whipping.
(3) Any person found in any public place in possession of any firearms, whether real or imitation, and in circumstances reasonably indicating that the possession of the firearms is with intent to the immediate or eventual commission by that person or any other person of any offence under section 402 of this Code shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for not less than fourteen years or more than twenty years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for attempted robbery and related acts. If person wey wan steal anything assault another person and, at or just after di assault, use or threaten to use actual violence on any person or property to get di thing, di court go give am prison for not less than 14 years but not more than 20 years. If di offender carry firearms or offensive weapon, or dey with person wey carry dem, or wound or use any other personal violence on person, di punishment na prison for life, with or without whipping. Person wey dem find for public place with firearms, real or imitation, for situation wey show say e wan use am to commit offence under section 402 of dis Code, go get prison for not less than 14 years or more than 20 years.

sections.title: Conspiracy to commit robbery
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text: Any person who conspires with any person to commit an offence under section 402 of this Code, whether or not he is present when the offence is committed or attempted to be committed, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence as a principal offender and shall be punished accordingly.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about planning together to commit robbery. If person plan together with any person to commit offence under section 402 of dis Code, whether e dey there when dem commit or try to commit am or e no dey there, dem go count am as principal offender and dem go punish am as such.

sections.title: Definition of firearms and offensive weapons
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin firearms and offensive weapon mean for sections 402, 403 and 403A of dis Code. 'Firearms' include canon, gun, flint-lock gun, revolver, pistol, explosive, ammunition or other firearm, whole or for pieces. 'Offensive weapon' na any article wey no be firearm, wey dem make or adapt to cause injury to person, or wey di person wey get am wan use for dat way. E include air gun, air pistol, bow and arrow, spear, cutlass, matchet, dagger, cudgel, or any wood, metal, glass or stone wey fit dem use as offensive weapon.

sections.title: Public servants demanding property, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text:
(1) Any person who, being employed in the public service of Nigeria, or in that of any other government, corruptly and under colour of his employment-
(a) demands or takes property from any person; or
(b) compels any person to sell any property at other than its fair market value; or
(c) obtains lodging from and against the will of any person without payment or for inadequate payment; or
(d) compels, whether partially or wholly for his own profit, any person to work without payment or for inadequate payment, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
(2) Any person who, falsely representing himself by words, conduct, or otherwise, to be a person employed in the public service of Nigeria, or of any other government, or to be an agent of or act under the authority of, the government, unlawfully and in such assumed character-
(a) does any of the acts or things specified in paragraphs (a), (b), (c), and (d) of subsection
(1) of this section; or
(b) compels or orders any person to hand any property over to any other person, whether such property does or does not rightly belong, or is or is not rightly due, to the last- named person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
(3) Any person attempting, or inciting, soliciting, counselling, procuring, aiding, or abetting any person to commit any of the offences enumerated in subsections (1) and (2) of this section, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for five years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about public servants wey dey demand property. If person wey dey work for public service of Nigeria, or of any other government, corruptly and under cover of im work, demand or take property from person; force person sell property for price wey no be fair market value; collect lodging against person will without payment or with small payment; or force person work without payment or with small payment, e don commit felony (serious crime). Person wey falsely show say e be public servant or agent of government and do any of dem for dat false character, or force or order person give property to another person, don also commit felony. Person wey try, incite, solicit, counsel, procure, aid or abet any of dem don also commit felony. Di punishment for each one na prison for 5 years.

sections.title: Assault with intent to steal
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text: Any person who assaults any person with intent to steal anything, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about assault to steal. If person assault any person wey wan steal anything, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Demanding property with menaces with intent to steal
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to steal anything, demands it from any person with threats of any injury or detriment of any kind to be caused to him, either by the offender or by any other person, if the demand is not complied with, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about demanding property with threats. If person wey wan steal anything demand am from person with threats of any injury or harm to am, by di offender or by another person, if dem no do wetin e demand, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Demanding property by written threats
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text: Any person who, with intent to extort or gain anything from any person, and knowing the contents of the writing, causes any person to receive any writing demanding anything from any person without reasonable or probable cause, and containing threats of any injury or detriment of any kind to be caused to any person, either by the offender or any other person, if the demand is not complied with, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about demanding property by written threats. If person wey wan force or gain anything from person, as e sabi say wetin dey di writing, cause person receive writing wey demand anything from person without reasonable or probable cause, and wey get threats of injury or harm to any person, by di offender or another person, if dem no do wetin e demand, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Attempts at extortion by threats
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to extort or gain anything from any person-
(1) accuses or threatens to accuse any person of committing any felony or misdemeanor, or of offering or making any solicitation or threat to any person as an inducement to commit or permit the commission of any felony or misdemeanor; or
(2) threatens that any person shall be accused by any other person of any felony or misdemeanor or of any such act; or
(3) knowing the contents of the writing, causes any person to receive any writing containing any such accusation or threat as aforesaid, is guilty of a felony and if the accusation or threat of accusation is of-
(a) an offence for which the punishment of death or imprisonment for life may be inflicted; or
(b) any of the offences defined in Chapter 21 of this Code, or an attempt to commit any of such offences; or
(c) an assault with intent to have carnal knowledge of any person against the order of nature, or an unlawful and indecent assault upon a male person; or
(d) an attempt to commit the offence of rape, or an assault with intent to commit the offence of rape, or an unlawful and indecent assault upon a woman or girl; or
(e) a solicitation or threat offered or made to any person as an inducement to commit or permit the commission of any of the offences aforesaid, the offender is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
In any other case, the offender is liable to imprisonment for three years.
It is immaterial whether the person accused or threatened to be accused has or has not committed the offence or act of which he is accused or threatened to be accused.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about accusing or threatening to accuse person to get something. If person wey wan force or gain anything from person accuses, or threatens to accuse, any person of felony or misdemeanour, or threatens say another person go accuse am, or causes person to receive writing wey get such accusation or threat, e don commit felony (serious crime). If di accusation or threat na for offence wey fit carry death or prison for life, or any offence for Chapter 21 of dis Code, or attempt or assault wey wan commit rape, or assault wey wan have sex against di order of nature, or indecent assault on any person, or solicitation or threat to induce any of dem, di punishment na prison for 14 years. For any other case, na prison for 3 years. E no matter if di person wey dem accuse commit di offence or no commit am.

sections.title: Procuring execution of deeds, etc., by threats
sections.chapter: Chapter 36: Stealing with violence: extortion by threats
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud, and by means of any unlawful violence to, or restraint of, the person of another, or by means of any threat of violence or restraint to be used to the person of another, or by means of accusing or threatening to accuse any person of committing any felony or misdemeanor, or by offering or making any solicitation or threat to any person as an inducement to commit or permit the commission of any offence, compels or induces any person-
(a) to execute, make, accept, endorse, alter, or destroy, the whole or any part of any valuable security; or
(b) to write, impress, or affix, any name or seal upon or to any paper or parchment, in order that it may be afterwards made or converted into or used or dealt with as a valuable security, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about forcing person to sign deeds by threats. If person wey wan cheat, by unlawful violence or restraint on person, or threat of violence or restraint, or by accusing or threatening to accuse person of felony or misdemeanour, or by offering or making solicitation or threat to induce offence, force or induce person to execute, make, accept, endorse, alter or destroy valuable security, whole or part, or to write or put name or seal on paper so dat dem go later use am as valuable security, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text:
A person who breaks any part, whether external or internal, of a building, or opens by unlocking, pulling, pushing, lifting, or any other means whatever, any door, window, shutter, cellar flap, or other thing, intended to close or cover an opening in a building, or an opening giving passage from one part of a building to another, is said to break the building.
A person is said to enter a building as soon as any part of his body or any part of any instrument used by him is within the building.
A person who obtains entrance into a building by means of any threat or artifice used for that purpose, or by collusion with any person in the building, or who enters any chimney or other aperture of the building permanently left open for any necessary purpose, but not intended to be ordinarily used as a means of entrance, is deemed to have broken and entered the building.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin some words mean for housebreaking. Person 'break' building if e break any part of am, outside or inside, or open by unlocking, pulling, pushing, lifting or any other means any door, window, shutter, cellar flap or other thing wey close or cover opening for building or between parts of building. Person 'enter' building as soon as any part of im body, or any instrument wey e use, dey inside. Person wey enter by threat or trick, or by collusion with person inside, or wey enter chimney or other opening wey dem permanently leave open for necessary purpose but no be normal way to enter, dem go count am say e break and enter.

sections.title: Housebreaking: burglary
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) breaks and enters the dwelling-house of another with intent to commit a felony therein; or
(2) having entered the dwelling-house of another with intent to commit a felony therein, or having committed a felony in the dwelling-house of another, breaks out of the dwelling-house, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
If the offence is committed in the night, the offender is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about housebreaking and burglary. If person break and enter another person dwelling-house wey wan commit felony inside, or, after e enter wey wan commit felony inside or after e commit felony inside, break out of am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years. But if e do am for night, di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Entering dwelling-house with intent to commit felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who enters or is in the dwelling-house of another with intent to commit a felony therein, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
If the offence is committed in the night, the offender is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about entering dwelling-house to commit felony. If person enter or dey inside another person dwelling-house wey wan commit felony inside, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. But if e do am for night, di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Breaking into building and committing felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) breaks and enters a schoolhouse, shop, warehouse, store, office, or counting-house, or a building which is adjacent to a dwelling-house and occupied with it but is not part of it, and commits a felony therein; or
(2) having committed a felony in a schoolhouse, shop, warehouse, store, office, or counting- house, or in any such other building as last mentioned, breaks out of the building, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about breaking into building and committing felony. If person break and enter schoolhouse, shop, warehouse, store, office or counting-house, or building wey dey near dwelling-house and dem occupy am with am but no be part of am, and commit felony inside, or, after e commit felony inside, break out of am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Breaking into building with intent to commit felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text: Any person who breaks and enters a schoolhouse, shop, warehouse, store, office, or counting-house, or a building which is adjacent to a dwelling-house and occupied with it but is not part of it, with intent to commit a felony therein, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about breaking into building to commit felony. If person break and enter schoolhouse, shop, warehouse, store, office or counting-house, or building wey dey near dwelling-house and dem occupy am with am but no be part of am, wey wan commit felony inside, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Breaking into place of worship and committing felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text: Any person who breaks and enters a building ordinarily used for religious worship and commits a felony therein, or having committed a felony in any such building breaks out of it, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about breaking into place of worship and committing felony. If person break and enter building wey dem ordinarily use for religious worship and commit felony inside, or, after e commit felony inside, break out of am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Breaking into place of worship with intent to commit felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.text: Any person who breaks and enters a building ordinarily used for religious worship, with intent to commit a felony therein, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about breaking into place of worship to commit felony. If person break and enter building wey dem ordinarily use for religious worship wey wan commit felony inside, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Persons found armed, etc., with intent to commit felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 37: Burglary: Housebreaking: and like offences
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about people wey dem find armed or prepared to commit felony. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if dem find am: armed with dangerous or offensive weapon wey wan break or enter dwelling-house to commit felony; armed so for night wey wan break or enter any building to commit felony; with instrument of housebreaking for night without lawful excuse, wey e must prove; with such instrument for day wey wan commit felony; with face masked or blackened or disguised wey wan commit felony; inside any building for night wey wan commit felony; or inside any building for day wey wan commit felony and don take steps to hide im presence. Di punishment na prison for 3 years. If di court don find am guilty before of felony about property, di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Definition
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text: Any representation made by words, writing, or conduct, of a matter of fact, either past or present, which representation is false in fact and which the person making it knows to be false or does not believe to be true, is a false pretence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin false pretence mean. False pretence na any statement wey person make by words, writing or conduct about matter of fact, past or present, wey false and wey di person sabi say e false or no believe say e true.

sections.title: Obtaining goods by false pretences
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
Any person who by any false pretence, and with intent to defraud, obtains from any other person anything capable of being stolen, or induces any other person to deliver to any person anything capable of being stolen, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
If the thing is of the value of one thousand naira or upwards, he is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
It is immaterial that the thing is obtained or its delivery is induced through the medium of a contract induced by the false pretence.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant unless found committing the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about getting goods by false pretence. If person by false pretence, wey wan cheat, get anything wey fit dem steal from another person, or make another person deliver am to any person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. If di thing value na 1,000 naira or more, di punishment na prison for 7 years. E no matter if e get am, or make dem deliver am, through contract wey di false pretence cause. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant) unless dem find am dey commit di offence.

sections.title: Obtaining credit by false pretences or other fraud
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
(1) Any person who by any false pretence or by means of any other fraud obtains credit for himself or any other person- [1966 No. 84.]
(a) in incurring any debt or liability; or
(b) by means of an entry in a debtor and creditor account between the person giving and the person receiving credit, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
(2) The offender cannot be arrested without warrant unless found committing the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about getting credit by false pretence or other fraud. If person, by false pretence or any other fraud, get credit for imself or another person by incurring debt or liability, or by entry for debtor and creditor account between person wey give credit and person wey receive am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant) unless dem find am dey commit di offence.

sections.title: Presumption as to false pretences in certain circumstances
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
Where in any proceedings for an offence under section 419 or 4l9A of this Code it is proved that the accused- [1966 No. 84.]
(a) obtained or induced the delivery of anything capable of being stolen; or
(b) obtained credit for himself or any other person, by means of a cheque that, when presented for payment within a reasonable time, was dishonoured on the ground that no funds or insufficient funds were standing to the credit of the drawer of the cheque in the bank on which the cheque was drawn, the thing or its delivery shall be deemed to have been obtained or induced, or the credit shall be deemed to have been obtained, by a false pretence, unless the court is satisfied by evidence that when the accused issued the cheque he had reasonable grounds for believing, and did in fact believe, that it would be honoured if presented within a reasonable time after its issue by him.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about when di court go presume say na false pretence. For case under section 419 or 419A of dis Code, if dem prove say di accused get anything wey fit dem steal, or get credit for imself or another person, with cheque wey bank refuse to pay when dem present am within reasonable time because di drawer account no get money or no get enough money, di court go take am say na false pretence. But e no go be so if evidence satisfy di court say, when di accused issue di cheque, e get reasonable ground to believe, and truly believe, say bank go pay am if dem present am within reasonable time.

sections.title: Obtaining execution of a security by false pretences
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
Any person who by any false pretence, and with intent to defraud, induces any person to execute, make, accept, endorse, alter, or destroy, the whole or any part of any valuable security, or to write, impress, or affix, any name or seal upon or to any paper or parchment in order that it may be afterwards made or converted into or used or dealt with as a valuable security, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant unless found committing the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about getting signature on security by false pretence. If person by false pretence, wey wan cheat, make person execute, make, accept, endorse, alter or destroy valuable security, whole or part, or write or put name or seal on paper so dat dem go later use am as valuable security, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant) unless dem find am dey commit di offence.

sections.title: Cheating
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
Any person who by means of any fraudulent trick or device obtains from any other person anything capable of being stolen, or induces any other person to deliver to any person anything capable of being stolen or to pay or deliver to any person any money or goods, or any greater sum of money or greater quantity of goods than he would have paid or delivered but for such trick or device, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
A person found committing the offence may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cheating. If person by fraudulent trick or device get anything wey fit dem steal from another person, or make another person deliver am to any person, or pay or deliver any money or goods, or more money or goods than e for pay or deliver without di trick, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Police fit arrest person wey dem find dey commit di offence without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Conspiracy to defraud
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
Any person who conspires with another by deceit or any fraudulent means to affect the market price of anything publicly sold, or to defraud the public or any person, whether a particular person or not, or to extort any property from any person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about planning together to cheat. If person plan together with another person, by deceit or fraudulent means, to affect di market price of anything wey dem sell for public, or to cheat di public or any person, whether particular person or no, or to force property from any person, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Frauds on sale or mortgage of property
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text:
Any person who, being a seller or mortgagor of any property, or being the solicitor or agent of any such seller or mortgagor, with intent to induce the purchaser or mortgagee to accept the title offered or produced to him, and with intent to defraud-
(1) conceals from the purchaser or mortgagee any instrument material to the title, or any encumbrance; or
(2) falsifies any pedigree on which the title depends or may depend; or
(3) makes any false statement as to the title offered or conceals any fact material thereto, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about frauds when dem sell or mortgage property. If seller or mortgagor of property, or im solicitor or agent, wey wan make buyer or mortgagee accept di title wey dem offer, and wey wan cheat, hide from am any document wey matter for di title or any encumbrance; falsify any pedigree wey di title depend on; or make false statement about di title or hide any fact wey matter for am, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Pretending to exercise witchcraft or tell fortunes
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text: Any person who for gain or reward pretends to exercise or use any kind of witchcraft, juju, sorcery, enchantment, or conjuration, or undertakes to tell fortunes, or pretends from his skill or knowledge in any occult science to discover where or in what manner anything supposed to have been stolen or lost may be found, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about pretending to use witchcraft or tell fortunes. If person for gain or reward pretend to use any kind of witchcraft, juju, sorcery, enchantment or conjuration, or agree to tell fortunes, or pretend, from im skill or knowledge for occult science, to find where or how anything wey dem suppose steal or lost fit dey found, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Obtaining registration, etc., by false pretence
sections.chapter: Chapter 38: Obtaining property by false pretences: cheating
sections.text: Any person who wilfully procures or attempts to procure for himself or any other person any registration, licence or certificate under any Act or law or under any regulation made under the Nigerian (Constitution) Order in Council, 1951, or the Nigerian (Constitution) order in Council, 1954, or the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, by any false pretence, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and is liable to imprisonment for one year. [L.N. 155 of 1960. Cap. C23.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about getting registration, licence or certificate by false pretence. If person on purpose get, or try to get, for imself or another person any registration, licence or certificate under any Act or law, or under regulation wey dem make under di Nigerian (Constitution) Order in Council, 1951 or 1954, or di Constitution of di Federal Republic of Nigeria, by false pretence, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Receiving stolen property, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who receives anything which has been obtained by means of any act constituting a felony or misdemeanor, or by means of any act done at a place not in Nigeria, which if it had been done in Nigeria would have constituted a felony or misdemeanor, and which is an offence under the laws in force in the place where it was done, knowing the same to have been so obtained, is guilty of a felony.
If the offence by means of which the thing was obtained is a felony, the offender is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years, except in the case in which the thing so obtained was postal matter, or any chattel, money or valuable security contained therein, in which case the offender is liable to imprisonment for life.
In any other case the offender is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
For the purpose of proving the receiving of anything, it is sufficient to show that the accused person has, either alone or jointly with some other person, had the thing in his possession, or has aided in concealing it or disposing of it.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about receiving stolen property. If person receive anything wey dem get by act wey be felony or misdemeanour, or by act wey dem do for place wey no be Nigeria wey go be felony or misdemeanour if dem do am for Nigeria and wey be offence under di law for dat place, as e sabi say dem get am so, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years if di offence wey dem use get di thing na felony, and prison for life if di thing na postal matter or chattel, money or valuable security wey dey inside am. For any other case, na prison for 7 years. To prove say person receive thing, e dey enough to show say di accused, alone or with another person, don get am for im possession, or don help hide am or dispose of am.

sections.title: Unlawful possession of arms, etc., belonging to armed or police forces
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(a) knowingly detains, buys, exchanges, or receives, from any non-commissioned officer or private of the armed forces of Nigeria or from any member of the police forces, or from any deserter from either of such forces, or from any person acting for and on behalf of any of the persons above named; or
(b) solicits or entices any of the said persons to sell, make away with, or dispose of; or
(c) shall be employed by any of the said persons, well knowing him to belong to one or other of such forces in one of the several capacities hereinbefore mentioned, or to be a deserter from any of the said forces, to sell, make away with, or dispose of; or
(d) shall have in his possession and not give a satisfactory account of his possession of any arms, ammunition, clothing, accoutrements, medals or other appointments, furnished for the use of the armed forces of Nigeria or of the police forces, is liable to a fine of forty naira and to pay double the value of all or any of the several articles which he shall so become or be possessed of.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about having arms of di armed forces or police forces for wrong way. Person go face fine (money wey person go pay) of 40 naira, and e go pay double di value of di articles wey e get, if e: as e sabi say hold, buy, exchange or receive from non-commissioned officer or private of di armed forces of Nigeria, or member of di police forces, or deserter, or person wey dey act for dem; solicit or entice any of dem to sell or dispose of; be employed by any of dem, well knowing say e belong to dem or say e be deserter, to sell or dispose of; or get any arms, ammunition, clothing, accoutrements, medals or other appointments wey dem supply for di armed forces or police forces and no give satisfactory account of how e get am.

sections.title: Receiving after change of ownership
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text: When a thing has been obtained by means of any act constituting a felony or misdemeanor, or by means of an act done at a place not in Nigeria, which if it had been done in Nigeria would have constituted an offence, and which is an offence under the laws in force in the place where it was done, and another person has acquired a lawful title to it, a subsequent receiving of the thing is not an offence although the receiver knows that the thing had previously been so obtained.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about receiving after change of ownership. If dem get thing by act wey be felony or misdemeanour, or by act for place wey no be Nigeria wey go be offence for Nigeria and wey be offence under di law for dat place, and another person don get lawful title to am, if person receive am after dat, e no be offence, even if di receiver sabi say dem get am so before.

sections.title: Having possession of thing reasonably suspected of having been stolen
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text:
(1) Any person who is charged before any court with having in his possession or under his control in any manner or in any place, or for that he at any time within the three months immediately preceding the making of the complaint, did have in his possession or under his control in any manner or in any place, anything which is reasonably suspected of having been stolen or unlawfully obtained, and who does not give an account, to the satisfaction of the court, as to how he came by the same, is guilty of an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of two hundred naira or to imprisonment for six months.
(2) Where any person is charged before any court with having or with having had in his possession or under his control in any manner or in any place anything which has been stolen or unlawfully obtained, or which is reasonably suspected of having been stolen or unlawfully obtained, and declares that he received the same for some other person or that he was employed as a carrier, agent or servant for some other person, the court is hereby authorised and required, if practicable, to cause every such other person and also if necessary every former or pretended purchaser or other person through whose possession such thing as aforesaid has passed or who has had control thereof, to be brought before it and to examine witnesses upon oath touching the same; and if it appears to the court that any person has had possession or control of such thing and had reasonable cause to believe the same to have been stolen or unlawfully obtained, every such person shall be deemed to have had possession or control of such thing at the time and place when and where the same was found or seized, and is guilty of an offence and liable, on conviction to a fine of two hundred naira or to imprisonment for six months.
(3) The possession of or control by a carrier, agent or servant shall be deemed to be the possession of or control by the person who employed such carrier, agent or servant to have or deal with such thing and such person shall be liable on conviction to the punishment herein mentioned.
(4) The offender may be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about having thing wey dem reasonably suspect say dem steal. If person dey before court for having, or for having within di 3 months before di complaint, anything wey dem reasonably suspect say dem steal or get unlawfully, and e no give account wey satisfy di court about how e get am, e don commit crime. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 200 naira or prison for 6 months. If di person say e receive am for another person, or say e na carrier, agent or servant, di court must, if e possible, bring dat person and any other person wey di thing pass through, and examine witnesses for oath. Person wey get di thing and get reasonable cause to believe say dem steal am don also commit crime with di same punishment. Police fit arrest di offender without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Unlawfully using animals or vehicles
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully uses a horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, ostrich, bull, cow, ox, ram, ewe, wether, goat, or pig, or the young of any such animal, or any cycle or other vehicle whatsoever without the consent of the owner, or of the person in lawful possession thereof, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and is liable to imprisonment for one year, or to a fine of forty naira for every animal or vehicle so used.
The offender may be arrested without warrant by a police officer, or by the owner of the property in question, or his servant, or by any person authorised by such owner or servant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about using animals or vehicles for wrong way. If person for wrong way use horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, ostrich, bull, cow, ox, ram, ewe, wether, goat or pig, or dia young, or any cycle or other vehicle, without agreement (say 'yes') of di owner or person wey get lawful possession, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year, or fine of 40 naira for every animal or vehicle wey e use. Police officer, di owner, im servant or person wey dem authorise fit arrest di offender without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Suspicion of stealing animals
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text:
When any horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, ostrich, bull, cow, ox, ram, ewe, wether, goat, or pig, or the young of any of such animal is suspected, on reasonable grounds, to have been stolen, any person in whose possession or custody the skin, feathers or carcass, or any part of the skin or carcass, of the animal or bird so suspected to have been stolen, is found, is guilty of an offence, unless he proves that he came lawfully by the thing in question; and he is liable to a fine of one hundred naira.
The offender may be arrested without warrant by a police officer, or by the owner of the property in question, or his servant, or by any person authorised by such owner or servant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about suspicion of stealing animals. If dem reasonably suspect say dem steal horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, ostrich, bull, cow, ox, ram, ewe, wether, goat or pig, or dia young, person wey dem find skin, feathers or carcass, or any part of dem, for im possession or custody don commit crime. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of 100 naira. Police officer, di owner, im servant or person wey dem authorise fit arrest di offender without court paper (warrant). E get one defence (reason wey di law accept): di person fit prove say e get di thing for right way (di law allow am).

sections.title: Taking reward for recovery of property obtained by means of felony or misdemeanour
sections.chapter: Chapter 39: Receiving property stolen or fraudulently obtained and like offences
sections.text: Any person who corruptly receives or obtains, or corruptly agrees to receive or obtain, any property or benefit of any kind upon an agreement or understanding that he will help any person to recover anything which has been obtained by means of any act constituting a felony or misdemeanor, or by means of any act done at a place not in Nigeria, which if it had been done in Nigeria would have constituted an offence, and which is an offence under the laws in force in the place where it was done, is, unless he has used all due diligence to cause the offender to be brought to trial for the offence, guilty of a felony, and liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about taking reward to recover property wey dem get by felony or misdemeanour. If person corruptly receive or obtain, or corruptly agree to receive or obtain, property or benefit of any kind on agreement say e go help person recover anything wey dem get by act wey be felony or misdemeanour, or by act for place wey no be Nigeria wey go be offence for Nigeria and wey be offence under di law for dat place, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. But e no be crime if e don use all due diligence to cause di offender to go trial for di offence.

sections.title: Trustees fraudulently disposing of trust property
sections.chapter: Chapter 40: Frauds by trustees and officers of companies and corporations: false accounting
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trustees wey fraudulently dispose of trust property. If trustee destroy property wey e wan cheat, or, wey e wan cheat, use di property for way wey di trust no authorise, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant). If person don take civil case against trustee for any act wey be offence under dis section, dem no fit afterwards prosecute am for di same cause on complaint of di person wey take di civil case, unless di court or judge wey hear or dey hear di civil case sanction am. 'Trustee' include only: trustees under express trusts wey dem create by deed, will or writing; trustees wey Act, law or statute appoint; persons wey di duties of such trust pass to; and executors and administrators.

sections.title: Directors and officers of corporations or companies fraudulently appropriating property or keeping fraudulent accounts, or falsifying books or accounts
sections.chapter: Chapter 40: Frauds by trustees and officers of companies and corporations: false accounting
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) being a director or officer of a corporation or company, receives or possesses himself as such of any of the property of the corporation or company otherwise than in payment of a just debt or demand, and, with intent to defraud, omits either to make a full and true entry thereof in the books and accounts of the corporation or company, or to cause or direct such an entry to be made therein; or
(2) being a director, officer, or member of a corporation or company, does any of the following acts with intent to defraud-
(a) destroys, alters, mutilates, or falsifies, any book, document, valuable security, or account, which belongs to the corporation or company, or any entry in any such book, documents, or account, or is privy to any such act; or
(b) makes or is privy to making any false entry in any such book, document or account; or
(c) omits or is privy to omitting any material particular from any such book, document or account, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about directors and officers wey fraudulently take property or falsify books. Person don commit felony (serious crime) if: as director or officer of corporation or company, e receive or take any of im property, no be payment of just debt or demand, and wey e wan cheat no enter am fully and truly for im books and accounts or cause am to dey entered; or, as director, officer or member, wey e wan cheat, e destroy, alter, mutilate or falsify any book, document, valuable security or account wey belong to di corporation or company, or any entry for am, or know about am; make or know about making false entry; or leave out or know about leaving out any material particular. Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: False statements by officials of companies
sections.chapter: Chapter 40: Frauds by trustees and officers of companies and corporations: false accounting
sections.text:
Any person who, being a promoter, director, officer, or auditor, of a corporation or company, either existing or intended to be formed, makes, circulates, or publishes, or concurs in making, circulating, or publishing, any written statement or account which in any material particular, is to his knowledge false, with intent thereby to effect any of the following purposes-
(a) to deceive or to defraud any member, shareholder, or creditor, of the corporation or company, whether a particular person or not;
(b) to induce any person, whether a particular person or not, to become a member of, or to entrust or advance any property to, the corporation or company, or to enter into any security for the benefit thereof, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false statements by company officials. If promoter, director, officer or auditor of corporation or company, existing or wey dem wan form, make, circulate or publish, or agree to make, circulate or publish, any written statement or account wey, as e sabi, false for any material particular, wey wan deceive or cheat any member, shareholder or creditor, or wey wan induce any person to become member of, or to entrust or advance property to, di corporation or company, or to enter any security for im benefit, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Defence
sections.chapter: Chapter 40: Frauds by trustees and officers of companies and corporations: false accounting
sections.text:
It is a defence to a charge of any of the offences defined in this Chapter to prove that the accused person, before being charged with the offence, and in consequence of the compulsory process of a court in any action or proceedings instituted in good faith by a party aggrieved, or in a compulsory examination or deposition before a court, disclosed on oath the act alleged to constitute the offence.
A person is not entitled to refuse to answer any question or interrogatory in any civil proceeding in any court, on the ground that his doing so might tend to show that he had committed any such offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about defence (reason wey di law accept) for crimes for dis Chapter. Di accused fit prove say, before dem charge am, because of compulsory process of court for action or proceedings wey party wey dem wrong start for good faith, or for compulsory examination or deposition before court, e disclose di act for oath. Person no fit refuse to answer question for any civil proceeding for any court because e fit show say e commit any such offence.

sections.title: Fraudulent false accounting
sections.chapter: Chapter 40: Frauds by trustees and officers of companies and corporations: false accounting
sections.text:
Any person who, being a clerk or servant, or being employed or acting in the capacity of a clerk or servant, does any of the following acts with intent to defraud-
(a) destroys, alters, mutilates, or falsifies, any book, document, valuable security, or account, which belongs to or is in the possession of his employer, or has been received by him on account of his employer, or any entry in any such book, document, or account, or is privy to any such act; or
(b) makes, or is privy to making any false entry in any such book, document, or account; or
(c) omits, or is privy to omitting, any material particular from any such book, document, or account, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about fraudulent false accounting by clerk or servant. If clerk or servant, or person wey dey act as one, do any of dis wey e wan cheat: destroy, alter, mutilate or falsify any book, document, valuable security or account wey belong to or dey im employer possession, or wey e receive for im employer, or any entry for am, or know about am; make or know about making false entry; or leave out or know about leaving out any material particular, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: False accounting by public officer
sections.chapter: Chapter 40: Frauds by trustees and officers of companies and corporations: false accounting
sections.text: Any person who, being an officer charged with the receipt, custody, or management of any part of the public revenue, knowingly furnishes any false statement or return of any money or property received by him or entrusted to his care, or of any balance of money or property in his possession or under his control, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false accounting by public officer. If officer wey dem charge with receipt, custody or management of any part of public revenue knowingly give false statement or return of money or property wey e receive or dem entrust to am, or of any balance wey dey im possession or control, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Unlawful acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 41: Definitions
sections.text:
An act which causes injury to the property of another, and which is done without his consent, is unlawful unless it is authorised or justified or excused by law.
It is immaterial that the person who does the injury is in possession of the property injured or has a partial interest in it.
A person is not criminally responsible for any injury caused to property by the use of such force as is reasonably necessary for the purpose of defending or protecting himself, or any other person, or any property, from injury which he believes, on reasonable grounds, to be imminent.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin unlawful act mean for property. Act wey injure another person property and wey dem do without im agreement (say 'yes') dey for wrong way (against di law), unless law authorise, justify or excuse am. E no matter if di person wey do di injury dey possession of di property or get part interest for am. But person no go answer for crime for injury to property wey e cause by using force wey reasonably necessary to defend or protect imself, another person or property from injury wey e believe, with good reason, say e go happen soon.

sections.title: Acts done with intent to defraud
sections.chapter: Chapter 41: Definitions
sections.text:
When an act which causes injury to property, and which would be otherwise lawful, is done with intent to defraud any person, it is unlawful.
When an act which causes injury to property is done with intent to defraud any person, it is immaterial that the property in question is the property of the offender himself.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about acts wey dem do to cheat. If act wey injure property, wey for normal dey lawful, dem do am wey wan cheat person, e dey for wrong way (against di law). If act wey injure property dem do am wey wan cheat person, e no matter if di property na di offender own.

sections.title: Damage
sections.chapter: Chapter 41: Definitions
sections.text: The term "damage" used in relation to a document, or to a writing or inscription, includes obliterating and rendering illegible, either in whole or in part.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin damage mean. For document, writing or inscription, 'damage' include to rub out am or make am no fit read, whole or part.

sections.title: Arson
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about arson. If person on purpose set fire to any building or structure, complete or no complete; any vessel, complete or no complete; any stack of cultivated vegetable produce, or of mineral or vegetable fuel; or mine, or im workings, fittings or appliances, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Attempts to commit arson
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) attempts unlawfully to set fire to any such thing as is mentioned in section 443 of this Code; or
(2) wilfully and unlawfully sets fire to anything which is so situated that any such thing as is mentioned in section 443 of this Code is likely to catch fire from it, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to commit arson. If person try for wrong way (against di law) to set fire to any thing wey section 443 of dis Code mention, or on purpose and for wrong way set fire to anything wey dey for place wey any such thing fit catch fire from am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Setting fire to crops and growing plants
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about setting fire to crops and growing plants. If person on purpose and for wrong way (against di law) set fire to crop of cultivated vegetable produce, standing or cut; crop of hay or grass wey dem dey cultivate, natural or indigenous product of di soil or no, standing or cut; or any standing trees, saplings or shrubs wey dem dey cultivate, indigenous or no, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Attempting to set fire to crops, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(a) attempts unlawfully to set fire to any such thing as is mentioned in section 445 of this Code; or
(b) wilfully and unlawfully sets fire to anything which is so situated that any such thing as is mentioned in section 445 of this Code is likely to catch fire from it, is guilty of felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to set fire to crops and similar things. If person try for wrong way (against di law) to set fire to any thing wey section 445 of dis Code mention, or on purpose and for wrong way set fire to anything wey dey for place wey any such thing fit catch fire from am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Casting away ships
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) wilfully and unlawfully casts away or destroys any vessel, whether complete or not; or
(2) wilfully and unlawfully does any act which tends to the immediate loss or destruction of a vessel in distress; or
(3) with intent to bring a vessel into danger, interferes with any light, beacon, buoy, mark, or signal used for purposes of navigation, or exhibits any false light or signal, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about casting away ships. If person on purpose and for wrong way (against di law) cast away or destroy any vessel, complete or no complete; do any act wey go cause immediate loss or destruction of vessel wey dey in distress; or, wey wan bring vessel into danger, interfere with any light, beacon, buoy, mark or signal wey dem use for navigation, or show false light or signal, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Attempts to cast away ships
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who attempts unlawfully to cast away or destroy a vessel, whether completed or not, or attempts unlawfully to do any act tending to the immediate loss or destruction of a vessel in distress, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to cast away ships. If person try for wrong way (against di law) to cast away or destroy vessel, complete or no complete, or try for wrong way to do any act wey go cause immediate loss or destruction of vessel wey dey in distress, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Obstructing and injuring railways
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who unlawfully and with intent to obstruct the use of a railway or to injure any property upon a railway-
(1) deals with the railway or with anything whatever upon or near the railway in such a manner as to affect or endanger the free and safe use of the railway; or
(2) shows any light or signal, or in any way deal with any existing light or signal, upon or near the railway; or
(3) by any omission to do any act which it is his duty to do, causes the free and safe use of the railway to be endangered, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about blocking and injuring railways. If person for wrong way (against di law), wey wan block di use of railway or injure any property for railway, do anything with di railway or anything for or near am for way wey affect or endanger di free and safe use of am; show light or signal, or tamper with existing light or signal, near di railway; or, by failing to do act wey be im duty, cause di free and safe use of di railway to dey endangered, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life.

sections.title: Injuring animals
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who wilfully and unlawfully kills, maims, or wounds, any animal capable of being stolen, is guilty of an offence.
If the animal in question is a horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, bull, cow, ox, goat, pig, ram, wether, or ostrich, or the young of any such animal, the offender is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
In any other case the offender is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about hurting animals. If person kill, maim or wound any animal wey person fit steal, on purpose and for wrong way (against di law), e don commit crime. If di animal na horse, mare, gelding, ass, mule, camel, bull, cow, ox, goat, pig, ram, wether or ostrich, or di young one of any of dem, e na felony (serious crime) and e go face prison for 7 years. For any other animal, e na misdemeanour (small crime) and e go face prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Malicious injuries in general
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who wilfully and unlawfully destroys or damages any property, is guilty of an offence, which, unless otherwise stated, is a misdemeanor and he is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to imprisonment for two years.
Punishment in special cases Destroying or damaging an inhabited house or a vessel with explosives
(1) If the property in question is a dwelling-house or a vessel, and the injury is caused by the explosion of any explosive substance, and if-
(a) any person is in the dwelling-house or vessel; or
(b) the destruction or damage actually endangers the life of any person, the offender is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
River bank or wall, or navigation works, or bridges
(2) (a) If the property in question is a bank or wall of a river, canal, aqueduct, reservoir, or inland water, and the injury causes actual danger of inundation or damage to any land or building; or
(b)
(c) if the property in question is a railway, or is a bridge, viaduct, or aqueduct, which is constructed over a highway, railway or canal, or over which a railway, highway, or canal passes, and the property is destroyed; or if the property in question, being a railway, or being any such bridge, viaduct, or aqueduct, is damaged, and the damage is done with intent to render the railway, bridge, viaduct, or aqueduct, or the highway, railway, or canal passing over or under the same, or any part thereof, dangerous or impassable, and the same or any part thereof is thereby rendered dangerous or impassable, the offender is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for life.
Wills and registers
(3) If the property in question is a testamentary instrument, whether the testator is living or dead, or a register which is authorised or required by law to be kept for authenticating or recording the title to any property, or for recording births, baptisms, marriages, deaths, or burials, or a copy of any part of any such register which is required by law to be sent to any public officer, the offender is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
Wrecks
(4) If the property in question is a vessel in distress or wrecked, or stranded, or anything which belongs to such vessel, the offender is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Railways
(5) If the property in question is any part of a railway, or any work connected with a railway, the offender is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
Other things of special value
(6) (a) if the property in question, being a vessel, whether complete or not, is destroyed; or
(b) if the property in question, being a vessel, whether complete or not, is damaged, and the damage is done with intent to destroy it or render it useless; or manufacturing machine, or a manufacturing implement, or a machine or appliance used or intended to be used for performing any process connected with the preparation of any agricultural or pastoral produce, is destroyed; or
(c) if the property in question is a light, beacon, buoy, mark, or signal, used for the purposes of navigation, or for the guidance of persons engaged in navigation; or
(d) if the property in question is a bank or wall of a river, canal, aqueduct, reservoir, or inland water, or a work which appertains to a dock, canal, aqueduct, reservoir, or inland water, or which is used for the purposes of lading or unlading goods; or
(e) if the property in question, being a railway, or being a bridge, viaduct, or aqueduct, which is constructed over a highway, railway or canal, or over which a highway, railway, or canal passes, is damaged, and the damage is done with intent to render the railway, bridge, viaduct, or aqueduct, or the highway, railway, or canal, passing over or under the same, or any part thereof, dangerous or impassable; or
(f) if the property in question, being anything in process of manufacture, or an agricultural or an agricultural or manufacturing machine, or a manufacturing implement, or a machine or appliance used or intended to be used for performing any process connected with the preparation of any agricultural or pastoral produce, is destroyed ; or
(g) if the property in question, being any such thing, machine, implement, or appliance, as last aforesaid, is damaged, and the damage is done with intent to destroy the thing in question or to render it useless; or
(h) if the property in question is a shaft or a passage of a mine, and the injury is done with intent to damage the mine or to obstruct its working; or
(i) if the property in question is a machine, appliance, apparatus, building, erection, bridge, or road, appertaining to or used with a mine, whether the thing in question is completed or not; or
(f) if the property in question, being a rope, chain, or tackle, or whatever material, which is used in a mine, or upon any way or work appertaining to or used with a mine, is destroyed; or
(k) if the property in question, being any such rope, chain, or tackle, as last aforesaid, is damaged, and the damage is done with intent to destroy the thing in question or to render it useless; or
(I) if the property in question is a well, or bore for water, or the dam, bank, wall, or floodgate of a millpond or pool, the offender is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
Deeds and records
(7) If the property in question is a document which is deposited or kept in a public office, or which is evidence of title to any land or estate in land, the offender is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey destroy or damage property on purpose and for wrong way (against di law). E don commit misdemeanour (small crime) and e go face prison for 2 years if di law no give another punishment. For special cases e na felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for life if explosion damage house or vessel wey person dey inside or wey put life for danger, if river bank or wall damage cause flood danger, or if railway or bridge, viaduct or aqueduct wey dey over road, railway or canal get destroyed or damaged to make am dangerous or impassable. Di punishment na prison for 14 years for wills, birth, marriage and death registers, and railway property. Di punishment na prison for 7 years for wrecked vessels, vessels, machines, navigation lights, mine property, wells, and public office or land title documents. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Attempts to destroy property by explosives
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who, unlawfully and with intent to destroy or damage any property, puts any explosive substance in any place whatever, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about putting explosive for any place to destroy property. If person put explosive substance for any place for wrong way (against di law), wey wan destroy or damage any property, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Attempts to injure mines
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to injure a mine or to obstruct the working of a mine-
(1) unlawfully, and otherwise than by an act done underground in the course of working an adjoining mine-
(a) causes water to run into the mine or into any subterranean passage communicating with the mine; or
(b) obstructs any shaft or passage of the mine; or
(2) unlawfully obstructs the working of any machine, appliance, or apparatus, appertaining to or used with the mine, whether the thing in question is completed or not; or
(3) unlawfully and with intent to render it useless, injures or unfastens a rope, chain, or tackle of whatever material, which is used in the mine or upon any way or work appertaining to or used with the mine, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about person wey try to spoil a mine. If person wan injure di mine or stop di mine from working, and for wrong way (against di law) e let water enter am, block im shaft or passage, block any machine or equipment wey belong to am, or injure or loose rope, chain or tackle wey dem dey use for am so dat e go no work, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years. Di water or shaft part no cover act wey person do underground as e dey work for another mine wey dey beside am.

sections.title: Interfering with signals used for purposes of navigation
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who wilfully and unlawfully removes, defaces, or renders invisible, any light, beacon, buoy, mark or signal, used for purposes of navigation, or for the guidance of persons engaged in navigation, or unlawfully attempts to remove, deface or render invisible, any such thing, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about spoiling signals wey guide ships and boats. If person remove, spoil or hide any light, beacon, buoy, mark or signal wey dem dey use for navigation, on purpose and for wrong way (against di law), or try to do am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Interfering with navigation works
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) wilfully and unlawfully removes or disturbs any fixed objects or materials used for securing a bank or wall of a river, canal, aqueduct, reservoir, or inland water, or for securing any work which appertains to a dock, canal, aqueduct, reservoir, or inland water, or which is used for purposes of navigation or lading or unlading goods; or
(2) unlawfully does any act with intent to obstruct the carrying on, completion, or maintenance of the navigation of a navigable river or canal, and thereby obstructs such carrying on, completion, or maintenance, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about interfering with navigation works. E don commit felony (serious crime) if person remove or disturb fixed things wey dey hold di bank or wall of river, canal, aqueduct, reservoir or inland water, or wey dey hold work wey belong to dock or dey help navigation or loading and offloading goods, on purpose and for wrong way (against di law). E also be crime if person do any act for wrong way so dat e go block di work, completion or care of navigation of river or canal wey ship fit pass, and e really block am. Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Communicating infectious diseases to animals
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who wilfully and unlawfully causes, or is concerned in causing, or attempts to cause, any infectious disease to be communicated to or among any animal or animals capable of being stolen, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about spreading sickness to animals. If person cause, join to cause or try to cause infectious disease to reach animal or animals wey person fit steal, on purpose and for wrong way (against di law), e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Removing boundary marks with intent to defraud
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who wilfully and unlawfully, and with intent to defraud, removes or defaces any object or mark which has been lawfully erected or made as an indication of the boundary of any land, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about moving boundary marks to cheat person. If person remove or spoil any object or mark wey dem put for right way (di law allow am) to show di boundary of land, on purpose and for wrong way (against di law), by cheating, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Wilful damage, etc., to survey and boundary marks
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) wilfully removes, defaces or injures any survey mark or boundary mark which shall have been made or erected by or under the direction of any government department or in the course of or for the purposes of a government survey; or
(2) being under an obligation to maintain in repair any boundary mark made or erected as aforesaid, neglects or refuses to repair the same; or
(3) wilfully removes, defaces or injures any mark erected by an intending applicant for any lease, licence or right under the Minerals and Mining Act, [Cap.
