M12.] is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to imprisonment for three months or to a fine of forty naira, and may further be ordered by the court to pay the cost of repairing or replacing the survey mark or boundary mark and of making any survey rendered necessary by the offender's act or neglect.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about spoiling survey and boundary marks. If person remove, spoil or injure survey mark or boundary mark wey government department put or wey dem put for government survey, or if person wey must repair dat kind boundary mark no repair am, or refuse, or if person on purpose remove, spoil or injure mark wey person wey wan apply for lease, licence or right under di Minerals and Mining Act put, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 months or fine (money wey person go pay) of forty naira. Di court fit also order di person to pay di cost to repair or replace di mark and to do any survey wey im act or neglect make necessary.

sections.title: Obstructing railways
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who, by any unlawful act, or by any intentional omission to do any act which it is his duty to do, causes any engine or vehicle in use upon a railway to be obstructed in its passage on the railway, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about blocking railway. If person, by any act for wrong way (against di law) or by on purpose failing to do act wey na im duty, make engine or vehicle wey dey use railway no fit pass for di railway, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Obstructing aircraft
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who, by any unlawful act, obstructs, causes an alteration to be made in the course of, or in any way whatsoever hinders or impedes the movement of any aircraft, which is in motion on or in flight over any aerodrome, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about blocking aircraft. If person, by any act for wrong way (against di law), block aircraft, change di way e dey go, or hinder or stop di movement of aircraft wey dey move for aerodrome or dey fly over aerodrome, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Trespass on aerodrome
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who commits any nuisance or trespass in or upon any aerodrome or in or upon any building or premises situated on any aerodrome, is guilty of a simple offence and IS liable to imprisonment for three months or to a fine of forty naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trespass for aerodrome. If person do nuisance or trespass for any aerodrome, or for any building or place wey dey inside aerodrome, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 months or fine (money wey person go pay) of forty naira.

sections.title: Penalties for damage, etc., to railway works
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text:
Any person who-
(1) wilfully damages, injures, or obstructs any work, way, road, building, turnstile, gate, toll bar, fence, weighing machine, engine, tender, carriage, wagon, truck, material, or plant acquired for or belonging to any railway works; or
(2) pulls up, removes, defaces, or destroys, or in any way interferes with, any poles, stakes, flags, pegs, lines, marks, or anything driven or placed in or upon the ground, trees, stones, or building, or any other material, belonging to any railway works; or
(3) commits any nuisance or trespass in or upon any land, building, or premises, acquired for or belonging to any railway works; or
(4) wilfully molests, hinders, or obstructs, the officer in charge of any railway or his assistants or workmen in the execution of any work done or to be done in reference to the construction or maintenance of any such railway, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to imprisonment for three months or to a fine of forty naira.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about damage and wahala for railway works. E don commit simple offence (small crime) if person on purpose damage, injure or block any work, road, building, gate, fence, engine, carriage, wagon, material or plant wey belong to railway works; or pull up, remove, spoil, destroy or interfere with poles, stakes, flags, pegs, lines or marks wey belong to railway works; or do nuisance or trespass for land, building or place wey belong to railway works; or on purpose disturb or block di officer wey dey in charge of railway or im assistants or workmen as dem dey do work. Di punishment na prison for 3 months or fine (money wey person go pay) of forty naira.

sections.title: Sending letters threatening to burn or destroy
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: Any person who, knowing the contents of the writing, causes any person to receive any writing threatening that any building or vessel, whether complete or not, or any stack of cultivated vegetable produce, or any such produce that is in or under a building, shall be burnt or destroyed, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about letters wey threaten to burn or destroy things. If person, as e sabi di content, cause another person to receive writing wey threaten say dem go burn or destroy any building, vessel (even if dem never finish am), stack of cultivated farm produce, or farm produce wey dey inside or under building, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Arrest without warrant
sections.chapter: Chapter 42: Offences
sections.text: A person found committing any of the misdemeanors or simple offences defined in this Chapter of this Code may be arrested without warrant by a peace officer or a member of the police force, or by the owner of the property injured or his servant, or by any person authorised by such owner or servant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about arrest for di misdemeanours and simple offences for dis Chapter of dis Code. Police fit arrest person without court paper (warrant) if dem find am as e dey commit any of dem. Peace officer, member of di police force, di owner of di property wey dem injure, im servant, or any person wey di owner or servant authorise, fit arrest am without warrant.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.chapter: Chapter 43: Forgery in general: definitions
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain di meaning of some words for dis Division of dis Code. 'Bank note' mean any negotiable paper wey person, corporation, State, province or government for any part of di world issue to dey work like money, including bank bill, bank post bill, currency note or any note wey be legal tender for di country wey issue am. 'Document' mean register or register-book, book, paper, parchment or any material wey dem use write or print wey get letters or marks wey get clear meaning, but e no include trade marks on goods. 'Seal' mean stamp, die or anything wey fit make impression by pressure, ink or other way. 'Writing' mean inscription on wood, stone, metal or other material, and e include signature and any kind of mark.

sections.title: Further definitions
sections.chapter: Chapter 43: Forgery in general: definitions
sections.text:
A document or writing is said to be false-
(a) in the case of a document which is a register or record kept by lawful authority, or any entry in any such register, or which purports to be issued by lawful authority as testifying to the contents of any register or record kept by lawful authority, or as testifying to any facts or event, if any material particular stated in the document is untrue; or
(b) if the whole or some material part of the document or writing purports to be made by or on behalf of some person who did not make it or authorise it to be made, or if, in a case where the time or place of making is material, although the contents or writing is made by or by the authority of the person by whom it purports to be made, it is with a fraudulent intent falsely dated as to the time or place of making; or
(c) if the whole or some material part of the document or writing purports to be made by or on behalf of some person who does not in fact, exist; or
(d) if the document or writing is made in the name of an existing person, either by that person himself or by his authority, with the fraudulent intention that it should pass as being made by some person, real or fictitious, other than the person who makes it or authorises it to be made.
A seal or mark is said to be counterfeit if it is made without lawful authority, and is in such form as to resemble a genuine seal or mark, or, in the case of a seal, in such a form as to be capable of producing impressions resembling those produced by a genuine seal.
A representation of the impression of a seal is said to be counterfeit if it is not in fact made by the seal.
The term "resemble", applied to anything, includes the case where the thing is made to resemble, or is apparently intended to resemble, the object spoken of.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin make document or writing be false, and wetin make seal or mark be counterfeit. Document or writing dey false if register or record wey lawful authority dey keep, or document wey dey claim say authority issue am, get any important thing wey no true; if di whole or important part dey claim say person wey no make am or no authorise am make am, or na by cheating dem put wrong date or place when time or place matter; if e dey claim say person wey no really exist make am; or if person make am for name of person wey exist, by di person or im authority, wey wan make am pass as another person, real or no real. Seal or mark dey counterfeit if dem make am without lawful authority and e resemble genuine one, or fit make impression wey resemble genuine seal. Representation of seal impression dey counterfeit if di seal no really make am. 'Resemble' include when dem make something to resemble or e look like say dem wan make am resemble di object.

sections.title: Definition of forgery
sections.chapter: Chapter 43: Forgery in general: definitions
sections.text:
A person who makes a false document or writing knowing it to be false, and with intent that it may in any way be used or acted upon as genuine, whether in the State or elsewhere, to the prejudice of any person, or with intent that any person may, in the belief that it is genuine, be induced to do or refrain from doing any act, whether in the State or elsewhere, is said to forge the document or writing.
A person who makes a counterfeit seal or mark, or makes an impression of a counterfeit seal knowing the seal to be counterfeit, or makes a counterfeit representation of the impression of a genuine seal, or makes without lawful authority an impression of a genuine seal, with intent in either case that the thing so made may in any way be used or acted upon as genuine, whether in the State or elsewhere, to the prejudice of any person, or with intent that any person may, in the belief that it is genuine, be induced to do or refrain from doing any act, whether in the State or elsewhere, is said to forge the seal or mark.
The term "make a false document or writing" includes altering a genuine document or writing in any material part, either by erasure, obliteration, removal, or otherwise; and making any material addition to the body of a genuine document or writing; and adding to a genuine document or writing any false date, attestation, seal or other material matter.
It is immaterial in what language a forged document or writing is expressed.
It is immaterial that the forger of anything forged may not have intended that any particular person should use or act upon it, or that any particular person should be prejudiced by it, or be induced to do or refrain from doing any act.
It is immaterial that the thing forged is incomplete or does not purport to be a document, writing, or seal, which would be binding in law for any particular purpose, if it is so made, and is of such a kind, as to indicate that it was intended to be used or acted upon.
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain wetin forgery mean. Person don forge document or writing if e make false document or writing as e sabi say e dey false, wey wan make person use am or act on am as genuine, for State or anywhere, to hurt person, or so dat person go do or no do something because e believe say e genuine. Person don forge seal or mark if e make counterfeit seal or mark, make impression of counterfeit seal as e sabi, make counterfeit of genuine seal impression, or make impression of genuine seal without lawful authority, wey wan make dem use am as genuine. 'Make false document' include changing genuine document by erasing, removing or other way, adding important thing to am, or adding false date, attestation, seal or other important thing. E no matter di language. E no matter if e no wan make any particular person use am or get hurt. E no matter if di forged thing no complete or no get force of law, as long as e show say dem wan use am.

sections.title: Certain matters immaterial
sections.chapter: Chapter 43: Forgery in general: definitions
sections.text: In the case of an offence which involves the forging or uttering of a document or writing relating to the payment of money, or to the delivery or transfer of any property, or to the creation or performance of any obligation, it is immaterial in what country the money or property is, or purports to be, payable, deliverable, or transferable, or the obligation is or purports to be, an obligation to be performed; and, if the money or the property purports to be payable, deliverable or transferable or the obligation purports to be an obligation to be performed in some country out of Nigeria, it is immaterial whether the document or writing is under seal or not.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wetin no matter for forgery or uttering offences. If di document or writing na about payment of money, delivery or transfer of property, or creation or performance of obligation, e no matter which country di money or property dey, or wey dem go pay, deliver or transfer am, or where di obligation go happen. If e say dem go pay, deliver, transfer or perform am for country outside Nigeria, e no matter whether di document get seal or no get.

sections.title: Punishment of forgery in general
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.pidgin: Dis section tell di punishment for forgery. Person wey forge document, writing or seal don commit felony (serious crime) unless di law talk another thing, and e go face prison for 3 years if di law no give another punishment. For special cases, di punishment dey higher. Prison for life na for forging di public seal of Nigeria or any State, great or privy seal of Commonwealth country, seal of di President or Governor, or document wey get any of dem. Prison for 14 years na for forging securities, public debt papers, share transfers, land title papers, wills, probate, bank notes, bills, deeds, receipts, bills of lading, insurance policies, powers of attorney, witness signatures, and registers of births, marriages and deaths; also signature of di President, Governor, Minister or commissioner, public revenue stamps and public money papers. Prison for 7 years na for forging court seals, court papers, evidence, marriage papers, post stamps, contracts, receipts and quality marks. Forging telegram message get di same punishment as forging document wey get di same content. Check di full law text for all di details.

sections.title: Uttering false documents and counterfeit seals
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who knowingly and fraudulently utters a false document or writing, or a counterfeit seal, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he had forged the thing in question.
It is immaterial whether the false document or writing, or counterfeit seal, was made in Nigeria or elsewhere.
The term "fraudulently" means an intention that the thing in question shall be used or acted upon as genuine, whether in Nigeria or elsewhere, to the prejudice of some person, whether a particular person or not, or that some person whether a particular person, or not, shall, in the belief that the thing in question is genuine, be induced to do or refrain from doing some act, whether in Nigeria or elsewhere.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about using false documents and counterfeit seals. If person, as e sabi and by cheating, utter false document or writing, or counterfeit seal, e don commit di same kind of crime and e go face di same punishment as if e forge am. E no matter if dem make am for Nigeria or another place. 'By cheating' mean say person wan make dem use am or act on am as genuine, for Nigeria or anywhere, to hurt person, whether na particular person or not, or so dat person go do or no do something because e believe say e genuine.

sections.title: Uttering cancelled or exhausted documents
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who knowingly utters as and for a subsisting and effectual document any document which has by any lawful authority been ordered to be revoked, cancelled, or suspended, or the operation of which has ceased by effluxion of time, or by death, or by the happening of any other event, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he had forged the document.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about using document wey don finish. If person, as e sabi, utter as valid document any document wey lawful authority don order make dem revoke, cancel or suspend, or wey don stop to work because time don pass, death or any other event, e don commit di same kind of crime and e go face di same punishment as if e forge di document.

sections.title: Uttering cancelled stamps
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who knowingly utters as and for a valid and uncancelled stamp a stamp, or an impression of a seal, used for any purpose connected with the public revenue of Nigeria or of any part of a Commonwealth country or any country under the protection of a Commonwealth country which has been already used or which has been cancelled, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he had forged the stamp or seal. [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about using stamps wey don use or cancel. If person, as e sabi, utter as valid and uncancelled stamp, or impression of seal, wey dem use for public revenue of Nigeria or any part of Commonwealth country or country wey Commonwealth country dey protect, and dem don already use am or cancel am, e don commit di same kind of crime and e go face di same punishment as if e forge di stamp or seal.

sections.title: Procuring execution of documents by false pretences
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who, by means of any false and fraudulent representation as to the nature, contents, or operation, of a document, procures another to sign or execute the document, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he had forged the document.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about making person sign document by lying. If person use false and cheating statement about di nature, content or operation of document to make another person sign or execute am, e don commit di same kind of crime and e go face di same punishment as if e forge di document.

sections.title: Obliterating crossings on cheques
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud-
(1) obliterates, adds to or alters the crossing on a cheque; or
(2) knowingly alters a crossed cheque, the crossing on which has been obliterated, added to, or altered, is guilty of a felony, and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about changing crossing on cheques. If person, wey wan cheat, rub out, add to or change di crossing on cheque, or as e sabi change crossed cheque wey dem don rub out, add to or change di crossing, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Making documents without authority
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud-
(1) without lawful authority or excuse, makes, signs, or executes, for or in the name or on account of another person, whether by procuration or otherwise, any document or writing; or
(2) knowingly utters any document or writing so made, signed, or executed, by another person, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about making documents without authority. If person, wey wan cheat, make, sign or execute any document or writing for another person name or on im account without lawful authority or excuse, or as e sabi utter any document or writing wey another person make, sign or execute like dat, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Demanding property upon forged testamentary instruments
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who procures the delivery or payment to himself or any other person of any property or money by virtue of any probate or letters of administration granted upon a forged testamentary instrument, knowing the testamentary instrument to have been forged, or upon or by virtue of any probate or letters of administration obtained by false evidence, knowing the grant to have been so obtained, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he had forged the document or thing by virtue whereof he procures the delivery or payment.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about collecting property with forged wills. If person make delivery or payment of property or money reach imself or another person through probate or letters of administration wey dem grant on forged will as e sabi say dem forge am, or through one wey dem get by false evidence as e sabi, e don commit di same kind of crime and e go face di same punishment as if e forge di document or thing wey e use collect di delivery or payment.

sections.title: Purchasing forged bank notes
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, purchases or receives from any person, or has in his possession, a forged bank note, whether filled up or in blank, knowing it to be forged, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about forged bank notes. If person, without lawful authority or excuse, buy or receive forged bank note from person, or get am for im possession, as e sabi say e dey forged, whether e dey filled or blank, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di person go get di work to prove say e get lawful authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Falsifying warrants for money payable under public authority
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who, being employed in the public service, knowingly and with intent to defraud makes out or delivers to any person a warrant for the payment of any money payable by public authority for a greater or less amount than that to which the person on whose behalf the warrant is made out is entitled, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false warrants for public money. If person wey dey work for public service, as e sabi and by cheating, make out or give person warrant for payment of public money for amount wey pass or no reach wetin di person dey entitled to, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Falsification of register
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who, having the actual custody of any register or record kept by lawful authority, knowingly permits any entry which, in any material particular, is to his knowledge false, to be made in the register or record, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about falsifying register. If person wey dey keep register or record wey lawful authority dey keep, as e sabi allow person to enter anything wey e know say no true for any important part, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Sending false certificate of marriage to registrar
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text: Any person who signs or transmits to a person authorised by law to register marriages, a certificate of marriage, or any document purporting to be a certificate of marriage, which in any material particular is to his knowledge false, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false marriage certificate. If person sign or send to person wey di law authorise to register marriages, marriage certificate or document wey dey claim say e na marriage certificate, wey e know say e dey false for any important part, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: False statements for the purpose of registers of births, deaths, and marriages
sections.chapter: Chapter 44: Punishment of forgery and like offences
sections.text:
Any person who knowingly and with intent to procure the same to be inserted in a register of births, deaths, or marriages, makes any false statements touching any matter required by law to be registered in any such register, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false statements for registers of births, deaths and marriages. If person, as e sabi, make false statement about any matter wey di law require make dem register for dat kind register, so dat dem go enter am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Instruments and materials for forgery
sections.chapter: Chapter 45: Preparation for forgery
sections.text:
Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
(1) makes, or begins or prepares to make, or uses, or knowingly has in his possession or disposes of, any paper resembling any paper such as is specially provided by the proper authority for the purpose of being used for making any of the following things-
(a) any document acknowledging or being evidence of the indebtedness of the Government of Nigeria or of any part of Nigeria or of the government of any Commonwealth country or any country under the protection of a Commonwealth country, or of any foreign prince or State, or of any person carrying on the business of banking, to any person; or
(b) any stamp, licence, permit, or other document, used for the purposes of the public revenue of Nigeria or of any part of Nigeria or of any part of a Commonwealth country or any country under the protection of a Commonwealth country; or
(c) any bank note, or any machinery or instrument or material for making such paper, or capable of producing in or on paper any words, figures, letters, marks, or lines, resembling any words, figures, letters, marks or lines used in or on paper specially provided for any such purpose; or
(2) impresses or makes upon any plate or material any words, figures, letters, marks, or lines, the print whereof resembles, in whole or part, the words, figures, letters, marks, or lines used in any such document as aforesaid; or
(3) uses or knowingly has in his possession or disposes of, any plate or material upon which any such words, figures, letters, marks or lines, are impressed or made; or
(4) uses, or knowingly has in his possession or disposes of, any paper on which is written or printed the whole or any part of the usual contents of any such documents as aforesaid, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years, and any such paper, document, bank note, or any machinery or instrument or material for making or capable of producing such paper, document or bank note which are found in his possession shall be forfeited to the State by order of the court before which he is tried or if there is no trial, by order of the court before which the offence is inquired into.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about tools and materials for forgery. If person, without lawful authority or excuse, make, begin or prepare to make, use, or as e sabi get or give out paper wey resemble paper wey authority provide to make government debt documents, public revenue stamps, licences, permits, bank notes, or machine or material wey fit make dat kind paper; or print words, figures or marks wey resemble dem on plate or material; or use, get or give out dat plate or material; or use, get or give out paper wey get di whole or part of di usual content of dem, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di person go get di work to prove say e get lawful authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 14 years. Di court go forfeit to di State any paper, document, bank note, machine, tool or material wey dem find with am.

sections.title: Unlawful inquires relating to the possibility of forgery
sections.chapter: Chapter 45: Preparation for forgery
sections.text:
(1) Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, either orally or in writing makes inquiries of any other person, whether in Nigeria or at any place not in Nigeria-
(a) as to the cost of obtaining or the cost of supplying or as to obtaining or supplying any machinery or instrument or material for the making of any paper or capable of producing in or on any paper any words, figures, letters, marks or lines resembling any words, figures, letters, marks or lines used in or on paper specially provided for any purpose mentioned in paragraph
(1) of section 480 of this Code; or
(b) as to the cost of printing or otherwise reproducing or as to printing or otherwise reproducing any document referred to in subsection (1) of section 480 of this Code; no matter by what name such document may be referred to; or
(c) as to whether such other person or any other person is prepared to print or otherwise reproduce or would be prepared to print or otherwise reproduce any such document as aforesaid; or
(d) as to whether such other person or any other person is prepared to obtain or would be prepared to obtain any such document as aforesaid by any means other than paying full value for the same, is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment for one year.
(2) In the case of written inquiries in connection with any of the matters or subjects to which subsection
(1) of this section relates, the fact that such inquiries were reduced into writing shall be sufficient proof of an attempt to commit the offence and the offender shall be subject to a like penalty as if he had committed the offence.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about asking questions wey show say person dey think of forgery. If person, without lawful authority or excuse, ask another person by mouth or writing, for Nigeria or outside, about di cost or how to get or supply machine or material wey fit make forgery paper; about di cost or how to print or reproduce di documents wey section 480 of dis Code talk about; whether person dey ready to print or reproduce dem; or whether person dey ready to get dem without paying di full value, e don commit crime. Di person go get di work to prove say e get lawful authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 1 year. If person write di questions down, dat one na enough proof say e try to commit di offence, and e go face di same punishment as if e commit am.

sections.title: Counterfeit stamps
sections.chapter: Chapter 45: Preparation for forgery
sections.text:
Any person who, without authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him [L.N. 112 of 1964 ]
(1) makes or mends, or begins or prepares to make or mend, or uses, or knowingly has in his possession or disposes of, any die, plate, or instrument, capable of making an impression resembling that made by any die, plate or instrument used for the purpose of making any stamp, whether impressed or adhesive, which is used for the purposes of the public revenue of the Nigerian Postal Service in Nigeria or in any other country, or capable of producing in or on paper any words, figures, letters, marks, or lines, resembling any words, figures, letters, marks, or lines used in or on any paper specially provided by the proper authority for any such purpose; or
(2) knowingly has in his possession or disposes of any paper or other material which has on it the impression of any such die, plate, or instrument, or any paper which has on it any such words, figures, letters, marks, or lines, as aforesaid; or
(3) fraudulently, and with intent that use may be made of any such stamp as aforesaid, or of any part of it, removes the stamp from any material in any way whatever; or
(4) fraudulently, and with intent that use may be made of any part of such stamp, mutilates the stamp; or
(5) fraudulently fixes or places upon any material or upon any such stamp, any stamp or part of a stamp which has been in any way removed from any other material, or out of or from any other stamp; or
(6) fraudulently, and with intent that use may be made of any such stamp which has been already impressed upon or attached to any material, erases or otherwise removes, either really or apparently, from such material anything whatever written on it; or
(7) knowingly has in his possession or disposes of anything obtained or prepared by any such unlawful act as aforesaid, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about counterfeit stamps. If person, without authority or excuse, make or mend, begin or prepare to make or mend, use, or as e sabi get or give out die, plate or tool wey fit make impression like di one wey dem use make stamps for public revenue or Nigerian Postal Service stamps for Nigeria or any country; or as e sabi get paper or material wey get dat kind impression or words; or by cheating remove, cut, join, put or erase thing for stamp so dat dem go use am; or as e sabi get or give out anything wey dem get by dem kind act, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di person go get di work to prove say e get authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Paper for postal purposes
sections.chapter: Chapter 45: Preparation for forgery
sections.text: Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, knowingly has in his possession or disposes of any paper which has been specially provided by the proper authority for the purpose of being used for postage stamps, money orders, or postal orders, before such paper has been lawfully issued for public use, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about paper for postal use. If person, without lawful authority or excuse, as e sabi get or give out paper wey authority provide for postage stamps, money orders or postal orders, before dem lawfully issue am for public use, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di person go get di work to prove say e get lawful authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Paper and dies for postage stamps
sections.chapter: Chapter 45: Preparation for forgery
sections.text:
Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him-
(1) makes, or begins or prepares to make, or uses for any postal purpose, or has in his possession, or disposes of any imitation or representation on paper or any other material, of any stamp used for denoting any rate of postage of Nigeria, or of any other country; or
(2) makes or mends, or begins or prepares to make or mend, or uses, or has in his possession or disposes of, any die, plate, instrument, or material, for making any such imitation or representation, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year or to a fine of one hundred naira and any stamps, and any other such things as aforesaid, which are found in his possession, are forfeited to the State.
For the purposes of this section of this Code, a stamp purporting to denote a rate of postage of any country is to be taken to be a stamp used for postal purposes in that country, until the contrary is shown.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about paper and dies for postage stamps. If person, without lawful authority or excuse, make, begin or prepare to make, use for postal purpose, get or give out imitation of any postage stamp of Nigeria or any country; or make or mend, begin or prepare to make or mend, use, get or give out die, plate, tool or material to make dat imitation, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di person go get di work to prove say e get lawful authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 1 year or fine (money wey person go pay) of one hundred naira. Di State go take any stamps and other dem things wey dem find with am. Stamp wey claim say na postage rate of any country go count as postal stamp for dat country until person show say no be so.

sections.title: Impersonation in general
sections.chapter: Chapter 46: Impersonation
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud any person, falsely represents himself to be some other person, living or dead, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
If the representation is that the offender is a person entitled by will or operation of law to any specific property and he commits the offence to obtain such property or possession thereof, he is liable to imprisonment for fourteen years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about pretending to be another person. If person, wey wan cheat person, falsely say e be another person, alive or dead, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. If e claim say e be person wey will or operation of law give right to special property and e do am to get dat property or possession of am, e go face prison for 14 years.

sections.title: Falsely acknowledging deeds, recognisances, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 46: Impersonation
sections.text: Any person who, without lawful authority or excuse, the proof of which lies on him, makes, in the name of any other person, before any court or person lawfully authorised to take such an acknowledgment, an acknowledgment of liability of any kind, or an acknowledgment of deed or other instrument, is guilty of a felony and liable to imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about false acknowledgement for another person name. If person, without lawful authority or excuse, make acknowledgement of liability or of deed or other instrument for another person name before court or person wey di law authorise to take am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di person go get di work to prove say e get lawful authority or excuse. Di punishment na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Impersonation of a person named in a certificate
sections.chapter: Chapter 46: Impersonation
sections.text: Any person who alters any document which has been issued by lawful authority to another person, and whereby that other person is certified to be a person possessed of any qualification recognised by law for any purpose, or to be the holder of any office, or to be entitled to exercise any profession, trade, or business, or to be entitled to any right or privilege, or to enjoy any rank or status, and falsely represents himself to be the person named in the document, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he had forged the document.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about using another person certificate to pretend. If person change document wey lawful authority issue to another person to certify say di person get qualification, office, right to do profession, trade or business, right or privilege, rank or status, and e falsely say na im be di person wey dem name for di document, e don commit di same kind of crime and e go face di same punishment as if e forge di document.

sections.title: Lending, etc., certificate for impersonation
sections.chapter: Chapter 46: Impersonation
sections.text:
Any person who, being a person to whom any document has been issued by lawful authority whereby he is certified to be a person possessed of any qualification recognised by law for any purpose, or to be the holder of any office, or to be entitled to exercise any profession, trade, or business, or to be entitled to any right or privilege, or to enjoy any rank or status, sells, gives or lends the document to another person with intent that that other person may represent himself to be the person named therein, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about lending certificate so person fit pretend. If person wey lawful authority issue document to, certifying say e get qualification, office, right to do profession, trade or business, right or privilege, rank or status, sell, give or lend di document to another person so dat di person go say na im be di person wey dem name inside, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Impersonation of person named in a testimonial or character
sections.chapter: Chapter 46: Impersonation
sections.text: Any person who, with the purpose of obtaining any employment, alters any document of the nature of a testimonial or character given to another person, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about changing testimonial or character letter. If person change document wey be testimonial or character wey dem give another person, so dat e go get employment, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Lending, etc., testimonial for impersonation
sections.chapter: Chapter 46: Impersonation
sections.text: Any person who, being a person to whom any such document as is mentioned in section 488 of this Code has been given, gives, sells or lends such document to another person with the intent that that other person may alter such document for the purpose of obtaining any employment, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about lending testimonial so person fit change am. If person wey dem give di kind document wey section 488 of dis Code talk about, give, sell or lend am to another person so dat di person go change am to get employment, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Fraudulent dealing with property by debtors
sections.chapter: Chapter 47: Fraudulent debtors
sections.text:
Any person who, with intent to defraud his creditors or any of them-
(1) makes any gift, delivery, or transfer of his property, or any charge on his property; or
(2) conceals or removes any part of his property after or within two months before the date of any unsatisfied judgment or order for payment of money obtained against him, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for one year.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about debtors wey cheat dem creditors. If person, wey wan cheat im creditors or any of dem, make any gift, delivery, transfer or charge on im property; or hide or remove any part of im property after, or within 2 months before, date of any judgment or order wey no dem don satisfy for payment of money wey dem obtain against am, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 1 year.

sections.title: Making or dealing in infringing copies of copyright work
sections.chapter: Chapter 48: Offences in relation to copyright
sections.text:
Any person who knowingly-
(a) makes for sale or hire any infringing copy of a work in which copyright subsists; or
(b) sells or lets for hire, or by way of trade exposes or offers for sale or hire any infringing copy of any such work; or
(c) distributes infringing copies of any such work either for the purposes of trade or to such an extent as to affect prejudicially the owner of the copyright; or
(d) by way of trade exhibits in public any infringing copy of any such work, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding four naira for every copy dealt with in contravention of this section of this Code, but not exceeding one hundred naira in respect of the same transaction; or, on the case of a second or subsequent offence, either to such fine or to imprisonment for two months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about copying and selling copyright work wey dem copy without permission. If person, as e sabi, make infringing copy of work wey get copyright for sale or hire; sell, hire, or by way of trade show or offer am for sale or hire; share am for trade or reach di level wey e hurt di copyright owner; or by way of trade show am for public, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) wey no pass four naira for every copy, but e no go pass one hundred naira for di same transaction. For second or later offence, na either dat fine or prison for 2 months.

sections.title: Being in possession of plate for making infringing copies: giving unathorised performances of copyright work
sections.chapter: Chapter 48: Offences in relation to copyright
sections.text: Any person who knowingly makes or has in his possession any plate for the purposes of making infringing copies of any work in which copyright subsists, or knowingly and for his private profit causes any such work to be performed in public without the consent of the owner of the copyright, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of one hundred naira, or, in the case of a second or subsequent offence, either to such fine or to imprisonment for two months.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about plates for making infringing copies and unauthorised performances. If person, as e sabi, make or get plate to make infringing copies of work wey get copyright, or as e sabi and for im private profit make dem perform dat work for public without di copyright owner agreement, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of one hundred naira. For second or later offence, na either dat fine or prison for 2 months.

sections.title: Forfeiture of copies or plates
sections.chapter: Chapter 48: Offences in relation to copyright
sections.text: The court before which any proceedings are taken for any offence under sections 491 and 492 of this Code may, whether the alleged offender is convicted or not, order all copies of the work or all plates in the possession of the alleged offender, which appear to it to be infringing copies or plates for the purpose of making infringing copies, to be destroyed or delivered up to the owner of the copyright or otherwise dealt with as the court may think fit.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about wetin court fit do with copies or plates. For any case wey dem take under sections 491 and 492 of dis Code, di court fit order, whether di person dey found guilty or not, say make dem destroy all copies of di work or plates wey dey di accused possession wey look like infringing copies or plates to make infringing copies, or give dem to di copyright owner, or deal with dem any other way wey di court think say e good.

sections.title: Corrupt acceptance of gift
sections.chapter: Chapter 49: Secret commissions and corrupt practices
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) being an agent, corruptly accepts or obtains or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gift or consideration as an inducement or reward for doing or for forbearing to do or for having after the commencement of this Code done or forborne to do, any act in relation to his principal's affairs or business, or for showing or forbearing to show favour or do favour to any person in relation to his principal's affairs or business; or Corrupt gift to agent
(b) corruptly gives or agrees to give or offers any gift or consideration to any agent as an inducement or reward for doing or forbearing to do, or for having after the commencement of this Code done or forborne to do, any act in relation to his principal's affairs or business, or for showing or forbearing to show favour or disfavour to any person in relation to his principal's affairs or business; or Gift to agent of receipt, etc., with intent to mislead principal
(c) knowingly gives to any agent, or, being an agent, knowingly uses with intent to deceive his principal, any receipt, account or other document in respect of which the principal is interested and which contains any statement which is false or erroneous or defective in any material particulars, and which, to his knowledge, is intended to mislead his principal, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years or to a fine of one thousand naira or to both such imprisonment and fine.
(2) For the purposes of this section, the expression "consideration" includes valuable consideration of any kind; the expression "agent" includes any person employed by or acting for another; and the expression "principal" includes an employer.
(3) A person serving under the State or, in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, the government of the State, as the case may be, or any local government council, is an agent within the meaning of this section.
(4) A prosecution for an offence under this section of this Code shall not be instituted except by or with the consent of a law officer.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about corrupt gifts to agents. E don commit misdemeanour (small crime) if agent corruptly accept, collect, agree to accept or try to collect gift or consideration as reward for doing or no doing act, or for showing or no showing favour, about im principal business; if person corruptly give, agree to give or offer dat kind gift to agent; or if person, as e sabi, give agent, or agent use to deceive im principal, receipt, account or document wey get false or wrong important statement wey e sabi say e wan mislead di principal. Di punishment na prison for 2 years or fine (money wey person go pay) of one thousand naira or both. 'Consideration' include any valuable thing, 'agent' include anybody wey another person employ or wey dey act for am, and 'principal' include employer. Person wey dey serve di State, di government of di State, Abuja for FCT, or any local government council na agent. Dem fit start case only by or with consent of law officer.

sections.title: Offences of cruelty
sections.chapter: Chapter 50: Cruelty to animals
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) cruelly beats, kicks, ill-treats, over-rides, over -dri ves, over-loads, tortures, infuriates, or terrifies any animal, or causes or procures, or being the owner, permits any animal to be so used; or
(b) by wantonly or unreasonably doing or omitting to do any act, or causing or procuring the commission or omission of any act, causes any unnecessary suffering, or being the owner, permits any unnecessary suffering to be caused to any animal; or
(c) conveys or carries, or being the owner, permits to be conveyed or carried any animal in such manner or position as to cause such animal unnecessary suffering; or
(d) wilfully without any reasonable cause or excuse administers, or causes or procures, or, being the owner, permits such administration of, any poisonous or injurious drug or substances to any animal, or wilfully without any reasonable cause or excuse causes any such substance to be taken by any animal; or
(e) subjects, or causes or procures, or, being the owner, permits, to be subjected, any animal to any operation which is performed without due care and humanity; or
(f) causes, or procures, or assists at the fighting or baiting of any animal, or keeps, uses, manages, or acts or assists in the management of any premises or place for the purpose, or partly for the purpose, of fighting or baiting any animal, or permits any place to be so kept, managed or used, or receives or causes or procures any person to receive money for the admission of any person to such premises or place, is guilty of an offence of cruelty and is liable to imprisonment for six months or to a fine of fifty naira or to both such imprisonment and fine.
(2) For the purposes of this section, an owner shall be deemed to have committed cruelty within the meaning of this Chapter if he shall have failed to exercise reasonable care and supervision in respect of the protection of the animal therefrom:
Provided that, when an owner is convicted of permitting cruelty within the meaning of this Chapter by reason only of his having failed to exercise such care and supervision, he is not liable to imprisonment without the option of a fine.
(3) Nothing in this Chapter shall apply-
(a) to the commission or omission of any act in the course of the destruction, or the preparation for destruction, of any animal as food for mankind, unless such destruction or such preparation was accompanied by the infliction of unnecessary suffering; or
(b) to the coursing or hunting of any captive animal, unless such animal is liberated in an injured, mutilated or exhausted condition; but a captive animal shall not, for the purpose of this section, be deemed to be coursed or hunted before it is liberated for the purpose of being coursed or hunted, or after it has been recaptured, or if it is under control.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about cruelty to animals. Person don commit offence of cruelty if e cruelly beat, kick, ill-treat, over-ride, over-drive, over-load, torture, infuriate or terrify animal, or cause am or, as owner, allow am; wantonly or unreasonably cause or allow unnecessary suffering; carry animal for way wey cause am unnecessary suffering; on purpose give animal poisonous or injurious drug without reasonable cause; do operation without due care and humanity; or dey involve for animal fighting or baiting or keep place for am or collect money for people to enter. Di punishment na prison for 6 months or fine (money wey person go pay) of fifty naira or both. Owner don commit cruelty if e fail to take reasonable care and supervision, but if na only dat one, e no go face prison without option of fine. Dis Chapter no cover act wey dem do as dem dey kill or prepare animal as food, unless dem cause unnecessary suffering, or coursing or hunting captive animal, unless dem release am injured, maimed or tired.

sections.title: Court may order destruction of animal
sections.chapter: Chapter 50: Cruelty to animals
sections.text: When the owner of any animal is convicted of an offence of cruelty under section 495 of this Code, it shall be lawful for the court, if the court is satisfied that it would be cruel to keep the animal alive, to direct that the animal be destroyed, and to assign the animal to a suitable person for that purpose. Any reasonable expenses incurred in destroying the animal may be ordered by the court to be paid by the owner, and thereupon shall be recoverable in like manner as a fine.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about court power to destroy animal. If owner of animal dey found guilty of cruelty under section 495 of dis Code, and di court satisfy say e go be cruelty to keep di animal alive, di court fit order say make dem destroy di animal and give am to suitable person to do am. Di court fit order di owner to pay reasonable expenses wey dem use destroy am, and dem go collect am like fine.

sections.title: Court may deprive person of ownership
sections.chapter: Chapter 50: Cruelty to animals
sections.text:
If the owner of any animal is guilty of cruelty within the meaning of this Chapter to any animal, the court upon his conviction thereof, may if it thinks fit, in addition to any other punishment, deprive such person of the ownership of the animal, and may make such order as to the disposal of the animal as it may think fit:
Provided that no order shall be made under this section of this Code, unless it is shown by evidence as to a previous conviction, or as to the character of the owner, or otherwise, that the animal, if left with the owner, is likely to be exposed to further cruelty.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about court power to take animal from owner. If owner of animal dey found guilty of cruelty to any animal, di court fit, if e think say e good, in addition to any other punishment, take di ownership of di animal from am and order how dem go deal with di animal. But di court go make dat order only if evidence of previous conviction, di owner character or other thing show say di animal go likely face more cruelty if e stay with di owner.

sections.title: Power of police to take charge of animal or vehicle
sections.chapter: Chapter 50: Cruelty to animals
sections.text: When a person in charge of an animal or vehicle is arrested it shall be lawful for any police officer to take charge of such animal or vehicle and to deposit the same in a place of safe custody until the termination of the proceedings or until the court shall direct such animal or vehicle to be delivered to the person charged or to the owner, and the reasonable costs of such detention, including the reasonable costs of any veterinary treatment shall, in the event of a conviction in respect of the animal, be paid by the owner, and such costs may be recovered in like manner as a fine.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about police power over animal or vehicle. When dem arrest person wey dey in charge of animal or vehicle, police officer fit take charge of am and put am for safe place till di case finish or till di court order say make dem give am to di person wey dem charge or to di owner. If di court find di owner guilty for di animal matter, di owner go pay di reasonable cost of keeping am, including reasonable cost of veterinary treatment, and dem go collect am like fine.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.chapter: Chapter 50: Cruelty to animals
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain di meaning of some words for dis Chapter. 'Animal' mean any domestic or captive animal. 'Captive animal' mean any animal wey no be domestic animal, of any kind, including bird, fish or reptile, wey dey captivity or confinement, or wey dem maim, pinion or put any tool on am to stop am from escaping. 'Domestic animal' mean any animal or bird wey dey tame, or wey dem don tame or dey tame enough to serve person for some purpose.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 51: Miscellaneous offences in relation to ships and wharves
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain di meaning of some words for dis Chapter. 'Crew' include masters, mates, pilots, engineers, stokers, deckhands and all person wey dey work for di navigation or service of di ship. 'Government' mean di government of di Federation and e include State government. 'Passenger steamer' mean every steamship wey carry one or more persons wey no be crew, di owner, im family, friends and servants. 'Ship' include every kind of vessel wey dey serve di Government and every passenger steamer wey dey do local navigation for inland and territorial waters of Nigeria.

sections.title: Offences in relation to ships
sections.chapter: Chapter 51: Miscellaneous offences in relation to ships and wharves
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about offences for ships. Person fit pay fine (money wey person go pay) of ten naira, and di fine no stop dem from collecting any fare wey e suppose pay, if on ship e do any of dis: drunk or disorderly and still try to enter after crew refuse am, or no comot when crew ask am; molest passenger after warning; obstruct, impede or molest crew for navigation or management of di ship; try to enter ship wey full after dem refuse am, or no comot when dem ask am before di ship leave; travel or try to travel without paying fare wey e wan avoid; pass di distance wey e pay for without paying more wey e wan avoid; refuse to comot where e pay reach; no pay fare or show ticket when crew ask; travel for better class wey no be im ticket; or stay for place wey no dey for public passengers and refuse to comot when crew order am. Crew member wey dey in charge and people wey e call fit arrest without court paper (warrant) person wey commit di offence and wey im name and address dem no sabi. If person wey commit di offence refuse to give im name and address when officer or quartermaster ask, or give false one, e go face fine of forty naira.

sections.title: Entering ship or wharf without ticket
sections.chapter: Chapter 51: Miscellaneous offences in relation to ships and wharves
sections.text:
(1) Any person who-
(a) not being a passenger by a ship or not having purchased a ticket to travel by a ship, enters upon any enclosed quay, wharf, or landing place, and on being ordered to leave such quay, wharf or landing place by any servant of the Nigerian Ports Authority or person in charge of such quay, wharf, or landing place or any police officer, refuses to do so; or
(b) not being a passenger by a ship or not having purchased a ticket to travel by a ship, attempts to enter upon any enclosed quay, wharf or landing place, and on being ordered to desist by any servant of the Nigerian Ports Authority or person in charge of such quay, wharf or landing place, or any police officer, persists in so doing, is guilty of a simple offence and is liable to a fine of four naira or in default to imprisonment for one month.
(2) Any duly authorised member of the crew or any police officer and all persons called by him to his assistance may, without warrant, arrest any person who commits any offence against this section of this Code and whose name and address are unknown to him.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about entering ship or wharf without ticket. If person wey no be passenger or no buy ticket enter enclosed quay, wharf or landing place, and refuse to comot when servant of Nigerian Ports Authority, person in charge or police officer order am, or try to enter and keep on doing am after dem order am to stop, e don commit simple offence (small crime). Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of four naira or, if e no pay, prison for 1 month. Duly authorised crew member or police officer and people wey e call fit arrest without court paper (warrant) person wey commit di offence and wey im name and address dem no sabi.

sections.title: Power to exclude drunken person from ship
sections.chapter: Chapter 51: Miscellaneous offences in relation to ships and wharves
sections.text: Any duly authorised member of the crew of any ship may refuse to receive on board thereof any person who by reason of drunkenness or otherwise is in such a state, or misconducts himself in such a manner, as to cause annoyance or injury to passengers on board, and if any such person is on board, may put him on shore at any convenient place.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about power to stop drunk person from entering ship. Duly authorised member of ship crew fit refuse to receive on board any person wey, because of drunkenness or any other reason, dey for state or misbehave so dat e go cause annoyance or injury to passengers. If dat kind person don dey on board, di crew member fit put am for land for any convenient place.

sections.title: Jurisdiction
sections.chapter: Chapter 51: Miscellaneous offences in relation to ships and wharves
sections.text: For the purpose of giving jurisdiction under this Chapter, every offence shall be deemed to have been committed and every cause of complaint to have arisen either in the district in which the same actually was committed or arose, or in any district in which the offender or person complained against is or may be found.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about where court get power for dis Chapter. Every offence and cause of complaint go count as dem commit am or e happen either for di district where e really happen, or for any district where dem fit find di offender or di person wey dem complain against.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.chapter: Chapter 52: Offences by members of a crew
sections.text:
In this Chapter, unless the context otherwise requires- [L.N. 112 of 1964.]
"Government" means the government of the Federation and includes a State government;
"ship" includes every description of vessel used in inland navigation or in the service of the Government, but does not include-
(a) ocean-going ships not in the service of the Government; or
sections.pidgin: Dis section explain di meaning of some words for dis Chapter. 'Government' mean di government of di Federation and e include State government. 'Ship' include every kind of vessel wey dem use for inland navigation or for service of di Government, but e no include ocean-going ships wey no dey for service of di Government.

sections.title: Obligation to complete voyage
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: (b)
sections.text:
A person serving in the crew of a ship shall complete any voyage the ship may be engaged in making when the period of his engagement expires:
Provided that the person serving after the term of his agreement has expired, shall be paid up to the date of the termination of the voyage, at the rate stipulated for under the terms of the agreement under which he is serving.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about di duty of crew to finish voyage. Person wey dey serve as crew of ship must finish any voyage wey di ship dey do when im agreement time end. But dem go pay person wey still dey serve after im agreement time don end up to di date di voyage end, for di rate wey im agreement talk.

sections.title: Offences by members of a crew
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: (b)
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about offences by members of ship crew. E don commit simple offence (small crime) if person agree to serve for ship crew and no start work; or if crew member desert or stay away from duty without leave or lawful cause, drink till e drunk for working hours, refuse without reasonable excuse to obey order of person wey get authority over am, use abusive or insulting words for person wey get authority over am, on purpose do act wey fit cause loss of or damage or serious risk to im employer property, or refuse without reasonable cause to do act wey e suppose do to protect im employer property. Di punishment na fine (money wey person go pay) of ten naira. Crew member wey join other crew to disobey lawful commands, neglect duty, or block di navigation of di ship or progress of di voyage go face prison for 3 months. Dem fit try di offender for any place where e dey or where dem bring am. Master or person in charge of ocean-going ship fit look into any offence under dis section and give di offender fine wey no pass ten naira, wey dem go collect by stopping am from im wages.

sections.title: Attempts to commit offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text: Any person who attempts to commit a felony or misdemeanor, is guilty of an offence which, unless otherwise stated, is a misdemeanor.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to commit offences. If person try to commit felony or misdemeanour, e don commit offence wey, unless di law talk another thing, na misdemeanour (small crime).

sections.title: Punishment of attempts to commit felonies
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text:
Any person who attempts to commit a felony of such a kind that a person convicted of it is liable to the punishment of death or of imprisonment for a term of fourteen years or upwards, with or without other punishment, is guilty of a felony and is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to imprisonment for seven years.
Any person who attempts to commit a felony of any other kind is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to a punishment equal to one half of the greatest punishment to which an offender convicted of the felony which he attempted to commit is liable.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about di punishment for trying to commit felonies. If person try to commit felony wey di person wey commit am fit face death or prison for 14 years or more, with or without other punishment, e don commit felony (serious crime) and e go face prison for 7 years if di law no give another punishment. If person try to commit any other kind of felony, e go face if di law no give another punishment, half of di greatest punishment wey person wey commit di felony wey e try fit face.

sections.title: Punishment of attempts to commit misdemeanours
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text: Any person who attempts to commit a misdemeanor is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to a punishment equal to one half of the greatest punishment to which an offender convicted of the offence which he attempted to commit is liable.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about di punishment for trying to commit misdemeanours. If person try to commit misdemeanour, e go face, if di law no give another punishment, half of di greatest punishment wey person wey commit di offence wey e try fit face.

sections.title: Punishment of attempts to commit simple offences
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text: Any person who attempts to commit a simple offence is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to one half of the greatest punishment to which an offender convicted of the offence which he attempted to commit is liable.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about di punishment for trying to commit simple offences. If person try to commit simple offence (small crime), e go face, if di law no give another punishment, half of di greatest punishment wey person wey commit di offence wey e try fit face.

sections.title: Reduction of punishment
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text: When a person is convicted of attempting to commit an offence, if it is proved that he desisted of his own motion from the further prosecution of his intention, without its fulfilment being prevented by circumstances independent of will, he is liable to one half only of the punishment of which he would otherwise be liable. If that punishment is imprisonment for life, the greatest punishment to which he is liable is imprisonment for seven years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about reducing punishment for attempts. If di court find person guilty of trying to commit offence, and dem prove say e stop by imself from continuing wetin e wan do, without anything outside im will stopping am, e go face only half of di punishment wey e for face. If dat punishment na prison for life, di greatest punishment wey e go face na prison for 7 years.

sections.title: Attempts to procure commission of criminal acts
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text:
(1) Any person who attempts to procure another to do an act or make an omission of such a nature that if he himself were to do the act or make the omission he would be guilty of an offence, is himself to be deemed guilty of attempting to commit such offence and to be punishable accordingly.
(2) Any person who while in Nigeria attempts to procure another to do an act or make an omission at a place not in Nigeria of such a nature-
(a) that if he were himself to do the act or make the omission in Nigeria he would be guilty of an offence; and
(b) that if he were himself to do the act or make the omission at the place where the act or omission is proposed to be done or made, he would himself be guilty of an offence under the laws in force at that place, is guilty of an offence of the same kind and is liable to the same punishment as if he were himself to attempt to do the same act or make the same omission in Nigeria.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about trying to make another person commit criminal act. If person try to make another person do act or omit to do act wey go be offence if e do am imself, dem go count am as guilty of trying to commit dat offence and e go get di same punishment. If person for Nigeria try to make another person do act or omission for place outside Nigeria wey go be offence if e do am for Nigeria, and also offence under di law for dat place, e don commit di same kind of offence and e go face di same punishment as if e try to do di same act or omission for Nigeria.

sections.title: Preparation to commit crimes with explosives, etc
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text: Any person who makes or knowingly has in his possession any explosive substance, or any dangerous or noxious engine, instrument, or thing whatever, with intent by means thereof to commit, or for the purpose of enabling any other person by means thereof to commit any felony, is guilty of a felony and is liable to imprisonment for three years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about preparing to commit crime with explosives. If person make or as e sabi get explosive substance, or any dangerous or harmful engine, instrument or thing, wey wan use am to commit felony, or to help another person use am to commit felony, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 3 years.

sections.title: Neglect to prevent felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 53: Attempts, incitements, and preparations to commit offences
sections.text: Every person who, knowing that a person designs to commit or is committing a felony, fails to use all reasonable means to prevent the commission or completion thereof, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about failing to stop felony. If person sabi say another person wan commit or dey commit felony and e no use all reasonable means to stop am from happen or finish, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years.

sections.title: Conspiracy to commit felony
sections.chapter: Chapter 54: Conspiracy
sections.text: Any person who conspires with another to commit any felony, or to do any act in any part of the world which if done in Nigeria would be a felony, and which is an offence under the laws in force in the place where it is proposed to be done, is guilty of a felony and is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to imprisonment for seven years, or, if the greatest punishment to which a person convicted of the felony in question is liable is less than imprisonment for seven years, then to such lesser punishment.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about plan together to commit felony. If person plan together with another person to commit felony, or to do any act for any part of di world wey go be felony if dem do am for Nigeria and wey also be offence under di law of di place where dem wan do am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years if di law no give another punishment. If di greatest punishment for di felony na less than prison for 7 years, e go face dat lesser punishment.

sections.title: Conspiracy to commit felony against law of a State
sections.chapter: Chapter 54: Conspiracy
sections.text:
(1) Any person who while in a State conspires with another to do any act not in the State which if done in the State would be a felony against the law of the State and which is an offence against the law of the place where it is proposed to be done, is guilty of a felony and is liable, if no other punishment is provided, to imprisonment for seven years, or, if the greatest punishment to which a person convicted of the felony in question is liable is less than imprisonment for seven years, then to such lesser punishment.
(2) In this section and section 517 A of this Code, "law of a State" has the meaning assigned to it in section l0A of this Code.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about plan together to commit felony against di law of a State. If person wey dey for State plan together with another person to do act wey no dey for di State, wey go be felony against di law of di State if dem do am for di State and wey also be offence against di law of di place where dem wan do am, e don commit felony (serious crime). Di punishment na prison for 7 years if di law no give another punishment. If di greatest punishment for di felony na less than prison for 7 years, e go face dat lesser punishment. 'Law of a State' get di meaning wey section 10A of dis Code give am for dis section and section 517A.

sections.title: Conspiracy to commit offence
sections.chapter: Chapter 54: Conspiracy
sections.text:
Any person who conspires with another to commit any offence which is not a felony, or to do any act in any part of the world, which if done in Nigeria would be an offence but not a felony, and which is an offence under the laws in force in the place where it is proposed to be done, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about plan together to commit offence wey no be felony. If person plan together with another person to commit offence wey no be felony, or to do any act for any part of di world wey go be offence but no be felony if dem do am for Nigeria, and wey also be offence under di law of di place where dem wan do am, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime). Di punishment na prison for 2 years. Police no fit arrest am without court paper (warrant).

sections.title: Conspiracy to commit offence against law of a State
sections.chapter: Chapter 54: Conspiracy
sections.text:
Any person who, while in a State, conspires with another to do any act not in the State which if done in the State would be an offence against the law of the State (other than a felony) and which is an offence against the law of the place where it is proposed to be done, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is liable to imprisonment for two years.
The offender cannot be arrested without warrant.
sections.pidgin: Dis section talk about plan together to commit offence against di law of a State. If person wey dey for State plan together with another person to do act wey no dey for di State, wey go be offence against di law of di State (but no be felony) if dem do am for di State, and wey also be offence against di law of di place where dem wan do am, e don commit misdemeanour (small crime).
